183: | FEAT-BIL-02 | Usage statement | Explainable per-waybill ledger and adjustments |
184: | FEAT-ADM-01 | Reference/config management | Carriers, services, fees, statuses and calendars |
185: | FEAT-ADM-02 | Job/queue operations | Inspect, retry safely and dead-letter recovery |
186: | FEAT-ADM-03 | Audit log | Immutable actor/action/resource/change history |
187: | FEAT-SEC-01 | Privacy controls | Minimize, mask, export, retain and delete |
188: | FEAT-SEC-02 | Support access | Tenant-approved, time-bound and audited |
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/01-product/PRODUCT-VISION-SCOPE.md">
 1: # Product Vision and Scope
 2: 
 3: ## Product statement
 4: 
 5: Ship Dễ is an independent multi-carrier shipping operations and control platform for Vietnamese shops. It uses the shop’s own carrier accounts and contracts to reduce manual work and provide a trustworthy chain from quote to final money reconciliation.
 6: 
 7: ## Who it serves
 8: 
 9: Primary target:
10: 
11: - Shops with stable order volume.
12: - Shops using one or more own carrier accounts/contracts.
13: - Teams currently operating across OMS/POS and multiple carrier portals.
14: - Initial integration preference: Pancake POS plus GHN/GHTK, with Viettel Post and J&T adapters added after partner confirmation.
15: 
16: Operational users:
17: 
18: - Shop owner and operations manager.
19: - Order operator and customer service.
20: - Warehouse receiver.
21: - Finance/accounting.
22: - Ship Dễ operator and rate reviewer.
23: - Recipient through a protected tracking experience.
24: 
25: ## Jobs to be done
26: 
27: 1. Find a carrier that can serve the shipment.
28: 2. Compare normalized live prices and SLA without opening many carrier portals.
29: 3. Create, print, pick up and manage a shipment without re-entering data.
30: 4. Detect delivery problems early and take the safest supported action.
31: 5. Receive returns with evidence.
32: 6. Prove what the carrier should charge and remit under the shop’s real contract.
33: 7. Detect missing, duplicated or abnormal charges and COD.
34: 8. Build and track a claim before the deadline.
35: 
36: ## Product scope
37: 
38: ### Before shipment
39: 
40: - Authentication, users, roles, shop, branches and warehouses.
41: - Carrier account connection and capability discovery.
42: - Order creation/import.
43: - Address normalization and carrier serviceability.
44: - Live quotes, comparison and explainable recommendation.
45: - Shipment creation/update/cancel, pickup and labels.
46: 
47: ### In transit
48: 
49: - Canonical tracking ledger.
50: - Recipient tracking page/PWA.
51: - Exception detection and workbox.
52: - Redelivery or documented manual fallback.
53: - Return monitoring and warehouse receipt.
54: 
55: ### After shipment
56: 
57: - Contract rate/policy normalization and approval.
58: - Source order, statement and optional bank imports.
59: - Matching, audit and missing-settlement classification.
60: - Settlement batch and COD ledger.
61: - Discrepancy cases, evidence, deadlines and claims.
62: - Billing usage ledger, reports and audit log.
63: 
64: ## Boundaries
65: 
66: - No direct custody of shop COD without a separately approved licensed arrangement.
67: - No fake carrier availability, rate or external command result.
68: - No claim is submitted without explicit shop policy authorization.
69: - No ownership of fleet/warehouse is required; workflows support shop/partner assets.
70: - No financial conclusion without the corresponding evidence level.
71: - No cross-tenant access.
72: 
73: ## Definition of full product
74: 
75: The product is complete only when the primary end-to-end journey runs without database/admin intervention:
76: 
77: Create shop → connect carrier → create/import order → serviceability → quote → select → create waybill → label/pickup → tracking/exception/return → settlement audit → claim/report.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/02-business/END-TO-END-PROCESSES.md">
  1: # End-to-End Processes
  2: 
  3: ## Process map
  4: 
  5: \`\`\`mermaid
  6: flowchart LR
  7:   A[Register and configure shop] --> B[Connect carrier accounts]
  8:   B --> C[Create or import source order]
  9:   C --> D[Normalize address]
 10:   D --> E[Check serviceability]
 11:   E --> F[Get live quotes]
 12:   F --> G[Recommend and select carrier]
 13:   G --> H[Create shipment]
 14:   H --> I[Label and pickup]
 15:   I --> J[Track]
 16:   J --> K{Exception?}
 17:   K -- Yes --> L[Workbox and recovery action]
 18:   L --> J
 19:   K -- Return --> M[Receive return with evidence]
 20:   K -- Delivered --> N[Settlement eligibility]
 21:   N --> O[Import carrier statement]
 22:   O --> P[Match and audit]
 23:   P --> Q[Batch and bank reconciliation]
 24:   Q --> R{Finding?}
 25:   R -- No --> S[Close period]
 26:   R -- Yes --> T[Case and claim]
 27:   T --> U[Carrier outcome and recovery]
 28:   U --> S
 29: \`\`\`
 30: 
 31: ## PR-01 Onboard a shop
 32: 
 33: 1. Owner registers or receives an operator-created account.
 34: 2. Verify identity and accept terms/privacy.
 35: 3. Create shop, billing profile, first warehouse and return address.
 36: 4. Invite operational users and assign scopes.
 37: 5. Connect a carrier account; test credentials and capabilities.
 38: 6. Configure defaults, notifications and optional OMS.
 39: 7. Run a test serviceability/quote/create flow using non-production or approved test data.
 40: 
 41: Failure handling:
 42: 
 43: - Setup can be resumed.
 44: - Incomplete dependencies are shown as blocking checklist items.
 45: - Sensitive actions are disabled until roles and account permissions are valid.
 46: 
 47: ## PR-02 Quote and create a shipment
 48: 
 49: 1. Create/import source order and parcel.
 50: 2. Normalize origin/destination with user confirmation when ambiguous.
 51: 3. Check serviceability across connected eligible accounts.
 52: 4. Mark each account AVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN_ERROR.
 53: 5. Request quotes only from AVAILABLE candidates.
 54: 6. Normalize fee components, VAT, SLA and quote expiry.
 55: 7. Recommend cheapest, fastest and balanced options with explanation.
 56: 8. User selects or an approved routing policy selects.
 57: 9. Requote if the selected quote is stale or inputs changed.
 58: 10. Submit create command with idempotency key.
 59: 11. If timeout occurs, query by client order reference before retry.
 60: 12. On success, persist waybill, remote payload snapshot and selected quote.
 61: 13. Retrieve/generate label and offer pickup request.
 62: 14. Sync waybill/status to OMS.
 63: 
 64: No-carrier flow:
 65: 
 66: - Show per-carrier reason.
 67: - Let the user edit only affected inputs and retry without re-entry.
 68: - Save draft or record a manually selected external carrier.
 69: 
 70: ## PR-03 Manage an active shipment
 71: 
 72: 1. Receive webhook and/or poll carrier.
 73: 2. Preserve raw event and map to canonical status.
 74: 3. Update derived current state only after dedupe/order checks.
 75: 4. Detect pickup/delivery exceptions.
 76: 5. Prioritize and assign work.
 77: 6. Perform a supported update/redelivery only after permission and confirmation.
 78: 7. Use carrier-specific manual checklist if action API is unavailable.
 79: 8. Track resolution and metrics.
 80: 
 81: ## PR-04 Receive a return
 82: 
 83: 1. Shipment enters return status and expected-return queue.
 84: 2. Warehouse scans waybill.
 85: 3. System validates tenant/warehouse and prevents duplicate receipt.
 86: 4. Operator completes condition checklist.
 87: 5. Capture media directly with server timestamp and actor.
 88: 6. Create issue case if missing/wrong/damaged.
 89: 7. Confirm receipt and sync inventory/OMS where configured.
 90: 
 91: ## PR-05 Audit a settlement
 92: 
 93: 1. Freeze a period scope and approved rule versions.
 94: 2. Import source orders, carrier statements and actual shop contract rate.
 95: 3. Optionally import bank transactions.
 96: 4. Validate raw/control totals and promote valid revisions.
 97: 5. Match exact keys; queue ambiguity for human resolution.
 98: 6. Select effective rate/settlement rules.
 99: 7. Compute expected fee components and COD.
100: 8. Store one processing status and zero-to-many findings.
101: 9. Classify source-only orders into six missing states.
102: 10. Reconcile carrier batches and optional bank allocations.
103: 11. Create discrepancy cases where appropriate.
104: 12. Review, close period or carry cases forward.
105: 
106: ## PR-06 Manage a claim
107: 
108: 1. Classify claim and select effective Claim Policy.
109: 2. Compute deadline and evidence checklist.
110: 3. Assemble existing evidence; identify gaps.
111: 4. Internally verify amount and claim.
112: 5. Submit after user confirmation or eligible policy authorization.
113: 6. Store carrier reference/response.
114: 7. Track full/partial acceptance, rejection, supplement and unpaid state.
115: 8. Link actual recovery to bank evidence when available.
116: 9. Close with recovered-full or closed-unrecovered outcome.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/02-business/NOTIFICATIONS-REPORTS.md">
 1: # Notifications, Escalations and Reports
 2: 
 3: ## Notification matrix
 4: 
 5: | Event | Default audience | Severity | Channel | Dedupe/escalation |
 6: |---|---|---|---|---|
 7: | Invite/identity/security change | Affected user/owner | High | In-app + email | Never suppress security notice |
 8: | Carrier token invalid/expiring | Owner/ops | High | In-app + email | Escalate until fixed |
 9: | Serviceability all unavailable | Order operator | Medium | In-app | One per order/input version |
10: | Carrier API outage/timeout | Ops | Medium | In-app | Group by carrier incident |
11: | Create outcome unknown | Operator/manager | Critical | In-app + email | Remains open until reconciled |
12: | Pickup overdue | Ops/warehouse | High | In-app | Escalate by age |
13: | Delivery exception | CS/ops | High | In-app | Group by shipment/exception |
14: | Return expected/overdue | Warehouse/ops | Medium | In-app | Daily digest plus critical aging |
15: | Import blocked | Finance/operator | High | In-app | One per import revision |
16: | Manual match required | Finance/operator | Medium | In-app | Queue count digest |
17: | Audit finding created | Finance | Medium | In-app | Group by audit run |
18: | Bank short/over | Finance/owner | High | In-app + email | Remains until resolved |
19: | Claim deadline approaching | Finance/owner | Critical | In-app + email | Multi-level reminders |
20: | Claim accepted but unpaid | Finance | High | In-app | Aging escalation |
21: 
22: Users may configure noncritical channels and digests. Security, unknown create outcome and claim-deadline critical alerts cannot be fully disabled.
23: 
24: ## Report catalog
25: 
26: | ID | Report | Core dimensions/measures |
27: |---|---|---|
28: | REP-OPS-01 | Shipment operations | Created, failed, unknown, cancelled, picked, delivered, returned |
29: | REP-QTE-01 | Quote comparison | Availability, response latency, total cost, selected carrier |
30: | REP-CAR-01 | Carrier performance | SLA, delivery success, exceptions, return, fee variance |
31: | REP-EXC-01 | Exception rescue | Type, age, owner, action, outcome, prevented return |
32: | REP-RET-01 | Return receiving | Expected, received, duplicate, damage/mismatch evidence |
33: | REP-DQ-01 | Data quality | Readable, valid, missing, ambiguous and stale data |
34: | REP-AUD-01 | Audit findings | Processing status, finding type, amount, evidence |
35: | REP-MIS-01 | Missing settlement | Six states and aging |
36: | REP-BAT-01 | Settlement batches | Carrier transfer status and bank status separately |
37: | REP-COD-01 | COD ledger | Expected, carrier reported and actually received |
38: | REP-CASE-01 | Case portfolio | State, age, deadline, owner and outcome |
39: | REP-MONEY-01 | Evidence-level money | Suspected, verified, accepted and received separately |
40: | REP-BIL-01 | Ship Dễ usage | First billable event, price version and adjustments |
41: | REP-SEC-01 | Access/audit | Sensitive views, exports, deletes and support access |
42: 
43: Every summary supports drill-down to underlying records, calculation and source lineage. Export includes generation time, filters and data/rule version.
</file>

 1: # RBAC and Approval Matrix
 2: 
 3: Legend: A = full action, V = view, S = scoped/configurable, – = denied.
 4: 
 5: | Capability | Owner | Ops manager | Order operator | CS | Warehouse | Finance | Rate author | Rate reviewer | Ship Dễ operator |
 6: |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
 7: | Shop configuration | A | S | – | – | – | V | – | – | S |
 8: | Manage users/roles | A | S | – | – | – | – | – | – | S |
 9: | Connect observe token | A | S | – | – | – | – | – | – | S |
10: | Grant action permission | A | S | – | – | – | – | – | – | – |
11: | View/create source order | A | A | A | V | S | V | – | – | S |
12: | Quote/select carrier | A | A | A | V | – | V | – | – | S |
13: | Create/update shipment | A | A | A | S | – | – | – | – | S |
14: | Cancel/redeliver | A | A | S | S | – | – | – | – | S |
15: | Print/hand over | A | A | A | – | A | – | – | – | S |
16: | Track/view exceptions | A | A | A | A | S | V | – | – | S |
17: | Receive return/evidence | A | A | – | – | A | V | – | – | S |
18: | View contract rates | A | V | – | – | – | A | A | A | S |
19: | Author rate/policy | S | – | – | – | – | S | A | – | S |
20: | Approve rate/policy | A | – | – | – | – | S | – | A | S |
21: | Import settlement/bank | A | – | – | – | – | A | – | – | S |
22: | Run/review audit | A | V | – | – | – | A | – | – | S |
23: | Allocate bank receipt | A | – | – | – | – | A | – | – | S |
24: | Verify/submit claim | A | S | – | – | – | A | – | – | S |
25: | Export PII/finance | A | – | – | – | – | S | – | – | Time-bound |
26: | View immutable audit log | A | S | – | – | – | S | – | – | Time-bound |
27: 
28: ## Approval rules
29: 
30: | Action | Required approval |
31: |---|---|
32: | Approve rate/settlement/claim policy | Reviewer different from author |
33: | Grant carrier action permission | Owner or explicitly delegated manager |
34: | Cancel after pickup | Normally prohibited; approved exception procedure if carrier supports |
35: | Enable auto-routing | Owner/ops manager |
36: | Enable automatic claim submission | Owner plus finance; claim type and amount limit |
37: | Reopen a closed settlement period | Finance approver plus reason |
38: | Bank allocation correction after confirmation | Finance approver plus audit |
39: | Delete/export large PII dataset | Owner/authorized data administrator |
40: | Temporary Ship Dễ support access | Shop consent, scoped purpose and expiry |
41: 
42: ## Enforcement
43: 
44: - Backend is authoritative; hidden UI controls are insufficient.
45: - A user cannot grant a permission they do not hold.
46: - Permission evaluation includes tenant, branch, warehouse and carrier-account scope.
47: - Sensitive export/action checks require a fresh session or step-up authentication when configured.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/02-business/STATE-MACHINES.md">
  1: # State Machines
  2: 
  3: ## User registration and lifecycle (ST-USER)
  4: 
  5: ```mermaid
  6: stateDiagram-v2
  7:   [*] --> PENDING_VERIFICATION: self-register (FEAT-AUTH-01)
  8:   PENDING_VERIFICATION --> ACTIVE: verify email or phone (BR-AUTH-02)
  9:   PENDING_VERIFICATION --> PENDING_VERIFICATION: resend verification token
 10:   PENDING_VERIFICATION --> DISABLED: abuse/cleanup
 11:   ACTIVE --> SUSPENDED: admin suspension (FEAT-USR-02)
 12:   SUSPENDED --> ACTIVE: admin reinstate
 13:   ACTIVE --> DISABLED: account deactivation
 14: ```
 15: 
 16: ## User invite
 17: 
 18: \`\`\`mermaid
 19: stateDiagram-v2
 20: [*] --> PENDING
 21: PENDING --> ACCEPTED
 22: PENDING --> EXPIRED
 23: PENDING --> CANCELLED
 24: EXPIRED --> PENDING: resend
 25: \`\`\`
 26: 
 27: ## Carrier account
 28: 
 29: \`\`\`mermaid
 30: stateDiagram-v2
 31: [*] --> DRAFT
 32: DRAFT --> TESTING
 33: TESTING --> ACTIVE
 34: TESTING --> INVALID
 35: ACTIVE --> DEGRADED
 36: DEGRADED --> ACTIVE
 37: ACTIVE --> EXPIRED
 38: EXPIRED --> TESTING: rotate
 39: ACTIVE --> REVOKED
 40: \`\`\`
 41: 
 42: ## Quote
 43: 
 44: \`\`\`mermaid
 45: stateDiagram-v2
 46: [*] --> REQUESTED
 47: REQUESTED --> AVAILABLE
 48: REQUESTED --> UNSUPPORTED
 49: REQUESTED --> UNKNOWN_ERROR
 50: AVAILABLE --> SELECTED
 51: AVAILABLE --> EXPIRED
 52: SELECTED --> INVALIDATED: input changes
 53: \`\`\`
 54: 
 55: ## Shipment
 56: 
 57: \`\`\`mermaid
 58: stateDiagram-v2
 59: [*] --> DRAFT
 60: DRAFT --> CREATING
 61: CREATING --> CREATED
 62: CREATING --> CREATE_FAILED
 63: CREATING --> CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
 64: CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN --> CREATED: reconcile found
 65: CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN --> CREATING: safe retry
 66: CREATED --> READY_TO_PICK
 67: READY_TO_PICK --> PICKED
 68: READY_TO_PICK --> CANCELLED
 69: PICKED --> IN_TRANSIT
 70: IN_TRANSIT --> DELIVERY_FAILED
 71: DELIVERY_FAILED --> IN_TRANSIT: redelivery
 72: DELIVERY_FAILED --> RETURNING
 73: IN_TRANSIT --> DELIVERED
 74: RETURNING --> RETURNED
 75: \`\`\`
 76: 
 77: Carrier raw states never directly replace canonical history; mapping derives canonical transitions.
 78: 
 79: ## Operational exception
 80: 
 81: \`\`\`mermaid
 82: stateDiagram-v2
 83: [*] --> OPEN
 84: OPEN --> ACKNOWLEDGED
 85: ACKNOWLEDGED --> IN_PROGRESS
 86: IN_PROGRESS --> SNOOZED
 87: SNOOZED --> IN_PROGRESS
 88: IN_PROGRESS --> RESOLVED
 89: RESOLVED --> REOPENED
 90: REOPENED --> IN_PROGRESS
 91: \`\`\`
 92: 
 93: ## Return receipt
 94: 
 95: \`\`\`mermaid
 96: stateDiagram-v2
 97: [*] --> EXPECTED
 98: EXPECTED --> SCANNED
 99: SCANNED --> INSPECTING
100: INSPECTING --> RECEIVED_OK
101: INSPECTING --> RECEIVED_WITH_ISSUE
102: \`\`\`
103: 
104: ## Import and audit run
105: 
106: \`\`\`mermaid
107: stateDiagram-v2
108: [*] --> UPLOADED
109: UPLOADED --> VALIDATING
110: VALIDATING --> BLOCKED
111: VALIDATING --> STAGED
112: STAGED --> PROMOTED
113: PROMOTED --> SUPERSEDED: new revision
114: \`\`\`
115: 
116: \`\`\`mermaid
117: stateDiagram-v2
118: [*] --> QUEUED
119: QUEUED --> RUNNING
120: RUNNING --> COMPLETED
121: RUNNING --> FAILED
122: COMPLETED --> OFFICIAL
123: \`\`\`
124: 
125: ## Processing status
126: 
127: Exactly one per waybill snapshot:
128: 
129: - MATCHED
130: - SOURCE_ONLY
131: - CARRIER_ONLY
132: - AMBIGUOUS
133: - DATA_INCOMPLETE
134: 
135: Findings are separate records and do not form this state machine.
136: 
137: ## Settlement batch
138: 
139: Two independent dimensions:
140: 
141: Carrier transfer:
142: 
143: - NOT_REPORTED
144: - REPORTED
145: 
146: Bank reconciliation:
147: 
148: - NO_DATA
149: - UNMATCHED
150: - MATCHED_FULL
151: - RECEIVED_SHORT
152: - RECEIVED_OVER
153: 
154: ## Discrepancy case
155: 
156: \`\`\`mermaid
157: stateDiagram-v2
158: [*] --> SUSPECTED
159: SUSPECTED --> NEEDS_DATA
160: NEEDS_DATA --> SUSPECTED
161: SUSPECTED --> INTERNALLY_VERIFIED
162: SUSPECTED --> DISMISSED
163: INTERNALLY_VERIFIED --> READY_TO_SUBMIT
164: READY_TO_SUBMIT --> SUBMITTED
165: SUBMITTED --> CARRIER_ACCEPTED_FULL
166: SUBMITTED --> CARRIER_ACCEPTED_PARTIAL
167: SUBMITTED --> CARRIER_REJECTED
168: CARRIER_ACCEPTED_PARTIAL --> SUPPLEMENTING
169: CARRIER_REJECTED --> SUPPLEMENTING
170: SUPPLEMENTING --> SUBMITTED
171: CARRIER_ACCEPTED_FULL --> ACCEPTED_UNPAID
172: CARRIER_ACCEPTED_PARTIAL --> ACCEPTED_UNPAID
173: ACCEPTED_UNPAID --> PARTIALLY_RECOVERED
174: PARTIALLY_RECOVERED --> RECOVERED_FULL
175: ACCEPTED_UNPAID --> RECOVERED_FULL
176: RECOVERED_FULL --> CLOSED_RECOVERED
177: CARRIER_REJECTED --> CLOSED_UNRECOVERED
178: \`\`\`
179: 
180: Carry-forward is a case-period link, not a case state.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/03-ux/DESIGN-SYSTEM-UX-RULES.md">
 1: # Design System and UX Rules
 2: 
 3: ## Product UX principles
 4: 
 5: 1. One data entry should feed all downstream stages.
 6: 2. Fixing address/parcel data preserves the rest of the order.
 7: 3. The primary next action is obvious; destructive/external actions are confirmed.
 8: 4. Financial conclusions show evidence and calculation.
 9: 5. Provider errors use actionable language, never generic failure alone.
10: 6. Automation is visible, explainable and overridable under permission.
11: 7. Dense operational screens prioritize tables, filters and keyboard efficiency over decorative cards.
12: 
13: ## Visual foundation
14: 
15: - Use a restrained modern SaaS palette with one primary brand color, neutral surfaces and semantic status colors.
16: - Minimum WCAG AA contrast for text and controls.
17: - 8px spacing system; consistent 4/8/12/16/24/32 increments.
18: - Typography hierarchy: page title, section title, label, body, helper, metadata.
19: - Tables use sticky headers, compact/comfortable density and horizontal overflow handling.
20: 
21: ## Canonical components
22: 
23: - App shell, side navigation, top context selector.
24: - Data table, saved view, filter bar and bulk action bar.
25: - Form field wrappers and schema error summary.
26: - Stepper/checklist.
27: - Status badge and evidence badge.
28: - Money comparison cells.
29: - Timeline/event ledger.
30: - File uploader/import issue viewer.
31: - Confirmation dialog with effect summary.
32: - Workbox item/assignment control.
33: - Toast plus persistent notification center.
34: - Skeleton, empty, forbidden, not-found and incident state.
35: 
36: ## Content rules
37: 
38: - Say what happened, why, whether data was changed and what to do next.
39: - Distinguish: carrier rejected, carrier unavailable, credentials invalid and provider could not be reached.
40: - Never claim money received without bank evidence.
41: - Never label a suspicion as confirmed carrier error.
42: - Show exact scope of destructive actions: carrier, account, order and effect.
43: 
44: ## Responsive
45: 
46: - Desktop is primary for order/finance operations.
47: - Tablet supports warehouse and operational queues.
48: - Mobile/PWA prioritizes scan, tracking, exception acknowledgement and recipient views.
49: - Dense comparison/audit tables may use a summary card plus drill-down on narrow screens; data is not removed.
50: 
51: ## Accessibility
52: 
53: - Keyboard order and visible focus.
54: - Labels independent of placeholders.
55: - Status conveyed by text/icon, not color alone.
56: - Dialog focus trap and return.
57: - Live announcements for async command completion.
58: - Accessible table headers and error summaries.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/04-data/DATA-LIFECYCLE-IMPORTS.md">
 1: # Data Lifecycle, Sources and Imports
 2: 
 3: ## Source-of-truth matrix
 4: 
 5: | Data | Primary source | Notes |
 6: |---|---|---|
 7: | Source order/COD expected | OMS/manual approved source | Versioned snapshot |
 8: | Address canonical selection | User-confirmed Ship Dễ mapping | Carrier IDs are adapter mappings |
 9: | Pre-shipment availability/quote | Carrier API response for exact account/input | Time-bound evidence |
10: | Shipment/waybill result | Carrier action response plus reconciliation lookup | Unknown outcome remains explicit |
11: | Tracking raw event | Carrier webhook/poll response | Canonical state is derived |
12: | Expected charge | Approved actual contract rate version | Not current public quote by default |
13: | Actual charged amount | Carrier settlement statement | Carrier claim, not bank proof |
14: | Actual receipt | Bank/payment evidence | Batch-level allocation |
15: | Claim acceptance | Carrier response evidence | Separate from payment |
16: 
17: ## Import lifecycle
18: 
19: 1. UPLOADED: private object stored; malware check and hash.
20: 2. VALIDATING: format/header/type/control totals.
21: 3. BLOCKED: key/control error prevents promotion.
22: 4. STAGED: rows normalized; nonblocking gaps retained.
23: 5. PROMOTED: immutable revision eligible for snapshots.
24: 6. SUPERSEDED: newer confirmed logical revision replaces future use.
25: 
26: No silent partial import:
27: 
28: - Missing/invalid keys and control-total mismatch block promotion.
29: - Optional field absence marks only dependent checks data-incomplete.
30: - Every excluded row has a visible issue record.
31: 
32: ## Required source-order fields
33: 
34: - Carrier/account if shipment exists.
35: - Waybill if shipment exists.
36: - Source order ID.
37: - Expected COD.
38: - Delivery status, source and status_as_of.
39: - Delivered/created/handover dates as available.
40: - Declared weight/dimensions.
41: - Service, route/zone, payer, declared value and return status.
42: 
43: ## Carrier statement fields
44: 
45: - Carrier/account, waybill, source order ID if present.
46: - Batch reference.
47: - Carrier COD.
48: - Individual fee components.
49: - Carrier charged weight.
50: - Batch totals.
51: - Actual carrier close/report dates.
52: 
53: ## Bank fields
54: 
55: - Transaction ID, transfer reference, posting date, amount and direction.
56: - Unrelated transaction PII should be masked/removed before ingestion where practical.
57: 
58: ## Lineage
59: 
60: Every normalized record stores:
61: 
62: - source_file_id, revision, sheet and row.
63: - raw payload/hash.
64: - mapping version.
65: - normalization version.
66: - promotion time and actor.
67: 
68: Every audit result stores exact input revisions and rule versions.
69: 
70: ## Retention
71: 
72: Retention periods are configuration plus legal/product policy, not hardcoded. Deletion:
73: 
74: - Must preserve legally/business-required audit metadata.
75: - Removes or irreversibly anonymizes PII when eligible.
76: - Is logged with actor, scope, reason and outcome.
77: - Never breaks financial lineage without an approved archival representation.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/04-data/DOMAIN-MODEL-ERD.md">
 1: # Domain Model and ERD
 2: 
 3: ## Aggregates
 4: 
 5: ### Identity and tenancy
 6: 
 7: - Tenant, Shop, Branch, Warehouse.
 8: - User, Membership, Role, Permission, UserSession, Invitation.
 9: 
10: ### Carrier and shipping
11: 
12: - Carrier, CarrierService, CarrierAccount, CarrierCapability, CredentialVersion.
13: - SourceOrder, OrderItem, Parcel.
14: - Address, CarrierAddressMapping.
15: - QuoteRequest, CarrierQuote, RoutingDecision.
16: - Shipment, ShipmentCommand, Label, PickupRequest.
17: - TrackingEvent, ShipmentCurrentState, OperationalException.
18: - ReturnReceipt, ReturnEvidence.
19: 
20: ### Audit and money
21: 
22: - SourceFile, ImportBatch, ImportRow, ImportIssue.
23: - ContractDocument, RateContractVersion, RateRule.
24: - SettlementPolicyVersion, ClaimPolicyVersion.
25: - AuditPeriod, AuditRun, AuditSnapshot.
26: - MatchLink, ProcessingResult, Finding.
27: - SettlementBatch, SettlementLine.
28: - BankTransaction, BatchBankAllocation.
29: - DiscrepancyCase, CaseEvent, Evidence, ClaimSubmission, RecoveryReceipt.
30: - BillingEvent, UsageStatement.
31: - AuditEvent, Notification, SupportAccessGrant.
32: 
33: ## Core relationships
34: 
35: \`\`\`mermaid
36: erDiagram
37:   TENANT ||--o{ USER_MEMBERSHIP : has
38:   TENANT ||--o{ SHOP : owns
39:   SHOP ||--o{ BRANCH : has
40:   BRANCH ||--o{ WAREHOUSE : has
41:   SHOP ||--o{ CARRIER_ACCOUNT : connects
42:   WAREHOUSE ||--o{ SOURCE_ORDER : originates
43:   SOURCE_ORDER ||--|{ ORDER_ITEM : contains
44:   SOURCE_ORDER ||--|{ PARCEL : packs
45:   SOURCE_ORDER ||--o{ QUOTE_REQUEST : requests
46:   QUOTE_REQUEST ||--o{ CARRIER_QUOTE : returns
47:   CARRIER_QUOTE ||--o| ROUTING_DECISION : selected
48:   SOURCE_ORDER ||--o{ SHIPMENT : fulfills
49:   SHIPMENT ||--o{ SHIPMENT_COMMAND : changes
50:   SHIPMENT ||--o{ TRACKING_EVENT : records
51:   SHIPMENT ||--o{ OPERATIONAL_EXCEPTION : raises
52:   SHIPMENT ||--o| RETURN_RECEIPT : returns
53:   CARRIER_ACCOUNT ||--o{ RATE_CONTRACT_VERSION : prices
54:   CARRIER_ACCOUNT ||--o{ SETTLEMENT_POLICY_VERSION : settles
55:   AUDIT_PERIOD ||--o{ AUDIT_RUN : runs
56:   AUDIT_RUN ||--o{ PROCESSING_RESULT : produces
57:   PROCESSING_RESULT ||--o{ FINDING : contains
58:   FINDING ||--o| DISCREPANCY_CASE : opens
59:   SETTLEMENT_BATCH ||--o{ SETTLEMENT_LINE : contains
60:   SETTLEMENT_BATCH ||--o{ BATCH_BANK_ALLOCATION : allocates
61:   BANK_TRANSACTION ||--o{ BATCH_BANK_ALLOCATION : allocates
62:   DISCREPANCY_CASE ||--o{ CASE_EVENT : history
63:   DISCREPANCY_CASE ||--o{ CLAIM_SUBMISSION : submits
64:   DISCREPANCY_CASE ||--o{ RECOVERY_RECEIPT : recovers
65: \`\`\`
66: 
67: ## Modeling rules
68: 
69: - Every business table carries tenant_id, created_at and created_by where meaningful.
70: - Carrier waybill uniqueness is carrier_account_id + normalized_waybill, not global waybill.
71: - Raw carrier/import/event payloads are immutable and stored separately from normalized fields.
72: - Commands and external responses have correlation_id and idempotency_key.
73: - Financial values are integer VND; never floating point.
74: - Timestamps are UTC; business display and settlement calendar use Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh unless policy says otherwise.
75: - Historical snapshots reference exact rule/data versions.
76: - Soft delete is limited to configurable/master data. Financial, command, audit and evidence records are append-only or status-closed.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/CARRIER-ADAPTER.md">
 1: # Carrier Adapter Contract
 2: 
 3: ## Goals
 4: 
 5: - One canonical interface for frontend/domain services.
 6: - Carrier-specific payloads and statuses remain inside adapters.
 7: - Capability checks precede commands.
 8: - Adapters preserve raw evidence and return normalized outcomes.
 9: 
10: ## Canonical methods
11: 
12: \`\`\`typescript
13: interface CarrierAdapter {
14:   testConnection(ctx: AccountContext): Promise<ConnectionTest>;
15:   getCapabilities(ctx: AccountContext): Promise<CapabilitySet>;
16:   normalizeAddress(input: CanonicalAddress): Promise<AddressMappingResult>;
17:   checkServiceability(input: ServiceabilityRequest): Promise<ServiceabilityResult>;
18:   getQuotes(input: QuoteRequest): Promise<CarrierQuote[]>;
19:   createShipment(input: CreateShipmentRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
20:   findShipmentByClientRef(input: ClientReferenceLookup): Promise<RemoteShipmentLookup>;
21:   getShipment(input: ShipmentLookup): Promise<CarrierShipment>;
22:   updateShipment(input: UpdateShipmentRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
23:   cancelShipment(input: CancelShipmentRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
24:   getLabel(input: LabelRequest): Promise<LabelResult>;
25:   requestPickup(input: PickupRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
26:   trackShipment(input: ShipmentLookup): Promise<CarrierTrackingResult>;
27:   requestRedelivery(input: RedeliveryRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
28:   fetchSettlement(input: SettlementRequest): Promise<SettlementResult>;
29:   submitClaim(input: ClaimRequest, idem: IdempotencyContext): Promise<CommandResult>;
30: }
31: \`\`\`
32: 
33: ## Capability result
34: 
35: Each method capability carries:
36: 
37: - support: SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED, PARTNER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED or TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE.
38: - permission: required token/account scope.
39: - environment: sandbox/production.
40: - evidence level and source URL/reference.
41: - last verified at.
42: - constraints by status/service/account.
43: 
44: ## Normalized command outcomes
45: 
46: - SUCCEEDED: provider acknowledged effect with durable reference.
47: - REJECTED: explicit business/auth/validation rejection.
48: - OUTCOME_UNKNOWN: network/timeout after request may have reached provider.
49: - UNSUPPORTED: capability not available for account/provider.
50: - TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE: known outage/circuit open.
51: 
52: Only REJECTED known-safe or verified not-found permits a new attempt according to policy. OUTCOME_UNKNOWN starts reconciliation.
53: 
54: ## Adapter responsibilities
55: 
56: - Authentication/header/signature.
57: - Provider address/service mapping.
58: - Payload conversion and unit conversion.
59: - Provider error classification.
60: - Sanitized raw request/response evidence.
61: - Status mapping and unknown-status preservation.
62: - Webhook signature verification/deduplication key.
63: - Rate-limit and retry hints.
64: - Provider-specific reconciliation lookup.
65: 
66: ## Domain responsibilities
67: 
68: - Permission and approval.
69: - Routing policy.
70: - Command idempotency record.
71: - State transition.
72: - Notifications/workbox.
73: - Audit and billing.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/CARRIER-CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md">
 1: # Carrier Capability Matrix
 2: 
 3: Evidence date: 2026-08-24. Production use requires a connected shop account and sandbox/partner verification even when public documentation exists.
 4: 
 5: Legend:
 6: 
 7: - O: VERIFIED_OFFICIAL public documentation.
 8: - P: PARTNER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.
 9: - U: UNVERIFIED; implement interface stub and manual fallback only.
10: 
11: | Capability | GHN | GHTK | Viettel Post | J&T Vietnam |
12: |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
13: | Address master/mapping | O | O/partial | P | P |
14: | Serviceability/service list | O | O/solution/fee response | P | P |
15: | Live fee quote | O | O | P | Public web only; partner API P |
16: | EDD/SLA | O | P/response-dependent | P | P |
17: | Create shipment | O | O | P | P |
18: | Lookup by client reference | O | P | P | P |
19: | Update shipment | O/status constrained | P | P | P |
20: | Cancel before pickup | O | O | P | P |
21: | Label | O | O | P | P |
22: | Pickup/shift | O | Account/flow dependent P | P | P |
23: | Tracking polling | O | O | P | Public tracking; partner API P |
24: | Status webhook | O | O | P | P |
25: | Update COD | O/status constrained | P | P | P |
26: | Redelivery | O | P | P | P |
27: | Return command | O | P | P | P |
28: | Settlement API | U/file fallback | U/file fallback | U/file fallback | U/file fallback |
29: | Claim/ticket API | O ticket surface; business fit P | P | P | P |
30: 
31: ## Interpretation
32: 
33: - This table proves interface feasibility, not automatic permission.
34: - A provider may expose a public endpoint but restrict it by shop/account/status.
35: - For Viettel Post and J&T Vietnam, public consumer pages or third-party integrations are insufficient evidence for production endpoint/schema.
36: - Until partner confirmation, Ship Dễ supports manual/file workflows for those capabilities and returns PARTNER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED.
37: 
38: ## Confirmation checklist
39: 
40: For every P capability obtain:
41: 
42: 1. Official partner documentation/version.
43: 2. Test and production base URLs.
44: 3. Authentication and permission scopes.
45: 4. Sample requests/responses and errors.
46: 5. Idempotency/client-reference behavior.
47: 6. Status constraints.
48: 7. Webhook signature/retry semantics.
49: 8. Rate limits/SLA/support channel.
50: 9. Contractual permission to store/process returned data.
51: 10. Sandbox test evidence stored in the decision log.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/ERROR-IDEMPOTENCY-RETRY.md">
 1: # Error, Idempotency and Retry Contract
 2: 
 3: ## Canonical error classes
 4: 
 5: | Code | Meaning | Retry |
 6: |---|---|---|
 7: | VALIDATION_ERROR | Invalid user/input data | After correction |
 8: | FORBIDDEN | Permission/scope denied | No |
 9: | CONFLICT | Version/state/idempotency conflict | Re-fetch |
10: | CARRIER_UNSUPPORTED | Explicit capability/route rejection | No until input/config changes |
11: | CARRIER_AUTH_REQUIRED | Invalid/insufficient credentials | After account fix |
12: | CARRIER_RATE_LIMITED | Provider limit | Scheduled retry per header/policy |
13: | CARRIER_TIMEOUT | No timely response | Reads may retry; commands reconcile first |
14: | CARRIER_UNAVAILABLE | Provider outage/circuit open | Deferred retry/manual |
15: | CARRIER_RESPONSE_INVALID | Schema/unexpected response | Quarantine and adapter incident |
16: | COMMAND_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN | External effect may have occurred | Remote reconciliation only |
17: | DATA_INCOMPLETE | Evidence missing for a rule | Add data |
18: | RULE_NOT_APPROVED | Rule cannot support conclusion | Approve/fix version |
19: | IMPORT_BLOCKED | Key/control validation failed | Correct revision |
20: 
21: ## Idempotency
22: 
23: - Required for create shipment, update/cancel, pickup, redelivery, claim submission, period close, bank confirmation and billing event.
24: - Store tenant, operation, key, request hash, command state, result reference and expiry policy.
25: - Same key + same request returns existing command/result.
26: - Same key + different request returns IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
27: - Idempotency records outlive typical client retry windows and are never deleted before external reconciliation guarantees.
28: 
29: ## Retry policy
30: 
31: Safe automatic retry:
32: 
33: - Read-only GET/query.
34: - Webhook/event processing after durable dedupe.
35: - Background calculations using immutable snapshot.
36: 
37: Conditional retry:
38: 
39: - Rate-limited read/write only when provider declares safety or client idempotency is proven.
40: - External commands only after provider lookup proves not applied.
41: 
42: Never blind retry:
43: 
44: - Shipment create with unknown outcome.
45: - Cancel/update/redelivery when remote state is unknown.
46: - Claim submission.
47: - Bank allocation confirmation.
48: 
49: ## Circuit breaker
50: 
51: Per carrier account and capability:
52: 
53: - Closed: normal.
54: - Open: fail fast with TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE/manual fallback.
55: - Half-open: bounded probe.
56: 
57: An account auth failure does not open the carrier globally. A provider incident does not disable unrelated carriers.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/GHN.md">
 1: # GHN Integration
 2: 
 3: Evidence level: VERIFIED_OFFICIAL for the public API surface listed below; shop permission and sandbox behavior still require verification.
 4: 
 5: Official documentation home: https://api.ghn.vn/home/docs
 6: 
 7: Observed public capabilities include:
 8: 
 9: - Province/district/ward master data.
10: - Available services.
11: - Fee calculation and expected delivery time.
12: - Create, preview, detail by waybill/client order code.
13: - Update, cancel, return, print and pickup shifts.
14: - Update COD and delivery again.
15: - Status callback/webhook and status/failure reason catalog.
16: - Ticket surface.
17: 
18: ## Required implementation rules
19: 
20: - Store GHN shop_id/account scope and token secret reference.
21: - Use GHN IDs only inside adapter mappings; domain keeps canonical address.
22: - Query available services before quote/create.
23: - Persist selected service and raw fee components.
24: - Use client_order_code as reconciliation reference when supported.
25: - On timeout, query order by client reference before create retry.
26: - Respect status-specific update/COD/cancel/redelivery constraints from current documentation.
27: - Verify callback authenticity using the current supported mechanism; if no strong signature is documented for the account, combine allow-list/secret strategy with polling reconciliation and record the residual risk.
28: 
29: ## Mandatory sandbox cases
30: 
31: - Supported and unsupported route.
32: - Fee components and volumetric weight.
33: - Create success, validation failure and timeout/unknown simulation.
34: - Query by client reference.
35: - Cancel before and after pickup.
36: - Update COD in allowed/disallowed states.
37: - Delivery-again in allowed/disallowed states.
38: - Duplicate/out-of-order callback.
39: - Unknown status/failure code.
40: 
41: Endpoint paths are not duplicated here as immutable truth; the adapter configuration and tests are pinned to the provider version verified at implementation time.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/GHTK.md">
 1: # GHTK Integration
 2: 
 3: Evidence level: VERIFIED_OFFICIAL for the documented OpenAPI surface; actual token permissions and account behavior require sandbox verification.
 4: 
 5: Official documentation: https://docs.giaohangtietkiem.vn/
 6: 
 7: Observed public capabilities include:
 8: 
 9: - Token authentication with configurable access permissions.
10: - Submit shipment.
11: - Shipment status.
12: - Solution/service list.
13: - Fee calculation.
14: - Label printing.
15: - Cancellation.
16: - Pickup-address list and address/product support.
17: - Status webhook.
18: - Enterprise/partner flows including account-related APIs subject to partner permissions.
19: 
20: ## Required implementation rules
21: 
22: - Token permissions are least-privilege and stored per shop account.
23: - X-Client-Source/partner code is configuration, not hardcoded.
24: - Account-creation APIs are not treated as generally available; enable only after GHTK partner permission.
25: - Persist GHTK tracking label and shop reference.
26: - Separate explicit rejection from transport timeout.
27: - If no documented reliable lookup by client reference is confirmed, unknown create outcome remains manual/partner reconciliation rather than blind retry.
28: - Parse fee response into normalized components while retaining raw response.
29: - Use webhook plus polling reconciliation when needed.
30: 
31: ## Mandatory sandbox cases
32: 
33: - Authentication and permission-denied per method.
34: - Fee quote and special address behavior.
35: - Create and duplicate client reference behavior.
36: - Create timeout reconciliation path.
37: - Label response formats.
38: - Cancel in allowed/disallowed statuses.
39: - Webhook duplicate/out-of-order delivery.
40: - Token expiry/revocation.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/INTERNAL-API.md">
 1: # Internal API Contract
 2: 
 3: The authoritative machine contract is contracts/openapi.yaml. This document defines resource semantics and command rules.
 4: 
 5: ## API conventions
 6: 
 7: - Base path: /api/v1.
 8: - JSON UTF-8; timestamps ISO-8601 UTC; money integer VND.
 9: - Bearer session/access token; tenant derived from authorized membership, never trusted from arbitrary client scope.
10: - Cursor or page pagination consistently per endpoint family.
11: - Every external-effect command requires Idempotency-Key and returns correlation_id.
12: - Errors use canonical error envelope.
13: - ETag/version field is used for optimistic concurrency on editable aggregates.
14: 
15: ## Resource groups
16: 
17: | Prefix | Purpose |
18: |---|---|
19: | /auth | Register, verify, login, MFA, refresh, logout, recovery |
20: | /me | Profile, sessions, memberships, preferences |
21: | /shops | Shop, branches and warehouses |
22: | /users, /roles | Invitations, users, roles and scopes |
23: | /carrier-accounts | Connection, capability and health |
24: | /orders | Source orders, items and parcels |
25: | /shipping-options | Serviceability, quotes and recommendations |
26: | /shipments | Create/update/cancel, labels and pickup |
27: | /tracking | Timeline/current state and recipient-safe view |
28: | /exceptions | Workbox, assignment and recovery actions |
29: | /returns | Expected returns, scan and evidence |
30: | /rates, /policies | Versions, rules, simulator and approval |
31: | /imports | Upload, validation, staging and promotion |
32: | /audit-periods, /audit-runs | Settlement audit lifecycle |
33: | /batches, /bank-transactions | Batch status and allocations |
34: | /cases, /claims | Discrepancy workflow and submissions |
35: | /reports | Role-scoped summaries/exports |
36: | /billing | Usage ledger and statements |
37: | /admin | Mapping, jobs, queues and immutable audit |
38: 
39: ## Command response
40: 
41: Successful asynchronous command:
42: 
43: \`\`\`json
44: {
45:   "data": {
46:     "command_id": "uuid",
47:     "status": "PENDING",
48:     "resource_id": "uuid"
49:   },
50:   "meta": {
51:     "correlation_id": "string"
52:   }
53: }
54: \`\`\`
55: 
56: Unknown carrier outcome is a valid command state, not an HTTP success/failure guess:
57: 
58: \`\`\`json
59: {
60:   "data": {
61:     "command_id": "uuid",
62:     "status": "OUTCOME_UNKNOWN",
63:     "next_action": "REMOTE_RECONCILIATION"
64:   },
65:   "meta": {
66:     "correlation_id": "string"
67:   }
68: }
69: \`\`\`
70: 
71: ## Error envelope
72: 
73: \`\`\`json
74: {
75:   "error": {
76:     "code": "CARRIER_TIMEOUT",
77:     "message": "Chưa xác định hãng đã tạo vận đơn hay chưa.",
78:     "retryable": false,
79:     "next_action": "WAIT_FOR_RECONCILIATION",
80:     "fields": []
81:   },
82:   "meta": {
83:     "correlation_id": "string"
84:   }
85: }
86: \`\`\`
87: 
88: Provider error text is stored in sanitized integration logs, not exposed raw when it contains sensitive or confusing data.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/05-api-integrations/OMS-BANK-WEBHOOKS.md">
 1: # OMS, Bank and Webhook Integrations
 2: 
 3: ## Pancake/OMS adapter
 4: 
 5: Canonical operations:
 6: 
 7: - Pull or receive source order changes with cursor/watermark.
 8: - Upsert by tenant + source system + source order code.
 9: - Preserve source payload/revision.
10: - Push waybill, selected carrier, label link and canonical shipping status where permitted.
11: - Prevent feedback loops using origin/correlation metadata.
12: - Backfill and reconcile missed updates.
13: - CSV/XLSX import remains fallback.
14: 
15: Production Pancake endpoints/scopes require current official/partner documentation and account consent.
16: 
17: ## Bank source
18: 
19: Initial mode is private CSV/XLSX import. Optional bank API can implement the same canonical contract.
20: 
21: Rules:
22: 
23: - Only inbound transactions are candidates for carrier receipt.
24: - Exact batch reference may auto-match.
25: - Amount/date/counterparty without exact reference is suggestion-only.
26: - Many-to-many allocations require amount per link.
27: - Allocation sum cannot exceed transaction amount.
28: - Raw bank file is restricted data with shorter access list.
29: 
30: ## Webhook receiver
31: 
32: - Provider-specific route terminates at adapter.
33: - Verify signature/secret before acceptance.
34: - Store raw body hash, headers needed for verification, received time and provider event key.
35: - Acknowledge quickly after durable enqueue.
36: - Deduplicate and process asynchronously.
37: - Reject replay outside policy where provider timestamp/signature supports it.
38: - Unknown status is stored and mapped later.
39: - Polling reconciles missing/out-of-order events.
40: 
41: ## Domain events
42: 
43: Key events:
44: 
45: - order.created, quote.requested, quote.available, routing.selected.
46: - shipment.create_requested, shipment.created, shipment.outcome_unknown.
47: - shipment.status_changed, exception.opened, exception.resolved.
48: - return.expected, return.received, return.issue_found.
49: - import.promoted, audit.completed, finding.created.
50: - batch.bank_status_changed, case.status_changed, claim.submitted, recovery.recorded.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/06-architecture/ADR.md">
 1: # Architecture Decision Records
 2: 
 3: ## ADR-001 TypeScript monorepo
 4: 
 5: - Status: Accepted.
 6: - Decision: Next.js frontend, NestJS backend and shared TypeScript contracts.
 7: - Reason: AI generation consistency, shared types and easier small-team handover.
 8: 
 9: ## ADR-002 Modular monolith first
10: 
11: - Status: Accepted.
12: - Decision: One deployable backend plus separate workers, with strict domain modules.
13: - Reason: Reduces operational complexity while preserving boundaries.
14: 
15: ## ADR-003 PostgreSQL as system of record
16: 
17: - Status: Accepted.
18: - Reason: Transactions, constraints, financial integrity and reporting.
19: 
20: ## ADR-004 Redis/BullMQ for asynchronous work
21: 
22: - Status: Accepted.
23: - Scope: Provider commands, reconciliation, polling, imports, audit and exports.
24: 
25: ## ADR-005 S3-compatible private object storage
26: 
27: - Status: Accepted.
28: - Scope: Raw files, labels, contract sources and evidence.
29: 
30: ## ADR-006 Carrier adapter boundary
31: 
32: - Status: Accepted.
33: - Decision: Domain/frontend never use provider-specific endpoints or statuses.
34: 
35: ## ADR-007 Immutable event/evidence and audit snapshots
36: 
37: - Status: Accepted.
38: - Decision: Raw tracking/import/evidence and completed audit-run inputs are not overwritten.
39: 
40: ## ADR-008 Web/PWA recipient experience first
41: 
42: - Status: Accepted.
43: - Reason: Lowest recipient friction; native app can reuse APIs if justified.
44: 
45: ## ADR-009 No direct COD custody
46: 
47: - Status: Accepted.
48: - Decision: COD ledger/bank proof only; money movement requires separately approved licensed partner architecture.
49: 
50: ## ADR template
51: 
52: New ADRs state context, considered options, decision, consequences, status and affected IDs.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/06-architecture/BACKEND-ARCHITECTURE.md">
 1: # Backend Architecture
 2: 
 3: ## Stack
 4: 
 5: - NestJS modular monolith initially.
 6: - PostgreSQL with Prisma or an equivalent migration-first ORM selected in ADR.
 7: - Redis and BullMQ for jobs/scheduling.
 8: - S3-compatible object storage for private files/evidence.
 9: - OpenAPI generated from the authoritative contract/code with drift check.
10: 
11: ## Why a modular monolith
12: 
13: - The domain is broad but the initial team is small.
14: - Strong transaction and traceability needs are easier to manage.
15: - Clear module boundaries allow later extraction without premature distributed complexity.
16: 
17: ## Layers
18: 
19: - Domain: entities, value objects, rules and state transitions.
20: - Application: use cases, commands, queries and authorization.
21: - Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, object storage, queues, mail and adapters.
22: - Interface: REST, webhook and worker handlers.
23: 
24: ## Key patterns
25: 
26: ### Outbox/inbox
27: 
28: - Local state change and outgoing event commit together.
29: - Incoming provider events use inbox dedupe.
30: - Workers are at-least-once; handlers are idempotent.
31: 
32: ### External command saga
33: 
34: 1. Validate permission/state.
35: 2. Persist command PENDING and outbox.
36: 3. Worker sends adapter request.
37: 4. Apply SUCCEEDED/REJECTED/OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
38: 5. Unknown starts reconciliation job/work item.
39: 6. Emit state/notification events.
40: 
41: ### Audit run
42: 
43: 1. Validate promoted imports and approved rule coverage.
44: 2. Build immutable input snapshot.
45: 3. Match records.
46: 4. Calculate expected components.
47: 5. Produce processing result plus findings.
48: 6. Aggregate summaries from details.
49: 7. Mark completed; human/system selects official run.
50: 
51: ## Database rules
52: 
53: - All tenant data includes tenant_id.
54: - Composite unique constraints enforce provider/account identities and billing idempotency.
55: - Money is bigint integer VND.
56: - State transitions occur through application services, not arbitrary CRUD.
57: - Raw/evidence/audit tables are immutable.
58: - Optimistic version guards editable aggregates.
59: 
60: ## Background jobs
61: 
62: - Carrier quote fan-out and timeout collection.
63: - External shipment commands/reconciliation.
64: - Tracking polling/backfill.
65: - Exception detection and escalation.
66: - File validation/promotion.
67: - Audit runs.
68: - Claim deadline notifications and authorized submission.
69: - Report/export generation.
70: - Retention/deletion.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/06-architecture/FRONTEND-ARCHITECTURE.md">
 1: # Frontend Architecture
 2: 
 3: ## Stack
 4: 
 5: - Next.js App Router and TypeScript.
 6: - Shared design-system package.
 7: - TanStack Query for server state.
 8: - React Hook Form plus shared Zod schemas for forms.
 9: - TanStack Table for operational data grids.
10: - Role/scope-aware route and action guards.
11: - Playwright for E2E and component/unit tooling selected in the implementation ADR.
12: 
13: ## Structure
14: 
15: \`\`\`text
16: apps/web/
17:   app/
18:   features/
19:     auth/
20:     organization/
21:     carriers/
22:     orders/
23:     quotes/
24:     shipments/
25:     tracking/
26:     exceptions/
27:     returns/
28:     reconciliation/
29:     claims/
30:     reports/
31:     admin/
32:   components/
33:   lib/
34:   styles/
35: \`\`\`
36: 
37: Feature folders own page composition, hooks and view models. Shared business types come from generated OpenAPI/shared contracts, not handwritten duplicates.
38: 
39: ## State rules
40: 
41: - Server state lives in query cache; avoid duplicating in global client stores.
42: - Draft form state is local/persisted explicitly.
43: - Permission and active tenant context are centrally available.
44: - A command disables duplicate submit and displays durable command state.
45: - OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is a first-class blocking state with reconciliation progress.
46: 
47: ## API client
48: 
49: - Generated typed client from OpenAPI where practical.
50: - Adds auth, tenant context, correlation and idempotency headers.
51: - Maps canonical errors to field/global UI content.
52: - Does not silently retry unsafe mutations.
53: 
54: ## Quality gates
55: 
56: - No page with mock-only data in production build.
57: - Every primary button is covered by a test or intentionally disabled with explanation.
58: - All screens implement loading, empty, error, forbidden and success behavior.
59: - Accessibility lint plus keyboard testing for primary journeys.
60: - Visual consistency uses tokens/components; no ad-hoc per-page palette.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/06-architecture/SECURITY-NFR-OBSERVABILITY.md">
 1: # Security, Privacy, NFR and Observability
 2: 
 3: ## Security controls
 4: 
 5: - Password hashing with a current memory-hard algorithm.
 6: - Short-lived access tokens and rotating/revocable sessions.
 7: - MFA/step-up for owners, finance and sensitive operations.
 8: - Backend RBAC and resource scope authorization.
 9: - Tenant isolation enforced in repository/query layer and tested.
10: - Credential values stored only in secret manager/encrypted vault.
11: - TLS in transit and encryption at rest.
12: - Private object storage with short-lived authorized downloads.
13: - File type/size/malware validation.
14: - Webhook authenticity and replay controls where provider supports them.
15: - CSRF/XSS/SQL injection protections and secure headers.
16: - Rate limit auth, OTP, public tracking and webhook routes.
17: - Sensitive data masking in UI/log/export.
18: - Immutable security/audit events.
19: 
20: ## Threat highlights
21: 
22: | Threat | Primary control |
23: |---|---|
24: | Cross-tenant data leak | Tenant-scoped repository, authorization and integration tests |
25: | Token exposure | Secret reference only, log scrubbing, rotation |
26: | Duplicate carrier command | Persistent idempotency and remote reconciliation |
27: | Forged/replayed webhook | Signature/secret, timestamp, inbox dedupe and polling validation |
28: | Malicious upload | Type/size/malware scan and private staging |
29: | Support misuse | Shop consent, time-limited grant and audit |
30: | Claim spam | Policy limits, evidence completeness and idempotency |
31: | Incorrect financial conclusion | Approved version, snapshot, lineage and evidence level |
32: 
33: ## Privacy
34: 
35: - Collect only fields required for fulfillment, evidence or compliance.
36: - PII classification controls view/export permissions.
37: - Recipient tracking exposes the minimum via signed link/OTP.
38: - Retention is configurable and documented; deletion is audited.
39: - Raw source/evidence access is narrower than normalized operational data.
40: 
41: ## NFR targets
42: 
43: Initial targets, to be validated before production:
44: 
45: - Web API p95 under 500 ms excluding external carrier wait.
46: - Quote aggregation presents available partial results within configured budget, default 8 seconds.
47: - User commands acknowledge durably within 2 seconds before async provider work where applicable.
48: - No loss of accepted webhook/import/command records.
49: - Duplicate shipment effects: zero under retry/concurrency test.
50: - 99.5% monthly platform availability target excluding provider incidents, with provider health shown separately.
51: - Audit run baseline capacity: at least 100,000 source plus 100,000 statement rows with measured completion target set after prototype.
52: - RPO 15 minutes and RTO 4 hours initial target; production owner must approve.
53: 
54: ## Observability
55: 
56: Logs:
57: 
58: - Structured JSON, correlation_id, tenant/account hashed identifiers.
59: - No password, OTP, token, full bank data or unmasked recipient PII.
60: 
61: Metrics:
62: 
63: - API latency/error, auth failures.
64: - Carrier latency/error/circuit by capability/account.
65: - Command unknown outcome and reconciliation aging.
66: - Queue depth, retries, dead-letter count.
67: - Webhook verification/dedupe/lag.
68: - Tracking freshness/unmapped codes.
69: - Import and audit duration/errors.
70: - Claim deadline jobs.
71: 
72: Alerts:
73: 
74: - Unknown create outcome aging.
75: - Cross-tenant/security control failure.
76: - Repeated credential failures.
77: - Queue backlog/dead-letter.
78: - Carrier incident threshold.
79: - Audit summary invariant failure.
80: - Backup/restore failure.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/06-architecture/SYSTEM-ARCHITECTURE.md">
 1: # System Architecture
 2: 
 3: ## Context
 4: 
 5: \`\`\`mermaid
 6: flowchart LR
 7:   U[Shop users] --> WEB[Ship Dễ Web/PWA]
 8:   R[Recipient] --> WEB
 9:   WEB --> API[Ship Dễ API]
10:   API --> OMS[Pancake/OMS]
11:   API --> CARRIERS[Carrier adapters]
12:   API --> BANK[Bank file/API]
13:   CARRIERS --> GHN[GHN]
14:   CARRIERS --> GHTK[GHTK]
15:   CARRIERS --> VTP[Viettel Post]
16:   CARRIERS --> JT[J&T Vietnam]
17: \`\`\`
18: 
19: ## Containers
20: 
21: \`\`\`mermaid
22: flowchart TB
23:   WEB[Next.js Web/PWA] --> API[NestJS API]
24:   API --> PG[(PostgreSQL)]
25:   API --> REDIS[(Redis)]
26:   API --> OBJ[(S3-compatible object storage)]
27:   API --> Q[Job queue]
28:   Q --> WORKER[Worker service]
29:   WORKER --> PG
30:   WORKER --> OBJ
31:   WORKER --> ADAPTER[Carrier adapter layer]
32:   API --> ADAPTER
33:   WEBHOOK[Webhook ingress] --> Q
34:   SCHED[Scheduler] --> Q
35: \`\`\`
36: 
37: ## Backend modules
38: 
39: - Identity and tenancy.
40: - Organization/warehouse.
41: - Carrier accounts/capabilities.
42: - Source orders.
43: - Address/serviceability.
44: - Quotes/routing.
45: - Shipments/pickup/labels.
46: - Tracking/events.
47: - Exceptions/returns.
48: - Files/imports.
49: - Rate and policy.
50: - Audit/reconciliation.
51: - Settlement/bank/COD.
52: - Cases/claims.
53: - Notifications/reports/billing.
54: - Admin/audit/support access.
55: 
56: ## Architectural invariants
57: 
58: - Domain code never calls carrier endpoints directly; only adapters do.
59: - External commands are persisted before dispatch.
60: - Async results use correlation/idempotency identifiers.
61: - Raw external data is immutable; normalized state is derived/versioned.
62: - Tenant filtering is applied at repository/query boundary and tested.
63: - Financial calculations run on immutable snapshots.
64: - Read models/dashboard summaries can be rebuilt from authoritative records.
65: 
66: ## Transaction boundaries
67: 
68: - Local command creation and outbox event are one database transaction.
69: - External network call is outside database transaction.
70: - Provider result is applied idempotently in a new transaction.
71: - Bank allocation confirmation locks affected transaction/batch totals.
72: - Official audit-run selection and period close use optimistic/pessimistic controls as appropriate.
73: 
74: ## Availability strategy
75: 
76: - A carrier outage degrades only the affected capability/account.
77: - Quotes return partial results with explicit missing/unknown carriers.
78: - Tracking uses webhook plus polling/backfill.
79: - Manual/file paths remain for settlement and unverified providers.
80: - Circuit breaker, bounded retry and dead-letter recovery are observable.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/07-ai-build/AI-CODING-GUARDRAILS.md">
 1: # AI Coding Guardrails
 2: 
 3: ## Mandatory behavior
 4: 
 5: The coding agent must:
 6: 
 7: 1. Read README and documents in stated order.
 8: 2. Cite requirement IDs in code comments only where they clarify non-obvious rules; keep traceability in tests/PR descriptions.
 9: 3. Implement vertical slices including UI, API, database, permission, errors, audit and tests.
10: 4. Run lint, typecheck, tests and build before declaring a slice complete.
11: 5. Use migrations and seed fixtures; never rely on manual database edits.
12: 6. Preserve all existing passing behavior while extending later slices.
13: 7. Record discovered specification conflicts; do not invent a silent resolution.
14: 
15: ## Prohibited behavior
16: 
17: - Do not remove a feature because it appears complex.
18: - Do not leave a primary action button unconnected.
19: - Do not hardcode user, shop, token, rate, status, fee or production carrier response.
20: - Do not reuse APIs from another J&T country for J&T Vietnam.
21: - Do not treat third-party Viettel/J&T information as official partner contract.
22: - Do not call carrier APIs outside adapters.
23: - Do not retry create/cancel/redelivery/claim blindly.
24: - Do not use float for VND.
25: - Do not merge processing status and findings.
26: - Do not call suspected/verified/accepted money “received” without bank evidence.
27: - Do not permit cross-tenant identifiers supplied by the client to bypass scope.
28: - Do not store credentials or PII in logs.
29: - Do not mark TODO as done; register it as explicit backlog/known limitation.
30: 
31: ## Slice completion response
32: 
33: For each slice, the agent reports:
34: 
35: - Requirements implemented.
36: - Files/migrations created or changed.
37: - Endpoints/screens/jobs added.
38: - Tests and commands run with results.
39: - Assumptions/decisions.
40: - Known limitations/blockers.
41: - Regression impact.
42: 
43: ## Review checkpoints
44: 
45: Stop for human review before:
46: 
47: - Schema change that invalidates prior data.
48: - Authentication/tenant model change.
49: - External command or automatic claim behavior.
50: - Financial formula/rate policy change.
51: - Data retention/delete behavior.
52: - Production carrier credential use.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/07-ai-build/DEFINITION-OF-READY-DONE.md">
 1: # Definition of Ready and Done
 2: 
 3: ## Feature Definition of Ready
 4: 
 5: A feature may enter implementation only when:
 6: 
 7: - Feature/use-case/rule/screen IDs exist.
 8: - Actor and permission are defined.
 9: - Preconditions, inputs, outputs and errors are defined.
10: - State transition is valid.
11: - Entity/API impact is identified.
12: - External capability evidence/fallback is known.
13: - Acceptance and test data exist.
14: - Dependency is complete or explicitly mocked under contract.
15: - No unresolved high-impact business decision remains.
16: 
17: ## Feature Definition of Done
18: 
19: - Frontend and backend are connected.
20: - Database migration and rollback/forward path exist.
21: - Authorization and tenant isolation are enforced/tested.
22: - Loading, empty, error, forbidden and success states exist.
23: - External commands use idempotency/reconciliation.
24: - Audit/history is recorded as specified.
25: - Unit/integration/E2E tests pass.
26: - OpenAPI/schema/docs and traceability are updated.
27: - Lint/typecheck/build pass from clean checkout.
28: - No production hardcode, fake primary action or hidden TODO.
29: - Accessibility and responsive checks are complete for affected screens.
30: - Known residual issue is registered and explicitly accepted.
31: 
32: ## Slice Definition of Done
33: 
34: In addition:
35: 
36: - End-to-end slice journey passes using deterministic mocks.
37: - Regression suite from prior slices passes.
38: - Seed/demo data works.
39: - Observability is present for async/external behavior.
40: - Human review checkpoint completed for sensitive changes.
41: 
42: ## Release Definition of Done
43: 
44: - All CORE features targeted for the release satisfy DoD.
45: - No critical/high security defect.
46: - No known duplicate-command or financial invariant failure.
47: - Backup/restore and rollback rehearsed.
48: - Production carrier capabilities have partner evidence.
49: - UAT sign-off and operational runbooks complete.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/07-ai-build/TECH-STACK-REPOSITORY.md">
 1: # Technology Stack and Repository
 2: 
 3: ## Default stack
 4: 
 5: - Runtime baseline: Node.js 24 locally, in CI and in build images.
 6: - Package manager: pnpm 11, exact version pinned in `packageManager` with explicit dependency build-script approvals.
 7: - Monorepo: Turborepo as a project dependency.
 8: - Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript.
 9: - Backend: NestJS, TypeScript.
10: - Database: PostgreSQL 16+.
11: - ORM/migrations: Prisma unless ADR changes it before implementation.
12: - Queue/cache: Redis and BullMQ.
13: - Object storage: S3-compatible; MinIO is the default local container.
14: - Validation: Zod for shared/client schemas; backend DTO/domain validation remains authoritative.
15: - API: REST/OpenAPI with validated generation of frontend TypeScript contracts.
16: - Testing: Vitest unit tests, Supertest API integration and Playwright browser E2E/visual tests.
17: - UI evidence: Storybook, MSW, axe-based accessibility and targeted Lighthouse CI budgets.
18: - Security baseline: Gitleaks plus package-manager dependency audit and reviewed build-script allowlists.
19: - Local orchestration: Docker Desktop/Compose; native PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO installs are not required.
20: 
21: ## Target code repository
22: 
23: ```text
24: apps/
25:   web/
26:   api/
27:   worker/
28: packages/
29:   ui/
30:   contracts/
31:   config/
32:   testkit/
33: infra/
34:   docker/
35:   migrations/
36: docs/
37: scripts/
38: ```
39: 
40: ## Required root commands
41: 
42: - `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
43: - `pnpm lint`
44: - `pnpm format:check`
45: - `pnpm typecheck`
46: - `pnpm test`
47: - `pnpm test:integration`
48: - `pnpm test:e2e`
49: - `pnpm test:a11y`
50: - `pnpm test:visual`
51: - `pnpm test:perf`
52: - `pnpm security:secrets`
53: - `pnpm build`
54: - `pnpm dev`
55: - `pnpm db:migrate`
56: - `pnpm db:seed`
57: - `pnpm mock:carriers`
58: 
59: Commands that do not apply to a package are routed from the root; agents must not bypass them by invoking a different global CLI.
60: 
61: ## Environment principles
62: 
63: - `.env.example` documents names and safe placeholders only.
64: - Secrets never enter source control, request logs or test snapshots.
65: - Local, test, staging and production configurations are explicit.
66: - Carrier adapters default to mock/disabled until credentials and capability evidence exist.
67: - Docker images and JavaScript package versions are pinned by reviewed files.
68: - Dependency lifecycle scripts are denied unless explicitly reviewed and allowlisted.
69: - Newly released dependencies are not adopted during an active Work Item.
70: 
71: ## Code boundaries
72: 
73: - Feature/domain modules cannot import provider-specific adapter internals.
74: - UI consumes generated/shared contracts, not duplicate hand-written shapes.
75: - State transitions live in domain/application services.
76: - Database access is tenant-scoped through approved repositories.
77: - Unsafe external commands go through command/outbox workflow.
78: - MSW and carrier mocks provide test evidence only and cannot be enabled in production.
79: - Storybook, screenshots and Lighthouse scores do not replace functional acceptance evidence.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/07-ai-build/VERTICAL-SLICE-PLAN.md">
  1: # AI Vertical-Slice Build Plan
  2: 
  3: The AI builds the entire target product, but in dependency-ordered vertical slices. “Later” means execution order only, not product exclusion.
  4: 
  5: ## Slice 0 — Repository and quality foundation
  6: 
  7: Deliver:
  8: 
  9: - Monorepo, apps/packages, Docker Compose.
 10: - CI commands, lint/typecheck/test/build.
 11: - PostgreSQL/Redis/object-store local services.
 12: - OpenAPI/schema validation.
 13: - Health/readiness and structured logging.
 14: 
 15: Exit: clean install and all root commands run.
 16: 
 17: ## Slice 1 — Identity, tenancy and organization
 18: 
 19: Deliver:
 20: 
 21: - Register/login/verify/recovery/MFA/session.
 22: - Tenant/shop/branch/warehouse.
 23: - Invitations, roles/scopes and profile.
 24: - Onboarding shell and audit events.
 25: - Screens/API/migrations/tests.
 26: 
 27: Exit: owner creates shop/warehouse and invited operator logs in with correct scope.
 28: 
 29: ## Slice 2 — Carrier accounts and adapter framework
 30: 
 31: Deliver:
 32: 
 33: - Carrier account connection, encrypted secret reference, test and health.
 34: - Capability registry/evidence.
 35: - Canonical adapter interface and mock server.
 36: - GHN/GHTK initial official adapters behind environment flags.
 37: - Viettel/J&T confirmation-required stubs/manual fallback.
 38: 
 39: Exit: capability UI accurately distinguishes supported, unsupported and unknown.
 40: 
 41: ## Slice 3 — Orders, address and shipping options
 42: 
 43: Deliver:
 44: 
 45: - Manual/file source orders and parcels.
 46: - Address normalization/mapping.
 47: - Serviceability fan-out.
 48: - Live quote normalization/snapshot.
 49: - Compare/recommend/auto-routing with explanation.
 50: - No-carrier and partial-outage UX.
 51: 
 52: Exit: AC-AVL, AC-QTE and AC-SEL journeys pass with mocks and verified sandboxes where available.
 53: 
 54: ## Slice 4 — Shipment, label and pickup
 55: 
 56: Deliver:
 57: 
 58: - Create command saga/idempotency/reconciliation.
 59: - Shipment detail, update/cancel/switch.
 60: - Label and print flows.
 61: - Pickup request/handover.
 62: - OMS waybill sync adapter shell.
 63: 
 64: Exit: timeout test proves no duplicate waybill; old label invalidates on switch.
 65: 
 66: ## Slice 5 — Tracking, recipient and exceptions
 67: 
 68: Deliver:
 69: 
 70: - Webhook/polling/inbox ledger and mappings.
 71: - Timeline/current state/freshness.
 72: - Recipient signed-link/OTP view.
 73: - Exception detector/workbox/tasks.
 74: - Redelivery command/manual fallback.
 75: 
 76: Exit: duplicate/out-of-order webhook tests pass and unknown status is preserved.
 77: 
 78: ## Slice 6 — Returns
 79: 
 80: Deliver:
 81: 
 82: - Expected-return queue.
 83: - Scan/duplicate check.
 84: - Condition checklist and direct evidence.
 85: - Chain of custody and issue case.
 86: 
 87: Exit: warehouse can complete scan-to-case flow without admin intervention.
 88: 
 89: ## Slice 7 — Rate, policy and data imports
 90: 
 91: Deliver:
 92: 
 93: - Contract source/private files.
 94: - Structured rate/settlement/claim policies.
 95: - Maker-checker, effective versions and simulator.
 96: - Import staging/validation/revision/lineage.
 97: 
 98: Exit: approved rate calculation reproduces golden examples and invalid imports never enter snapshot.
 99: 
100: ## Slice 8 — Audit and missing settlement
101: 
102: Deliver:
103: 
104: - Audit periods/runs/snapshots.
105: - Exact matching/manual queue.
106: - Component calculation and multiple findings.
107: - Six missing states and account-level threshold/carry.
108: - Results/explanation/dashboard.
109: 
110: Exit: deterministic golden audit and invariant totals pass.
111: 
112: ## Slice 9 — Batch, bank and COD
113: 
114: Deliver:
115: 
116: - Settlement batches/control totals.
117: - Dual status dimensions.
118: - Bank import/matching/suggestion/allocation.
119: - COD ledger and receipt evidence.
120: - Period close/reopen/adjustment.
121: 
122: Exit: many-to-many allocations and short/over/full tests pass.
123: 
124: ## Slice 10 — Cases and claims
125: 
126: Deliver:
127: 
128: - Case state machine, four money levels and carry-forward.
129: - Deadline policy/evidence checklist/package.
130: - Confirm-first claim submission.
131: - Policy-authorized auto-submit framework disabled until carrier capability confirmed.
132: - Response/outcome/recovery.
133: 
134: Exit: no expired/incomplete claim auto-submits; recovered value requires proof.
135: 
136: ## Slice 11 — Reports, billing and administration
137: 
138: Deliver:
139: 
140: - Role dashboards/reports/export.
141: - Billable-event ledger and usage statement.
142: - Notification/escalation.
143: - Admin mapping, jobs, queue and support access.
144: - Retention/export/delete workflows.
145: 
146: Exit: traceability and all primary E2E tests pass.
147: 
148: ## Slice 12 — Hardening and production readiness
149: 
150: - Security/performance/accessibility tests.
151: - Restore drill.
152: - Provider sandbox contract tests.
153: - Observability/incident runbooks.
154: - Remove unapproved mocks from production config.
155: - Human developer review and technical-debt triage.

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/08-testing/TEST-DATA-MOCKS.md">
 1: # Test Data and Carrier Mocks
 2: 
 3: ## Golden datasets
 4: 
 5: Create deterministic, anonymized fixtures:
 6: 
 7: - Auth/users/roles with positive and denied scopes.
 8: - Addresses: exact, ambiguous, unsupported and carrier-code mismatch.
 9: - Quotes: supported, explicit rejection, timeout, partial fees and expired.
10: - Create: success, business rejection, timeout-found, timeout-not-found and duplicate client key.
11: - Tracking: duplicate, out-of-order, unknown status and missing webhook.
12: - Return: valid, duplicate, wrong tenant/warehouse and damaged.
13: - Rates: zone/weight boundaries, volumetric, VAT, rounding, insurance, return and surcharge.
14: - Statements: clean, COD mismatch, fee mismatch, weight candidate, duplicate deduction, source-only and carrier-only.
15: - Bank: exact reference, suggested, one-to-many, many-to-one, short and over.
16: - Claims: complete, missing evidence, expired, partial accepted and installment recovery.
17: 
18: ## Mock carrier server
19: 
20: One canonical mock controller supports configurable scenarios per carrier/account:
21: 
22: - latency_ms and timeout.
23: - status code/error body.
24: - serviceability outcome.
25: - quote services/components/expiry.
26: - create durable effect before timeout.
27: - lookup by client reference.
28: - state-constrained update/cancel/redelivery.
29: - label bytes/reference.
30: - webhook emission, duplication and reordering.
31: - rate limiting and auth failure.
32: 
33: Mocks live only in local/test. Production configuration fails closed if a mock adapter is selected.
34: 
35: ## Data safety
36: 
37: - No production credential, phone, address, bank account or contract file.
38: - Synthetic test data is obvious and namespaced.
39: - UAT real data is minimized, separately controlled and never committed.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/08-testing/TEST-STRATEGY.md">
 1: # Test Strategy
 2: 
 3: ## Test levels
 4: 
 5: | Level | Purpose |
 6: |---|---|
 7: | Unit | Rules, calculations, value objects and state transitions |
 8: | Property/invariant | Allocation, totals, idempotency and money-level invariants |
 9: | API integration | Database, authorization, migration and endpoint contracts |
10: | Carrier contract | Adapter mapping against mock/sandbox evidence |
11: | Worker/event | Queue retry, inbox/outbox, dedupe and dead-letter |
12: | Component | Forms, tables, permission and states |
13: | E2E | User journey across frontend/backend |
14: | Security | Tenant isolation, auth, secret/PII and webhook |
15: | Performance | Quote fan-out, tables/imports/audit/jobs |
16: | UAT | Business acceptance with shop/operator examples |
17: 
18: ## Mandatory invariants
19: 
20: - Same create idempotency key never causes two carrier effects.
21: - UNKNOWN outcome never becomes safe retry without reconciliation.
22: - A user cannot access another tenant by changing an ID.
23: - Sum of bank allocation from a transaction does not exceed transaction amount.
24: - Summary totals equal detail aggregation.
25: - Four evidence money levels are not automatically summed.
26: - Missing optional data cannot turn into confirmed carrier error.
27: - Approved rate version is immutable.
28: - Raw event/import/evidence is not overwritten.
29: - Rerun does not duplicate case/billing without explicit new finding semantics.
30: 
31: ## Test ownership
32: 
33: - AI agent writes and runs tests with each slice.
34: - Human dev reviews test quality and adds provider/production edge cases.
35: - Product/BA owns golden business examples and UAT expected outcomes.
36: - Security owner reviews auth/tenant/secrets before production.
37: 
38: ## CI gates
39: 
40: - Format/lint.
41: - Typecheck.
42: - Unit/property.
43: - API integration with ephemeral database.
44: - Contract/schema validation.
45: - Build.
46: - E2E smoke.
47: - Dependency/secret scan.
</file>

48: ## Story template

61: 
62: - No story is “backend only” when a user-facing end-to-end slice is expected; split technical tasks under one deliverable story.
