<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/09-delivery/CI-CD-DEPLOYMENT.md">
 1: # CI/CD and Deployment
 2: 
 3: ## Environments
 4: 
 5: - Local: deterministic mock carriers and seeded data.
 6: - Test: ephemeral database per CI suite where practical.
 7: - Staging: production-like infrastructure, sandbox carrier accounts and anonymized fixtures.
 8: - Production: real credentials, mocks disabled, restricted admin access.
 9: 
10: ## Pull-request pipeline
11: 
12: 1. Install with lockfile.
13: 2. Format/lint.
14: 3. Typecheck.
15: 4. Unit/property tests.
16: 5. JSON Schema/OpenAPI/document validation.
17: 6. Database migration on clean and previous-version fixture.
18: 7. API integration tests.
19: 8. Build web/api/worker.
20: 9. E2E smoke using mock carriers.
21: 10. Secret/dependency/security scan.
22: 
23: ## Deployment
24: 
25: 1. Verify artifact/image provenance.
26: 2. Back up or verify recovery point.
27: 3. Run forward-compatible migration.
28: 4. Deploy backend/workers, then frontend as compatible.
29: 5. Run health/readiness and smoke.
30: 6. Verify queue/webhook/provider health.
31: 7. Monitor error/latency/unknown command metrics.
32: 
33: ## Rollback
34: 
35: - Prefer application rollback with backward-compatible schema.
36: - Destructive migrations require expand-migrate-contract across releases.
37: - Feature flags disable new external actions independently.
38: - Unknown commands are reconciled before any replay.
39: - Rollback does not delete audit/evidence records.
40: 
41: ## Production readiness
42: 
43: - UAT and security sign-off.
44: - Carrier partner/sandbox evidence.
45: - No production mock adapter.
46: - Restore drill.
47: - Alert routing and on-call owner.
48: - Runbooks reviewed.
49: - Data retention and support access configured.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/09-delivery/DEVELOPER-HANDOVER.md">
 1: # Developer Handover
 2: 
 3: ## Handover objective
 4: 
 5: The human developer receives a runnable, tested AI-generated product and focuses on review, provider reality, security, performance and production hardening—not rediscovering business requirements.
 6: 
 7: ## Required handover bundle
 8: 
 9: - Clean repository and tagged baseline.
10: - README and one-command local setup.
11: - Environment variable catalog with no secrets.
12: - Migrations and seed data.
13: - OpenAPI and generated API client.
14: - Mock carrier server/scenario catalog.
15: - Test command results and coverage summary.
16: - Architecture/ADR and module map.
17: - Carrier capability evidence and sandbox results.
18: - Known limitations and technical-debt register.
19: - Deployment/rollback and operations runbooks.
20: 
21: ## Developer review checklist
22: 
23: ### Architecture/code
24: 
25: - Module boundaries and dependency direction.
26: - Transaction/outbox/inbox correctness.
27: - Database indexes/constraints and migration safety.
28: - Async retry/dead-letter behavior.
29: - Error and logging consistency.
30: 
31: ### Security
32: 
33: - Auth/session/MFA.
34: - Tenant/resource authorization.
35: - Secret/PII/file access.
36: - Webhook verification.
37: - Injection/XSS/CSRF and rate limiting.
38: 
39: ### Carrier integrations
40: 
41: - Current official/partner contracts.
42: - Permission and status constraints.
43: - Timeout/idempotency/client-reference behavior.
44: - Error mapping and raw evidence sanitization.
45: - Sandbox/production differences.
46: 
47: ### Financial correctness
48: 
49: - Integer money and rounding.
50: - Approved effective rules.
51: - Detail/summary invariants.
52: - Processing status versus findings.
53: - Batch allocation and four money evidence levels.
54: 
55: ### Production
56: 
57: - Performance/load.
58: - Backup/restore.
59: - Metrics/alerts.
60: - Feature flags and rollback.
61: - Support access and retention.
62: 
63: ## Completion record
64: 
65: For each reviewed module record:
66: 
67: - Reviewer/date/commit.
68: - Issues found and severity.
69: - Fix/acceptance decision.
70: - Tests added.
71: - Residual risk/owner.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/09-delivery/OPERATIONS-RUNBOOK.md">
 1: # Operations Runbook
 2: 
 3: ## Carrier outage
 4: 
 5: 1. Confirm affected carrier/account/capability.
 6: 2. Open circuit for failing capability.
 7: 3. Preserve partial results and mark UNKNOWN_ERROR.
 8: 4. Notify affected operators with manual fallback.
 9: 5. Do not disable healthy carriers.
10: 6. Reprobe in half-open mode and close incident with timeline.
11: 
12: ## Shipment create outcome unknown
13: 
14: 1. Freeze further create attempts for source order/account.
15: 2. Query by client reference/approved lookup.
16: 3. Poll within bounded reconciliation window.
17: 4. If found, link waybill and mark command succeeded.
18: 5. If proven not found, permit retry with same lineage under policy.
19: 6. If still unknown, create manual work item; never blind retry.
20: 
21: ## Duplicate waybill suspected
22: 
23: 1. Stop label/pickup.
24: 2. Compare command/idempotency and remote references.
25: 3. Identify operationally valid waybill.
26: 4. Cancel duplicate only if carrier state/capability safely allows.
27: 5. Invalidate label and audit correction.
28: 6. Add regression fixture/root-cause action.
29: 
30: ## Webhook backlog
31: 
32: 1. Check queue depth, oldest age and verification failures.
33: 2. Scale/fix workers without clearing durable messages.
34: 3. Deduplicate/replay idempotently.
35: 4. Run tracking polling reconciliation.
36: 5. Report affected freshness window.
37: 
38: ## Import blocked
39: 
40: 1. Review blocking header/key/control errors.
41: 2. Download row issue report.
42: 3. Correct source/mapping and upload new revision.
43: 4. Promote only after validation.
44: 5. Never edit promoted raw rows.
45: 
46: ## Audit invariant failure
47: 
48: 1. Mark run failed/non-official.
49: 2. Preserve snapshot/log.
50: 3. Compare detail and summary/rule version.
51: 4. Fix code/rule through approved change.
52: 5. Rerun as new run; never overwrite.
53: 
54: ## Bank allocation correction
55: 
56: 1. Lock affected transaction/batches.
57: 2. Reverse/correct allocations with reason and approver.
58: 3. Recompute independent batch bank statuses.
59: 4. Update received/recovery evidence without rewriting case history.
60: 
61: ## Security/privacy incident
62: 
63: 1. Contain access/token and preserve evidence.
64: 2. Identify tenant/data scope.
65: 3. Rotate affected secrets.
66: 4. Follow notification/legal policy.
67: 5. Correct, test and document root cause.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/09-delivery/RISKS-OPEN-ISSUES.md">
 1: # Risks and Open Issues
 2: 
 3: ## Current open issues
 4: 
 5: | ID | Issue | Status | Required action |
 6: |---|---|---|---|
 7: | OI-001 | Viettel Post current partner API contract not publicly verified | Confirmation required | Obtain official partner docs/sandbox |
 8: | OI-002 | J&T Vietnam current partner API contract not publicly verified | Confirmation required | Obtain official Vietnam partner docs/sandbox |
 9: | OI-003 | Pancake API scopes/endpoints not included in current source pack | Confirmation required | Obtain official/partner contract |
10: | OI-004 | Exact claim deadlines by category/carrier may change | Legal/business verification | Source effective policies before enabling automation |
11: | OI-005 | Automatic claim submission support varies by carrier | Conditional | Confirm capability and shop authorization |
12: | OI-006 | Full-product KPI target values are not numerically set | Product decision | Set before pilot |
13: | OI-007 | Final production pricing after pilot | Product decision | Validate usage/WTP; initial per-audited-waybill retained |
14: | OI-008 | RPO/RTO and capacity targets need cost approval | Technical/product decision | Benchmark prototype and approve |
15: 
16: ## Major risks
17: 
18: | Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
19: |---|---|---|
20: | AI invents carrier API | Broken/unsafe integration | Capability evidence, adapter stubs, contract tests |
21: | Duplicate external command | Duplicate shipment/claim | Persistent idempotency and reconciliation |
22: | Wrong address mapping | Wrong route/price | Versioned mapping and user confirmation |
23: | Quote differs from final charge | Trust loss | Store quote + contract + statement evidence layers |
24: | False audit positive | Trust loss | Approved rule, conservative result and golden tests |
25: | Credential trust barrier | Adoption | File/read-only first, least privilege and transparent audit |
26: | Multi-carrier maintenance | Ongoing outages | Isolation, capability registry, observability and fallback |
27: | PII/financial leak | Severe | Tenant isolation, masking, private storage and access audit |
28: | One-shot AI code dump | Inconsistent product | Vertical slices, DoD and regression gates |
29: 
30: ## Resolution rule
31: 
32: No open issue may be silently replaced by an implementation assumption. High-impact items block production capability, not the whole codebase: build the interface, mock and fallback while the capability remains disabled.
</file>

184: 
185: `verifiedAt` is the UTC inspection day marker, not a tool execution timestamp.
186: All lifecycle claims remain DECLARED. UNAVAILABLE describes execution availability,
187: not a sixth lifecycle state. `registrationPending: true` and `toolId: null`
188: are explicitly incomplete contract records: the shared manifest has no entry.
189: They are not valid complete attachment evidence and cannot be promoted until a
190: separately scoped item registers the tool. Existing IDs/references reuse item 1.
191: Caller files prove repository code exists, not that the upstream package ran.
192: Requested versions are copied from the Work Item; unresolved versions were not
193: observed on a host. No live provider, credentials or login is needed by CI.
194: 
195: ## Caller, triggers and boundaries
196: 
197: Goal run dispatch uses `tools/ai-brain/orchestrate.js`; chat uses
198: `tools/ai-brain/hermes-session.js`. Reuse `tools/ai-brain/sources.js` for
199: source identity and `tools/ai-brain/route-probe.js` plus
200: `tools/ai-brain/route-health.js` for gateway failure/quota feedback.
201: Work Item + Controller candidate + worktree + permissions + timeout enter
202: `tools/ai-brain/executor.js`; logs/artifacts/exit status return to Controller.
203: Hermes must not select source/model/account or run a parallel dispatcher.
204: Gateway fallback and Controller fallback require one owner, never overlapping retries.
205: Paseo manages sessions, not scheduling. Harness qualification belongs to Controller;
206: a package name alone grants no role.
207: 
208: `tools/ai-brain/facts.js` is a local facts reader, not proof of a connected
209: shipde-brain repository. External memory requires task-scoped reads and writes
210: with commit/source provenance and recheck conditions; storing a file is insufficient.
211: Claude authority follows the current operator contract, not an older appendix role label.
212: The manifest uses anthropic-ai/claude-code; the appendix's anthropics spelling
213: is an alias, not a second installation.
214: 
215: ## Task and missing execution evidence
216: 
217: Required real acceptance: chat -> execution -> independent review -> response,
218: with candidate identity, decision log, launch result, run/session ID and exact SHA.
219: No such live task was run by this documentation item. Decision/launch artifacts
220: are NOT_RUN, review and acceptance PENDING; local adapter checks do not establish
221: live Hermes recall, gateway availability or a completed review.
222: 9router credentials for multiple providers remain unverified; never inspect or
223: print credentials to fill this gap. The requested 68e8b862 baseline is historical,
224: not the checked-out baseline. Reproduce offline with the verification command below.
225: 
226: ## Verification and handoff
227: 
228: Baseline inspected: `88933580ab502132a24ca18573db4e1efba69688`.
229: SHA: pending Claude commit. Changes remain uncommitted; CI and independent review
230: are pending. No EXECUTION_VERIFIED or ACCEPTED claim.

233: - `python docs/product-spec/scripts/validate_docs.py`

235: - PR contract deferred to Claude after commit per operator update 17/10.

238: The referenced appendix is available in the operator's hermes-live handoff but is
239: absent from this baseline. It is not copied outside the permitted item paths.

48: Compare Nox per security scope with current Gitleaks, Trivy, Semgrep and agent-scan gates on benign and violating fixtures; report findings, false positives, unavailable/error behavior, exit codes and coverage. Do not remove scanners before coverage parity. No default replacement or installation. All entries remain DECLARED.
49: 
50: ## Verification and limitations
51: 
52: Task/artifact: inspect repository declarations, run `node --test tools/ai-brain/test/repo-integration-group-9.test.js tools/ai-brain/test/repo-integration-evidence.test.js` and `python docs/product-spec/scripts/validate_docs.py`. Tests check evidence structure, not live tool availability.
53: 
54: SHA: pending Claude commit. No EXECUTION_VERIFIED or ACCEPTED claim. CI and independent review pending.
55: 
56: Local verification on 2026-10-17: group test plus shared evidence test passed 10/10 (zero failures); documentation validation passed with 193 markdown files, 130 feature IDs, 251 delivery rows and 1210 unique identifiers. PR contract deferred to Claude after commit, as requested.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/CLAUDE-START-PROMPT.md">
 1: # Claude Start Prompt
 2: 
 3: Use one new Claude Code CLI session per Work Item after opening `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-claude` (or the designated author worktree). Authenticate via native machine login (`claude auth login`). Replace all placeholders.
 4: 
 5: ```text
 6: Implement exactly one Ship Dễ Work Item: <WORK_ITEM_ID> on the Codex-prepared branch <BRANCH>.
 7: 
 8: Mandatory operating contract:
 9: 1. Read root AGENTS.md completely.
10: 2. Read SEMI-MANUAL-AI-WORKFLOW.md, the matching register row and the complete Work Item.
11: 3. Confirm Assigned author is CLAUDE (or GEMINI/collaborative repair), dependencies are merged, the branch is correct and the worktree is clean.
12: 4. Follow source precedence. Existing prototype code is evidence, not proof of completion.
13: 5. Plan the technical implementation before editing and map every acceptance row to code and evidence.
14: 6. If a material rule, acceptance condition or dependency is missing, mark BLOCKED with evidence and stop; do not invent behavior.
15: 7. Implement only this Work Item as a complete vertical feature: UI, backend, persistence, authorization, error/recovery states, audit, contracts and tests where applicable.
16: 8. Do not add another feature, broad cleanup or unrelated refactor.
17: 9. Run every required validation command. Never report a command as passed unless it actually ran successfully.
18: 10. Update the Work Item, register and traceability with implementation evidence. Fill every PR template section.
19: 11. Commit, push and open one Pull Request titled `[<WORK_ITEM_ID>] <business outcome>`.
20: 12. Set the item to READY_FOR_CODEX and stop. Do not merge or start another Work Item.
21: 
22: Final response:
23: - Work Item and branch
24: - Pull Request URL
25: - implemented requirement IDs
26: - commands actually run and exact results
27: - evidence locations
28: - assumptions, limitations or blockers
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Review-fix prompt
32: 
33: ```text
34: Read all current Codex/review findings on <PR_URL>. Fix every actionable finding for <WORK_ITEM_ID> on the existing branch only. Do not dismiss a finding without code/test evidence or a human-approved specification decision. Rerun the complete verification set, update PR evidence, push, set READY_FOR_CODEX and stop.
35: ```
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/CODEX-REVIEW-PROMPT.md">
 1: # Codex Feature Review Prompt
 2: 
 3: Use this only for manual recovery or an app-based review after the Pull Request is open. Normal operation waits for green CI and runs `codex review --base origin/main` through `control.ps1`; the repository review rules below remain authoritative. Codex is reviewer-only during either path.
 4: 
 5: ```text
 6: Independently review Ship Dễ Pull Request <PR_URL> for exactly <WORK_ITEM_ID>. Do not modify code and do not merge.
 7: 
 8: Review procedure:
 9: 1. Read the repository root AGENTS.md completely and apply its Code Review Rules.
10: 2. Read the Work Item, its FEATURE-DELIVERY-REGISTER row, source requirement documents, contracts and acceptance scenarios.
11: 3. Inspect the entire PR diff and enough surrounding code to trace each changed user action from UI through API/application logic, persistence, external adapter and audit behavior.
12: 4. Verify this PR contains only one Work Item and does not hide unrelated changes.
13: 5. Check each acceptance row individually, including failure, permission, tenant, duplicate, timeout, recovery, loading, empty and accessibility states where applicable.
14: 6. Check migrations, compatibility, idempotency, carrier evidence, money invariants, sensitive data and observability.
15: 7. Run or independently inspect the required lint, typecheck, unit, integration, E2E and build evidence. A test that never exercises the changed behavior is not evidence.
16: 8. Compare implementation against the full Definition of Done. Existing demo UI or a success toast is not sufficient.
17: 9. Post actionable findings on the Pull Request with file/line, violated requirement and expected safe behavior.
18: 10. Return exactly one verdict: PASS, CHANGES_REQUIRED or BLOCKED. Do not return PASS with an unresolved acceptance gap.
19: 
20: Required review report:
21: - PR, Work Item, reviewed commit SHA
22: - scope-integrity result
23: - requirement/acceptance matrix: ID | result | evidence | finding
24: - commands/tests independently verified
25: - findings ordered by P0/P1/P2/P3
26: - regression and residual-risk assessment
27: - final verdict
28: 
29: PASS requires: all acceptance rows pass, CI evidence is valid, no unresolved consequential finding exists, and the implementation is a real vertical feature rather than a mock or UI-only path.
30: ```
31: 
32: For the human-gated semi-automatic handoff, the controller detaches the dedicated Codex worktree at the immutable PR head, starts a fresh non-interactive review and saves the report outside Git. The human confirms before posting it and remains the only merge owner. This manual prompt is the recovery path and never weakens the requirement-by-requirement acceptance review.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/FOUNDATION-WORK-ITEMS.md">
 1: # Foundation Work Items
 2: 
 3: Product feature work is blocked until these items are merged in order. Each item gets its own assigned implementation author branch, Pull Request and Codex review.
 4: 
 5: ## Current repository finding
 6: 
 7: As verified on 2026-08-24, the product repository is a single Next.js 16.1.6 application using React 19.2.3, Prisma 6.19.2 and `package-lock.json`. The target specification defines a pnpm/Turborepo workspace with separate web, API and worker boundaries. Existing UI and behavior are retained as prototype/reference material, but mock arrays and client-side mutations do not count as completed product features.
 8: 
 9: Machine-wide CLI preparation is defined in `REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md`. Framework and test repositories below are installed as lockfile-pinned project dependencies in their assigned item, never globally and never by cloning upstream source.
10: 
11: ## TASK-FOUND-01 — Freeze and classify the prototype
12: 
13: **Outcome:** a clean, reproducible baseline before structural migration.
14: 
15: - Inventory routes, components, server code, Prisma schema, adapters, fixtures and tests.
16: - Map existing behavior to feature IDs as `REAL`, `PARTIAL`, `DEMO_ONLY` or `ABSENT`, with file evidence.
17: - Add smoke tests for critical visible flows so later migration cannot silently remove them.
18: - Repair the verification baseline, including the declared-but-missing ESLint dependency/configuration, without weakening lint rules.
19: - Add a deterministic formatting baseline and Gitleaks secret scan; failures may not be hidden with blanket exclusions.
20: - Align local documentation, package engines and GitHub Actions on Node.js 24 so the existing Windows runtime and CI do not validate different majors.
21: - Confirm clean `npm ci`, lint, build and current E2E commands.
22: - Record current security, data and hardcode gaps; do not fix unrelated features in this PR.
23: 
24: **Exit:** Codex confirms the inventory is evidence-based, the baseline checks are reproducible and behavior-loss/secret fixtures are detected.
25: 
26: ## TASK-FOUND-02 — Migrate repository structure without feature rewrite
27: 
28: **Outcome:** target monorepo skeleton while preserving the baseline UI.
29: 
30: - Introduce pnpm major 11 and Turborepo as project tooling, with an exact `packageManager` value, committed lockfile and explicit build-script allowlist.
31: - Move the existing Next.js application to `apps/web` with behavior-preservation tests passing.
32: - Create shared `packages/contracts`, `packages/config`, `packages/testkit` and `packages/ui` boundaries without speculative abstraction.
33: - Provide compatibility commands and update CI/documentation atomically.
34: - Do not implement product feature behavior in this structural PR.
35: 
36: **Exit:** clean install/lint/typecheck/test/build succeeds through root `pnpm` commands and the preserved flows remain usable.
37: 
38: ## TASK-FOUND-03 — Add API, worker and local infrastructure
39: 
40: **Outcome:** executable backend foundation for real vertical features.
41: 
42: - Scaffold NestJS `apps/api` and `apps/worker` with health/readiness endpoints.
43: - Add PostgreSQL 16+, Redis and S3-compatible local services through Docker Compose using pinned image versions or digests.
44: - Establish Prisma migration ownership, BullMQ queue/outbox boundary, structured logs and correlation IDs.
45: - Add `.env.example` with safe placeholders and mock carrier defaults.
46: - No production credential or live carrier command is permitted.
47: - Do not require native PostgreSQL, Redis, MinIO or Ubuntu installation on the Windows machine.
48: 
49: **Exit:** API, worker and dependencies start locally; health, migration and queue smoke tests pass from documented root commands.
50: 
51: ## TASK-FOUND-04 — Establish contracts and quality gates
52: 
53: **Outcome:** every later feature is testable and reviewable in the same way.
54: 
55: - Wire OpenAPI validation, `openapi-typescript` generation and shared contract drift checks.
56: - Provide Vitest unit, Supertest API integration and Playwright E2E harnesses plus deterministic carrier mocks.
57: - Add MSW handlers and `msw-storybook-addon` for approved loading, empty, error, partial, success and recovery states.
58: - Add Storybook state/interaction coverage, Playwright screenshot comparison and axe-based accessibility checks for approved UI.
59: - Add targeted Lighthouse CI budgets for the approved critical routes without running the full set on every local edit.
60: - Audit and pin only Vercel `react-best-practices` and `web-design-guidelines`; record the exact source commit and keep Ship Dễ screen/UX documents authoritative.
61: - Make root commands from the target stack document executable.
62: - Enable PR contract validation, secret scan, lint, typecheck, tests and build in CI.
63: - Add seed reset and isolated test database procedures.
64: 
65: **Exit:** deliberately broken contract, secret, accessibility, critical screenshot and test fixtures fail the correct CI gate, while all approved baseline checks pass.
66: 
67: ## Promotion rule
68: 
69: After `TASK-FOUND-04` is `MERGED`, promote only the first dependency-ready feature rows in `FEATURE-DELIVERY-REGISTER.csv` from `BLOCKED_BY_FOUNDATION` to `READY_FOR_AUTHOR`. Do not bulk-mark all 130 features ready.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/REPO-INTEGRATION-EVIDENCE.md">
  1: # Ship Dễ — Repository Integration Evidence Contract
  2: 
  3: ## Purpose
  4: 
  5: This contract defines the five-state integration lifecycle every external repository, tool or
  6: dependency moves through, and the evidence a Work Item must carry at each step. It exists so that
  7: no tool is reported as "attached" to Ship Dễ without a verifiable pointer on disk: a real file in
  8: this repository that proves the claim. A declaration in a planning document is not an installation,
  9: and an installation is not a wired command, and a wired command is not a verified execution.
 10: 
 11: `tools/ai-brain/data/tool-manifest.json` is the machine-readable inventory that this contract
 12: governs; `REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md` owns the human-readable install policy for the same tools.
 13: 
 14: ## The five states
 15: 
 16: ```
 17: DECLARED --> INSTALLED --> WIRED --> EXECUTION_VERIFIED --> ACCEPTED
 18: ```
 19: 
 20: The ladder is strictly monotonic. A tool may not skip a rung, and a tool may not be reported at a
 21: rung it has not proved.
 22: 
 23: ### 1. `DECLARED`
 24: 
 25: - Definition: the tool or repository is formally adopted in the specification layer
 26:   (`REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md`, `AI-TOOLCHAIN-DECISIONS.md`) with a purpose, roles, triggers and a
 27:   gate classification.
 28: - Prerequisite: none beyond a written adoption decision.
 29: - Evidence: an entry in `tool-manifest.json` with `installed: false` and an `evidenceRef` naming a
 30:   real repository file that carries the declaration.
 31: - Meaning of `installed: false` here: the tool is declared but this repository does not pin, vendor
 32:   or otherwise prove its presence. "Present on one operator's machine" is not the claim being made;
 33:   the claim is that the repository cannot yet point at a file that proves the tool is part of the
 34:   workspace, so it stays at `DECLARED` and no test, gate or report may treat it as available.
 35: 
 36: ### 2. `INSTALLED`
 37: 
 38: - Definition: the tool exists in this workspace as a pinned dependency, a resolved engine, a
 39:   package-manager pin, or a checked-in script/wrapper that the repository owns.
 40: - Prerequisite: a real file in this repository declares it (`package.json`,
 41:   `apps/api/package.json`, `packages/testkit/package.json`, ...).
 42: - Evidence: `installed: true` together with an `evidenceRef` of the form
 43:   `<path>/package.json:<key>` where that file exists and that key really holds the dependency.
 44:   The verification command in `tool-manifest-truth.test.js` re-reads the cited file and asserts the
 45:   dependency is genuinely present, so `installed: true` can never be a bare assertion.
 46: 
 47: ### 3. `WIRED`
 48: 
 49: - Definition: the tool is reachable from the repository's own entry points — a root or workspace
 50:   npm script, a git hook, or a Controller tool-gate.
 51: - Prerequisite: a non-null `command` on the manifest entry that names a defined script or an
 52:   executable target checked into the repository.
 53: - Evidence: the manifest `command` field, plus the script definition in the cited `package.json`,
 54:   `lefthook.yml` or `.github/workflows/` file.
 55: 
 56: ### 4. `EXECUTION_VERIFIED`
 57: 
 58: - Definition: the wired command has actually been run in this environment, with both a positive run
 59:   (exit `0` on clean input) and a demonstrated negative run (non-zero exit on a real violation or
 60:   negative fixture).
 61: - Prerequisite: the tool reached `WIRED`.
 62: - Evidence: recorded exit codes and command output in the Work Item's acceptance matrix, and an
 63:   automated test in `tools/ai-brain/test/` that reproduces the outcome.
 64: 
 65: ### 5. `ACCEPTED`
 66: 
 67: - Definition: CI is green on the exact commit, a fresh independent review returned `PASS`, and the
 68:   commit is merged into the integration baseline.
 69: - Prerequisite: independent review verdict `PASS`; the author never approves its own work.
 70: - Evidence: the merged commit OID, the review record on the Work Item, and the register row in the
 71:   `MERGED` state.
 72: 
 73: ## State transition rules
 74: 
 75: 1. Monotonic ladder: `DECLARED` -> `INSTALLED` -> `WIRED` -> `EXECUTION_VERIFIED` -> `ACCEPTED`.
 76:    Movement is one rung at a time and only forward.
 77: 2. No promotion without evidence: a rung may not be claimed if its evidence row above is missing or
 78:    points at a file that does not exist in the repository.
 79: 3. Fail-closed gates: any entry with `gate: true` that has no runnable command must carry
 80:    `command: null` and be explicitly marked `blocked: true` with a non-empty `blockedReason`. Such a
 81:    gate records `TOOL_GATE_UNAVAILABLE`, is never counted as a pass, and never blocks a run.
 82: 4. No retroactive rewriting: a previously verified rung may only be lowered with a written reason
 83:    and the evidence that invalidated it.
 84: 5. `installed` is a boolean, never `UNKNOWN`. An untestable tool is `false` (i.e. `DECLARED`), not
 85:    unknown — an unknown state would let a missing tool be silently treated as present.
 86: 
 87: ## Mandatory fields for Work Items that attach a repository
 88: 
 89: Every Work Item that introduces, upgrades, wires or verifies a repository/tool integration must
 90: record an evidence entry containing all of the following fields.
 91: 
 92: | Field | Type | Description | Allowed values / constraints |
 93: |---|---|---|---|
 94: | `workItemId` | `string` | The Work Item identifier | Non-empty, e.g. `GOAL-AUTOCLAW-REPOS-1` |
 95: | `toolId` | `string` | Tool identifier, matching a `tool-manifest.json` entry `id` | Non-empty; must match a manifest entry |
 96: | `repo` | `string` | Canonical repository identity | `owner/repo`, e.g. `gitleaks/gitleaks` |
 97: | `state` | `string` | Current integration lifecycle state | Exactly one of `DECLARED`, `INSTALLED`, `WIRED`, `EXECUTION_VERIFIED`, `ACCEPTED` |
 98: | `evidenceRef` | `string` | Repository file that proves the state | `<path>:<key>`; the path must exist in the repository |
 99: | `command` | `string \| null` | Command wired to run the tool | Non-empty string, or `null` when blocked/unavailable |
100: | `blocked` | `boolean` | Whether execution is blocked | `true` or `false` |
101: | `blockedReason` | `string \| null` | Why the tool is blocked | Non-empty when `blocked === true`, otherwise `null` |
102: | `verifiedAt` | `string` | When the state was verified | ISO-8601 date-time, e.g. `2026-10-14T12:00:00.000Z` |
103: | `verifiedBy` | `string` | Role or agent that performed the verification | Non-empty, e.g. `gemini`, `codex`, `human` |
104: 
105: `repo-integration-evidence.test.js` implements this table as `validateEvidenceRecord()` and proves
106: it rejects a missing field, an unknown `state`, an `evidenceRef` pointing at a file that does not
107: exist, and `blocked: true` without a reason.
108: 
109: ## Baseline state of the current manifest
110: 
111: Derived from `tools/ai-brain/data/tool-manifest.json`; `installed: true` means the tool is pinned in
112: this workspace and its `evidenceRef` was re-read from the cited `package.json` by the truth test.
113: 
114: | Tool | Repository | State | Evidence reference | Command | Gate |
115: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
116: | `eslint` | `eslint/eslint` | `WIRED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | `lint` | no |
117: | `lefthook` | `evilmartians/lefthook` | `INSTALLED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | — | no |
118: | `supertest` | `forwardemail/supertest` | `INSTALLED` | `apps/api/package.json:devDependencies` | — | no |
119: | `gitleaks` | `gitleaks/gitleaks` | `WIRED` | `package.json:scripts.security:secrets` | `security:secrets` | yes |
120: | `msw` | `mswjs/msw` | `INSTALLED` | `packages/testkit/package.json:dependencies` | — | no |
121: | `nestjs` | `nestjs/nest` | `INSTALLED` | `apps/api/package.json:dependencies` | — | no |
122: | `node` | `nodejs/node` | `INSTALLED` | `package.json:engines` | — | no |
123: | `opentelemetry-js` | `open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js` | `INSTALLED` | `apps/api/package.json:dependencies` | — | no |
124: | `openapi-typescript` | `openapi-ts/openapi-typescript` | `INSTALLED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | — | no |
125: | `pnpm` | `pnpm/pnpm` | `INSTALLED` | `package.json:packageManager` | — | no |
126: | `prettier` | `prettier/prettier` | `WIRED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | `format:check` | no |
127: | `prisma` | `prisma/orm` | `WIRED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | `db:generate` | no |
128: | `turbo` | `vercel/turborepo` | `INSTALLED` | `package.json:devDependencies` | — | no |
129: | `agent-scan` | `snyk/agent-scan` | `DECLARED` (blocked gate) | `REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md` | `null` | yes |
130: | all other entries | — | `DECLARED` | `REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md` | `null` | no |
131: 
132: The machine-wide CLI layer (git, gh, docker, 9router, dsh, codex, claude, gemini/agy, promptfoo,
133: trivy) is installed on operator machines by `scripts/ai/install-clis.ps1`, not by this repository.
134: The repository therefore records those tools as `DECLARED` (`installed: false`), which is the truth
135: about what this repository can prove, and each one is promoted to `INSTALLED` only when its
136: assigned Foundation Work Item pins or wraps it.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/SEMI-MANUAL-AI-WORKFLOW.md">
  1: # 9Router / Gemini → Codex Human-Gated Semi-Automatic Delivery Workflow
  2: 
  3: ## Decision
  4: 
  5: The tools do not share chat history. They coordinate through one GitHub repository, one root `AGENTS.md`, one prepared Work Item, one feature branch and one Pull Request. The versioned `scripts/ai/control.ps1` reads Git/GitHub state and routes one `Resume` action to Codex planning, the assigned implementation author or Codex review. The human starts each gate, approves consequential decisions and performs the merge; CI and versioned evidence carry every handoff.
  6: 
  7: ## Responsibility map
  8: 
  9: | Artifact/action                   | Claude |        Codex planner |           9Router worker |              Gemini |       Codex reviewer |                                           Human |
 10: | --------------------------------- | -----: | -------------------: | -----------------------: | ------------------: | -------------------: | ----------------------------------------------: |
 11: | Propose business/solution updates |  Owner | Validate and version |                       No |                  No |        Verify source |                               Approve decisions |
 12: | Prepare executable Work Item      |     No |                Owner |                       No |                  No |                   No |                                Resolve blockers |
 13: | Choose implementation author      |     No |            Recommend |                       No |                  No |  Challenge if unsafe |                                   Confirm/start |
 14: | Implement production code         |     No |                   No |            Low-risk only |       Primary owner |                   No |                                              No |
 15: | Add and run tests                 |     No |      Define evidence | Owner for assigned scope |               Owner | Verify independently |                                         Observe |
 16: | Open/update Pull Request          |     No | Planning commit only |      Owner when assigned | Owner when assigned |         Read/comment |                                         Observe |
 17: | Approve implementation            |     No |                   No |         No self-approval |    No self-approval |            Recommend |                                     Final owner |
 18: | Merge to `main`                   |     No |                   No |                       No |                  No |                   No | Owner (or controller auto-merge per TASK-AI-13) |
 19: 
 20: ## State flow
 21: 
 22: ```mermaid
 23: stateDiagram-v2
 24:     [*] --> ReadyForAuthor
 25:     ReadyForAuthor --> InProgress: controller starts assigned author
 26:     InProgress --> ReadyForCodex: PR and evidence complete
 27:     ReadyForCodex --> ChangesRequired: Codex finds gaps
 28:     ChangesRequired --> ReadyForCodex: same author fixes same PR
 29:     ReadyForCodex --> CodexPass: every gate passes
 30:     CodexPass --> ReadyForHumanMerge: gate passed
 31:     ReadyForHumanMerge --> GovernedAutoMerge: exact-HEAD preflight pass
 32:     GovernedAutoMerge --> Merged: expectedHeadOid confirmed
 33:     ReadyForHumanMerge --> Merged: manual human merge
 34:     InProgress --> Blocked: missing decision or dependency
 35:     ReadyForCodex --> Blocked: evidence cannot be verified
 36: ```
 37: 
 38: ## One-time local setup
 39: 
 40: | Workspace                           | Branch parked after setup | Purpose                                           |
 41: | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
 42: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-platform` | `main`                    | Integration baseline; never direct implementation |
 43: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-claude`   | `agent/claude`            | Claude business and solution analysis only        |
 44: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-dsh`      | `agent/dsh`               | 9Router/DSH low-risk author                       |
 45: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-gemini`   | `agent/gemini`            | Gemini primary author                             |
 46: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-codex`    | `agent/codex-review`      | Codex planning and independent review             |
 47: 
 48: Each application opens only its own workspace. Complete and verify this layout with `WINDOWS-SETUP-RUNBOOK.md` and the safe commands under `scripts/ai/`. Before a new Work Item, fetch `origin`, create the prepared feature branch from current `origin/main`, and confirm `git status` is clean. Do not reuse an unmerged branch for another item.
 49: 
 50: Configure DSH and 9Router exactly as recorded in `AI-TOOLCHAIN-DECISIONS.md`: local endpoint only, Ponytail/Caveman/Headroom/request logging OFF and no committed credential. Protect `main`: disallow direct pushes and force pushes, require Pull Requests, require the always-present `contract` and `application-gate` checks, and require resolved review conversations.
 51: 
 52: ## Per-Work-Item procedure
 53: 
 54: ### 1. Codex prepares the next item
 55: 
 56: Use `FEATURE-DELIVERY-REGISTER.csv` in ascending `delivery_order`. Dependencies must be `MERGED`. In a planning-only task, Codex creates the feature branch from latest `main`, creates/fills the Work Item, chooses `GEMINI` or `9ROUTER`, records risk and allowed paths, and changes only that row to `READY_FOR_AUTHOR`. It changes no production code.
 57: 
 58: Foundation items run before product features. Use `CODEX-PLANNING-PROMPT.md`.
 59: 
 60: ### 2. Controller starts the assigned author
 61: 
 62: The human runs `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\\scripts\\ai\\control.ps1 -Action Resume`. The controller discovers the earliest remote `READY_FOR_AUTHOR` branch, reads the assigned author from its Work Item, parks the Codex worktree, checks out the branch only in the correct author worktree, copies the completed prompt and opens Gemini/Antigravity or DSH/9Router. No Work Item ID, slug, branch or author is retyped.
 63: 
 64: The author verifies branch, Work Item, allowed scope and readiness before editing. It implements one Work Item, runs the required checks, updates evidence, opens one Pull Request, marks `READY_FOR_CODEX` and stops.
 65: 
 66: ### 3. CI verifies the handoff
 67: 
 68: The `contract` check runs for every Pull Request and validates the product specification, PR contract and PowerShell control-script syntax. The `application-gate` check also always reports: it runs clean install, lint, build and current E2E only when application-affecting paths changed, otherwise records that those checks are not applicable. A failed required check is returned to the same author with its exact log. The author must not claim readiness while CI is red.
 69: 
 70: ### 4. Controller starts independent Codex review
 71: 
 72: When `Resume` detects one non-draft implementation Pull Request and every required check is green, it detaches `shipde-codex` at the immutable PR head and runs a governed read-only review with structured schema output (`codex exec --sandbox read-only --output-schema <schema-file> --output-last-message <review-file> -` with the review prompt piped via stdin). The review is saved outside the repository. The human confirms before it is posted to GitHub. The reviewer reads repository evidence rather than planning or author chat and returns `PASS`, `CHANGES_REQUIRED` or `BLOCKED`.
 73: 
 74: If more than one implementation Pull Request is open during bootstrap or recovery, use `control.ps1 -Action Review -PullRequestNumber <number>`. The controller must select that exact open PR or stop; it never guesses between active Work Items.
 75: 
 76: ### 5. Correction loop
 77: 
 78: `CHANGES_REQUIRED` returns to the same implementation author and same branch. The author fixes findings, reruns the complete validation set and updates the PR evidence. Two failed 9Router correction rounds escalate the item to Gemini; record the author change in the Work Item. Every updated commit requires a fresh Codex verdict.
 79: 
 80: ### 6. Human merge, governed auto-merge and workspace sync
 81: 
 82: The human merges only when CI is green, every acceptance row has evidence, Codex returns `PASS`, review conversations are resolved and residual limitations are explicitly accepted.
 83: 
 84: Under `TASK-AI-13` (`HUMAN-DECISION-ORCHESTRATOR-CORE-PRIORITY-2026-09-08`), the supervisor supports deterministic exact-HEAD auto-merge after `READY_FOR_HUMAN_MERGE`. The controller performs single-snapshot preflight (exact 40-character commit OID, required GitHub Actions `SUCCESS` checks, trusted `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]` terminal `PASS`, zero unresolved threads, mergeable status, push permission), persists a crash-safe `MERGE_INTENT_PERSISTED` checkpoint, and executes one GraphQL `mergePullRequest` mutation with `expectedHeadOid`.
 85: 
 86: The bootstrap of `TASK-AI-13` itself requires manual human merge; subsequent items leverage governed auto-merge. After merge is confirmed by GitHub with its merge commit OID, reconcile the register to `MERGED`, record PR/merge commit, then run `control.ps1 -Action Sync` to park and fast-forward each clean agent worktree from `origin/main` before preparing another item.
 87: 
 88: ## Routing rules
 89: 
 90: ### Assign 9Router only for bounded low-risk work
 91: 
 92: - deterministic fixtures, carrier mocks and seed data;
 93: - focused unit tests for already specified behavior;
 94: - types, schemas or generated/mechanical updates with an existing contract;
 95: - small CRUD or lint fixes with no ownership, authorization or money decision;
 96: - documentation or evidence updates that do not change product meaning.
 97: 
 98: ### Assign Gemini for primary implementation
 99: 
100: - foundation migration and repository architecture;
101: - complete frontend/backend/persistence features;
102: - authentication, authorization and tenant isolation;
103: - carrier commands, retries, reconciliation and external effects;
104: - COD, wallet, billing and any money behavior;
105: - user-facing flows, design-system composition and accessibility;
106: - database migrations or cross-module changes.
107: 
108: ## Human gates
109: 
110: Normal daily operation uses only `control.ps1 -Action Resume` (or **Continue pipeline** from the Desktop shortcut); advanced stage-specific actions remain available for recovery. The human must explicitly approve or start:
111: 
112: 1. material business/solution decisions;
113: 2. the selected Work Item and implementation author;
114: 3. important UI outcomes;
115: 4. changes involving money, permissions, secrets, destructive migrations or production integrations;
116: 5. Codex review and final merge/release.
117: 
118: ## Unattended supervisor mode (TASK-AI-06+)
119: 
120: Run `control.ps1 -Action Supervise`. It validates AO and, when AO is stopped, stale, or running with the wrong profile, invokes `scripts/ai/start-agent-orchestrator.ps1 -Restart` automatically. The launcher forces AO to use its own Claude profile directory (default `%USERPROFILE%\.claude-9router`, overridable with `SHIPDE_NINEROUTER_PROFILE`), routed to the local 9Router gateway, and leaves the native `.claude` login untouched; AgentRouter handles Claude/provider quota fallback without replacing the AO session. The deterministic supervisor automates the per-Work-Item procedure:
121: 
122: AO is an external orchestration layer, not one of the adopted repositories/providers. Its canonical source, installed version and `ao status --json` health check are recorded separately in `tools/ecosystem-manifest.json`.
123: 
124: 1. **Discovers** normal remote `feat/*` and `fix/*` refs and selects the earliest prepared `READY_FOR_AUTHOR` Work Item.
125: 2. **Generates** the implementation prompt automatically (no clipboard/paste).
126: 3. **Spawns** an isolated AO worker using the current public `ao spawn` contract.
127: 4. **Monitors** session state, detecting inactivity and completion.
128: 5. **Nudges** stalled sessions before escalating.
129: 6. **Routes** each failed CI HEAD back to the same worker once.
130: 7. **Triggers** independent Codex review after CI is green and routes exact-HEAD findings back to the worker.
131: 8. **Under `TASK-AI-13` (`HUMAN-DECISION-ORCHESTRATOR-CORE-PRIORITY-2026-09-08`), executes** exact-HEAD auto-merge after durable exact-HEAD PASS when strict preflight passes; falls back to human notification when any preflight signal fails or during bootstrap.
132: 
133: The supervisor is a PowerShell state machine, not an LLM agent loop. It:
134: 
135: - Preserves fail-closed behavior (stops on unrecoverable errors).
136: - Authorizes deterministic exact-HEAD auto-merge under `TASK-AI-13` only when strict preflight passes; human merge remains authoritative during bootstrap and whenever any preflight signal fails.
137: - Relies on AgentRouter for provider/model fallback and treats surfaced exhaustion as a real blocker.
138: - Writes checkpoints for restart recovery.
139: - Respects all existing CI and review gates.
140: 
141: Normal unattended flow:
142: 
143: ```
144: delivery register → supervisor → assigned worker → local verification
145: → commit/push/PR → CI → automatic CI repair → independent Codex review
146: → automatic review repair → exact-HEAD PASS → governed exact-HEAD auto-merge (or human merge fallback on preflight failure)
147: → post-merge synchronization → next Work Item
148: ```
149: 
150: ## Final automation acceptance case (TASK-AI-07 through TASK-AI-12)
151: 
152: The completed orchestrator must perform the full governed flow from one command:
153: 
154: ```powershell
155: powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\control.ps1 -Action Resume
156: ```
157: 
158: The resulting sequence is: select the dependency-ready Work Item; compile the minimum profile; start the assigned worker in its branch/worktree; implement and test; open the PR; monitor and repair CI; invoke independent exact-HEAD Codex review; return review findings to the worker; perform governed exact-HEAD auto-merge after durable `PASS` (or stop for human merge if preflight fails); then reconcile `main` and continue with the next dependency-ready item.
159: 
160: The operator intervenes only for initial credential/login, destructive actions, conflicting or missing business rules, and Pull Request merge when auto-merge preflight fails or during TASK-AI-13 bootstrap. Routine prompt copying, agent-stall watching, CI comment transfer, quota-driven provider switching, and governed exact-HEAD auto-merge are controller responsibilities.
161: 
162: AO session controls keep **Automatically fix CI failures**, **Automatically fix review comments**, and **Terminate on merge** enabled. The controller remains authoritative for exact-HEAD gates, retry budgets, checkpoints and selecting the next Work Item.
163: 
164: ### Profile activation contract
165: 
166: The controller reads `tools/ecosystem-manifest.json` and activates only the governed capabilities needed for the selected Work Item:
167: 
168: | Work type                | Governed capability set                                                          |
169: | ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
170: | Specification            | OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Context7                                                     |
171: | Backend implementation   | Gemini, Serena, Context7, governed coding skills                                 |
172: | UI implementation        | Gemini, governed UI skills, Vercel Agent Skills, component inspection, Storybook |
173: | E2E/API                  | Playwright Test, MSW, Prism                                                      |
174: | Browser diagnosis        | Playwright CLI, Chrome DevTools MCP                                              |
175: | Research                 | `shipde-brain`, one of DSH/Hermes, Repomix                                       |
176: | Review                   | Codex plus controller or governed review daemon                                  |
177: | Multi-agent coordination | Beads plus governed mailbox capability                                           |
178: | Security                 | Agent Scan                                                                       |
179: | Cost                     | TokenTracker plus 9Router statistics                                             |
180: | Maintenance              | Renovate plus Lefthook                                                           |
181: 
182: This contract does not authorize installation of missing repositories or providers. If a named capability has no governed manifest entry, profile compilation stops fail-closed and reports the exact gap. The machine runs at most one implementation agent and one research agent, with one writer per Work Item.
183: 
184: ### Parallel product delivery lane
185: 
186: Toolchain hardening must not block product work. PR #8 is first returned to green CI and an exact-HEAD Codex verdict; `CHANGES_REQUIRED` returns to Gemini, while `PASS` waits for human merge. After merge, the controller reconciles the register and proceeds to `TASK-FOUND-04`: Playwright/Vitest harness, carrier mock server, test seed/reset, and OpenAPI drift validation using MSW and Prism within their assigned roles. Product flows then proceed in order: coverage check, rate comparison, create/cancel shipment, label printing, COD/settlement, webhook idempotency, claims, and finally redelivery/rerouting.
187: 
188: ## Failure handling
189: 
190: | Situation                                                                | Required action                                                                  |
191: | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
192: | Business rule missing or contradictory                                   | Mark `BLOCKED`; no agent may invent it                                           |
193: | Carrier capability unverified                                            | Use explicit unverified/unsupported state and deterministic mock/manual fallback |
194: | AgentRouter exhausts every approved route                                | Preserve checkpoint and stop fail-closed for human credential/provider action    |
195: | 9Router injects Ponytail/Caveman or changes evidence through compression | Stop, disable the feature and repeat verification from uncompressed evidence     |
196: | DSH/9Router version or model catalog changes mid-item                    | Pin the working version/model or mark `BLOCKED`; never silently substitute       |
197: | Author cannot open a PR                                                  | Push branch and provide commit; human opens PR with the template                 |
198: | CI fails                                                                 | Same author fixes the exact failure before review                                |
199: | Codex cannot verify evidence                                             | Return `BLOCKED`, never a conditional pass                                       |
200: | PR contains more than one Work Item                                      | Split before review                                                              |
201: | Existing prototype appears complete                                      | Reassess against the full Definition of Done; demo UI is insufficient            |
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/WINDOWS-SETUP-RUNBOOK.md">
  1: # Windows Setup and Operating Runbook
  2: 
  3: ## Completion definition
  4: 
  5: Setup is complete only when all five worktrees are healthy, all required machine CLIs resolve, Docker Compose is available, Claude/AgentRouter, Gemini/Antigravity and Codex can authenticate, 9Router and DSH can reach an approved free model, GitHub gates are green and `main` is protected. No API key is stored in Git.
  6: 
  7: Windows 10 Pro is used natively. Ubuntu/WSL is not required for this workflow. Docker Desktop may use its supported Windows backend; follow Docker's restart prompt if one appears.
  8: 
  9: ## Expected local layout
 10: 
 11: | Path                                | Role                                       |
 12: | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
 13: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-platform` | protected integration baseline             |
 14: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-claude`   | Claude business and solution analysis only |
 15: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-dsh`      | 9Router/DSH low-risk author                |
 16: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-gemini`   | Gemini primary author                      |
 17: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-codex`    | Codex planner and independent reviewer     |
 18: 
 19: These paths are worktrees of the same repository. Do not clone Playwright, Storybook, NestJS or other upstream source repositories. The complete classification is in `REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md`.
 20: 
 21: ## 1. Merge and synchronize the setup contract
 22: 
 23: After independent Codex `PASS`, squash-merge PR `#1`, then run:
 24: 
 25: ```powershell
 26: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-platform"
 27: git pull --ff-only origin main
 28: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\bootstrap-worktrees.ps1
 29: ```
 30: 
 31: The bootstrap script never resets, deletes or overwrites a dirty worktree. It stops and reports the exact workspace requiring attention.
 32: 
 33: Preview and then install the Desktop entry point for the state controller:
 34: 
 35: ```powershell
 36: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-control-shortcut.ps1
 37: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-control-shortcut.ps1 -Apply
 38: ```
 39: 
 40: This shortcut replaces any older app-launch menu. It opens the versioned controller; choose **Continue pipeline** for normal operation.
 41: 
 42: ## 2. Inventory and install every required CLI
 43: 
 44: Preview first:
 45: 
 46: ```powershell
 47: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-platform"
 48: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-clis.ps1 -InstallDocker
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: If the plan is correct, install only missing tools:
 52: 
 53: ```powershell
 54: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-clis.ps1 -Apply -InstallDocker
 55: ```
 56: 
 57: The script covers pnpm 11, 9Router, pinned DSH, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Claude Code and Docker Desktop. It does not reinstall or upgrade an existing CLI, sign in, start a provider or store a secret. Docker installation can require administrator approval, a restart and opening a new PowerShell window.
 58: 
 59: After restart, launch Docker Desktop and verify:
 60: 
 61: ```powershell
 62: docker version
 63: docker compose version
 64: ```
 65: 
 66: ### 2.1 Governed Ecosystem Management
 67: 
 68: Ship Dễ enforces tool admission and resource boundaries through `tools/ecosystem-manifest.json` and `tools/ecosystem-profiles.json`.
 69: 
 70: Preview missing machine tools without making changes:
 71: 
 72: ```powershell
 73: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-ecosystem.ps1
 74: ```
 75: 
 76: Install approved missing machine tools (preserves existing installations without upgrade and defers later foundation dependencies without modifying package manifests):
 77: 
 78: ```powershell
 79: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\install-ecosystem.ps1 -Apply
 80: ```
 81: 
 82: Validate catalog integrity, Playwright tri-role separation, and fail-closed policies:
 83: 
 84: ```powershell
 85: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\ecosystem.ps1 -Action Validate
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: Check ecosystem status, optional service states, and workspace containment:
 89: 
 90: ```powershell
 91: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\ecosystem.ps1 -Action Status
 92: ```
 93: 
 94: Run automated positive and negative policy proofs (malformed JSON, unpinned version, unknown profile tool, public 0.0.0.0 binding, enabled telemetry, optional services enabled by default, duplicate repository entries, and register idempotency):
 95: 
 96: ```powershell
 97: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\ecosystem.ps1 -Action Test
 98: ```
 99: 
100: Activate a task profile (e.g. `FOUNDATION`, `BACKEND_FEATURE`, `UI_FEATURE`):
101: 
102: ```powershell
103: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\ecosystem.ps1 -Action Activate -Profile FOUNDATION
104: ```
105: 
106: Deactivate the active profile and stop optional background services/MCP processes:
107: 
108: ```powershell
109: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\ecosystem.ps1 -Action Deactivate
110: ```
111: 
112: ## 3. Authenticate interactive tools
113: 
114: GitHub is already authenticated; verify it rather than pasting a token:
115: 
116: ```powershell
117: gh auth status
118: ```
119: 
120: Use the already authenticated Antigravity CLI as the preferred Gemini implementation client; Gemini CLI remains the fallback:
121: 
122: ```powershell
123: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-gemini"
124: agy --version
125: gemini --version
126: ```
127: 
128: Start Codex from its review worktree and use **Sign in with ChatGPT**, not an API key:
129: 
130: ```powershell
131: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-codex"
132: codex login status
133: ```
134: 
135: Claude Code is isolated in `shipde-claude` and remains business/solution-only. Its AgentRouter token must be read by an untracked local launcher or user credential environment, never copied into this repository. Validate the launcher with a harmless analysis prompt; do not route AgentRouter through 9Router.
136: 
137: ## 4. Configure 9Router safely
138: 
139: 1. Start `9router` and open `http://127.0.0.1:20128/dashboard`.
140: 2. Under Endpoint settings set RTK ON, Ponytail OFF, Caveman OFF, Headroom OFF and request logging OFF.
141: 3. Create a free-only combo named `shipde-low-risk` from currently available models using the preference order in `AI-TOOLCHAIN-DECISIONS.md`.
142: 4. Keep the service bound locally. Do not expose port `20128` to the internet.
143: 
144: ## 5. Connect DSH to 9Router
145: 
146: Start DSH from its own workspace:
147: 
148: ```powershell
149: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-dsh"
150: dsh web
151: ```
152: 
153: In DSH open Settings → Models → Add a custom provider and enter:
154: 
155: | Field        | Value                                                                          |
156: | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
157: | Provider ID  | `9router`                                                                      |
158: | Display name | `9Router Local`                                                                |
159: | Base URL     | `http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1`                                                    |
160: | API protocol | `openai-completions`                                                           |
161: | Credential   | paste the API key from the local 9Router dashboard                             |
162: | Model        | `shipde-low-risk`, or a verified current candidate if the combo is not exposed |
163: 
164: Choose Fetch available models before saving. Select `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-dsh` as the only DSH workspace for Ship Dễ.
165: 
166: Run the secure full check; the key is requested as a masked value and is never printed:
167: 
168: ```powershell
169: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-platform"
170: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\doctor.ps1 -TestDocker -TestModels
171: ```
172: 
173: ## 6. Protect GitHub `main`
174: 
175: First preview, then apply:
176: 
177: ```powershell
178: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-platform"
179: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\protect-main.ps1
180: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\protect-main.ps1 -Apply
181: ```
182: 
183: The script enables squash-only merging, deletes merged branches and requires the always-present `contract` and `application-gate` checks. It deliberately does not require a GitHub approval because the repository currently has one account; Codex verdict and human merge ownership remain required by the Work Item contract.
184: 
185: ## 7. Install project repositories through Foundation Work Items
186: 
187: Do not run global installs for the application framework or test stack. The assigned Gemini Foundation Pull Requests add and pin them in this order:
188: 
189: 1. `TASK-FOUND-01`: repair ESLint/format baseline and add secret scanning.
190: 2. `TASK-FOUND-02`: pnpm/Turborepo monorepo migration.
191: 3. `TASK-FOUND-03`: NestJS API/worker plus PostgreSQL, Redis and S3-compatible Docker services.
192: 4. `TASK-FOUND-04`: OpenAPI generation, Vitest/Supertest, Playwright, Storybook, axe, MSW and targeted Lighthouse CI.
193: 
194: Each Foundation item must pass its own CI and independent Codex review. Installing all project dependencies into the current prototype in PR `#1` would mix four different Work Items and remove the ability to identify which migration broke the product.
195: 
196: ## 8. Continue the delivery pipeline
197: 
198: For normal work, do not type Work Item ID, slug, branch, author or Pull Request number. Open **Ship De AI Control** and choose **Continue pipeline**, or run:
199: 
200: ```powershell
201: Set-Location "$env:USERPROFILE\AI\shipde-platform"
202: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\control.ps1 -Action Resume
203: ```
204: 
205: From durable Git/GitHub state the controller performs exactly one next safe transition:
206: 
207: - no prepared item and no implementation PR: open Codex planning with the exact prompt on the clipboard;
208: - one prepared `READY_FOR_AUTHOR` branch: verify its dedicated Work Item, select Gemini/Antigravity or 9Router/DSH, check out only that isolated worktree and copy the filled author prompt;
209: - one implementation PR with green CI: detach the Codex worktree at its immutable head and run non-interactive independent review;
210: - `CHANGES_REQUIRED`: offer to return the findings to the same author and branch;
211: - `PASS`: open the PR for the human merge owner.
212: 
213: The human pastes a prepared prompt when an interactive client opens, approves posting a review comment, resolves material product choices and performs the merge (or relies on governed exact-HEAD auto-merge under TASK-AI-13). The controller never invents a product decision, bypasses red CI or resets a dirty worktree.
214: 
215: ### Codex isolated-worker login
216: 
217: The Codex lane uses the separate `ShipDeWorker` Windows account. Install the approved Codex CLI for that user and complete the ChatGPT sign-in flow in a PowerShell session running as that user:
218: 
219: ```powershell
220: codex login
221: codex login status
222: ```
223: 
224: The operator account's `~/.codex` files are never copied, exported, or read. The isolated launcher sets `HOME` and `USERPROFILE` to the per-task worker root before checking login status and launching `codex exec`. If `codex login status` fails or the CLI is missing, the Controller records `CODEX_NOT_LOGGED_IN` as a local candidate failure and continues with another candidate. Authenticate the worker user before selecting Codex again.
225: 
226: The launcher reads the operator-owned attestation at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ShipDe\isolation-verdict.json` before preparing the worker. Codex execution requires a `CLOSED` verdict; a verdict supplied by the job is not sufficient. Re-run the isolation check to refresh the attestation before retrying a refused launch.
227: 
228: ## 9. Synchronize after human merge
229: 
230: After squash-merging the passing PR, run:
231: 
232: ```powershell
233: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\ai\control.ps1 -Action Sync
234: ```
235: 
236: This parks and fast-forwards every clean worktree. Then choose **Continue pipeline** again to prepare the next dependency-ready Work Item. The lower-level `start-work-item.ps1` and `review-pr.ps1` remain recovery tools, not the normal operating path.
237: 
238: ## Daily control rules
239: 
240: - Never open two apps on the same worktree.
241: - Never let an author work directly on `main` or `agent/codex-review`.
242: - Never paste API keys into chat, Work Items, `.env`, commits, screenshots or logs.
243: - Stop when a script reports a dirty workspace; inspect instead of resetting.
244: - Do not auto-upgrade a CLI during an active Work Item.
245: - After merge, run controller `Sync`; rerun `doctor.ps1` after tool, Docker, credential or model changes.
246: - Keep one active implementation Work Item until the workflow has passed its first complete cycle.
247: 
248: ## Final readiness checklist
249: 
250: - All five worktrees are present and clean.
251: - `git`, `gh`, `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `docker`, `9router`, `dsh`, `codex`, `claude` and at least one Gemini client (`agy` preferred, `gemini` fallback) resolve in a new PowerShell window.
252: - `gh auth status`, Antigravity/Gemini sign-in, Codex ChatGPT sign-in and the isolated Claude/AgentRouter launcher are healthy.
253: - Docker Desktop is running and `docker compose version` succeeds.
254: - 9Router port `20128` and DSH port `3080` are reachable when started.
255: - DSH successfully completes the `SHIPDE_OK` task through `shipde-low-risk`.
256: - Ponytail, Caveman, Headroom and request logging are OFF.
257: - GitHub `main` rejects direct/force pushes and requires `contract` plus `application-gate`.
258: - PR #1 is merged only after an independent Codex `PASS`.
259: - `TASK-FOUND-01` is the next and only implementation item.
260: - If an isolated Codex probe reports `CODEX_NOT_LOGGED_IN`, sign in as `ShipDeWorker` and confirm `codex login status` succeeds there. A missing CLI or failed status check is a local failure, and the Controller continues to another candidate.
</file>

<file path="packages/config/src/telemetry.ts">
  1: import {
  2:   trace,
  3:   context,
  4:   propagation,
  5:   Span,
  6:   Tracer,
  7:   SpanStatusCode,
  8:   ROOT_CONTEXT,
  9:   Context,
 10: } from '@opentelemetry/api';
 11: import { W3CTraceContextPropagator } from '@opentelemetry/core';
 12: import {
 13:   BasicTracerProvider,
 14:   SimpleSpanProcessor,
 15:   InMemorySpanExporter,
 16:   SpanExporter,
 17: } from '@opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base';
 18: import { resourceFromAttributes } from '@opentelemetry/resources';
 19: 
 20: let provider: BasicTracerProvider | null = null;
 21: let inMemoryExporter: InMemorySpanExporter | null = null;
 22: 
 23: // Register W3C propagator at module load so extractTraceContext works
 24: // regardless of whether initTelemetry has been called yet.
 25: propagation.setGlobalPropagator(new W3CTraceContextPropagator());
 26: 
 27: class NoopSpanExporter implements SpanExporter {
 28:   export(_spans: unknown[], resultCallback: (result: { code: number }) => void): void {
 29:     resultCallback({ code: 0 });
 30:   }
 31:   async shutdown(): Promise<void> {
 32:     return Promise.resolve();
 33:   }
 34: }
 35: 
 36: export interface TelemetryOptions {
 37:   inMemory?: boolean;
 38: }
 39: 
 40: /**
 41:  * Initializes OpenTelemetry distributed tracing foundation with standard service resource.
 42:  * In production/default runtime, uses NoopSpanExporter so finished spans are not retained in memory.
 43:  * InMemorySpanExporter is strictly restricted to test harnesses.
 44:  */
 45: export function initTelemetry(
 46:   serviceName: string,
 47:   serviceVersion = '0.1.0',
 48:   options: TelemetryOptions = {}
 49: ): {
 50:   tracer: Tracer;
 51:   shutdown: () => Promise<void>;
 52:   getRecordedSpans: () => unknown[];
 53: } {
 54:   if (!provider) {
 55:     if (options.inMemory) {
 56:       inMemoryExporter = new InMemorySpanExporter();
 57:       provider = new BasicTracerProvider({
 58:         resource: resourceFromAttributes({
 59:           'service.name': serviceName,
 60:           'service.version': serviceVersion,
 61:         }),
 62:         spanProcessors: [new SimpleSpanProcessor(inMemoryExporter)],
 63:       });
 64:     } else {
 65:       inMemoryExporter = null;
 66:       provider = new BasicTracerProvider({
 67:         resource: resourceFromAttributes({
 68:           'service.name': serviceName,
 69:           'service.version': serviceVersion,
 70:         }),
 71:         spanProcessors: [new SimpleSpanProcessor(new NoopSpanExporter())],
 72:       });
 73:     }
 74:     trace.setGlobalTracerProvider(provider);
 75:   }
 76: 
 77:   const tracer = trace.getTracer(serviceName, serviceVersion);
 78: 
 79:   return {
 80:     tracer,
 81:     shutdown: async () => {
 82:       if (provider) {
 83:         await provider.shutdown();
 84:         trace.disable();
 85:         provider = null;
 86:         inMemoryExporter = null;
 87:       }
 88:     },
 89:     getRecordedSpans: () => inMemoryExporter?.getFinishedSpans() || [],
 90:   };
 91: }
 92: 
 93: /**
 94:  * Retrieves a named tracer from the active OpenTelemetry provider.
 95:  */
 96: export function getTracer(serviceName = 'shipde-foundation'): Tracer {
 97:   return trace.getTracer(serviceName);
 98: }
 99: 
100: /**
101:  * Wraps an async operation in an OpenTelemetry span with error recording and status management.
102:  */
103: export async function withSpan<T>(
104:   tracer: Tracer,
105:   name: string,
106:   fn: (span: Span) => Promise<T>,
107:   attributes?: Record<string, string | number | boolean>,
108:   parentContext?: Context
109: ): Promise<T> {
110:   const activeCtx = parentContext || context.active();
111:   const options = { attributes };
112:   const execute = async (span: Span): Promise<T> => {
113:     try {
114:       const result = await fn(span);
115:       span.setStatus({ code: SpanStatusCode.OK });
116:       return result;
117:     } catch (err: unknown) {
118:       span.setStatus({
119:         code: SpanStatusCode.ERROR,
120:         message: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err),
121:       });
122:       span.recordException(err instanceof Error ? err : new Error(String(err)));
123:       throw err;
124:     } finally {
125:       span.end();
126:     }
127:   };
128: 
129:   if (activeCtx) {
130:     return tracer.startActiveSpan(name, options, activeCtx, execute);
131:   }
132:   return tracer.startActiveSpan(name, options, execute);
133: }
134: 
135: /**
136:  * Extracts W3C trace context from incoming HTTP headers or message carrier.
137:  */
138: export function extractTraceContext(headers: Record<string, string | string[] | undefined>) {
139:   const carrier: Record<string, string> = {};
140:   for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(headers)) {
141:     if (typeof value === 'string') {
142:       carrier[key.toLowerCase()] = value;
143:     } else if (Array.isArray(value) && value.length > 0 && typeof value[0] === 'string') {
144:       carrier[key.toLowerCase()] = value[0];
145:     }
146:   }
147:   return propagation.extract(ROOT_CONTEXT, carrier);
148: }
149: 
150: /**
151:  * Injects active W3C trace context into an outbound carrier object (e.g. queue job headers).
152:  */
153: export function injectTraceContext(carrier: Record<string, string>): void {
154:   propagation.inject(context.active(), carrier);
155: }
156: 
157: /**
158:  * Retrieves current active traceId and spanId if an OpenTelemetry span is active.
159:  */
160: export function getCurrentTraceAndSpanId(): { traceId?: string; spanId?: string } {
161:   const currentSpan = trace.getActiveSpan();
162:   if (currentSpan) {
163:     const spanContext = currentSpan.spanContext();
164:     return {
165:       traceId: spanContext.traceId,
166:       spanId: spanContext.spanId,
167:     };
168:   }
169:   return {};
170: }
</file>

<file path="packages/config/README.md">
 1: # @shipde/config
 2: 
 3: Shared workspace configuration profiles for TypeScript, linting, and toolchains across the Ship Dễ monorepo.
 4: 
 5: ## Purpose
 6: 
 7: - Centralize TypeScript base compiler options (`tsconfig.base.json`).
 8: - Provide shared environment and build-time constants.
 9: 
10: ## Boundary
11: 
12: - Contains reusable base configuration and type declarations.
13: - Does not contain runtime business logic or UI components.
</file>

 9: ## Boundary
