116: ## Audit and settlement
117: 
118: | Entity.field                              | Type    |        Required | Notes                                          |
119: | ----------------------------------------- | ------- | --------------: | ---------------------------------------------- |
120: | RateContractVersion.effective_from/to     | date    | Yes/conditional | Non-overlap for approved versions              |
121: | RateRule.source_clause                    | string  |             Yes | Page/clause/evidence                           |
122: | RateRule.approval_status                  | enum    |             Yes | DRAFT/REVIEW/APPROVED/REJECTED                 |
123: | SettlementPolicyVersion.opening_carry_vnd | integer |             Yes | Confirmed source                               |
124: | AuditRun.input_snapshot_hash              | string  |             Yes | Immutable reproducibility                      |
125: | ProcessingResult.status                   | enum    |             Yes | Exactly one processing status                  |
126: | Finding.type                              | enum    |             Yes | COD/FEE/WEIGHT/SURCHARGE/DUPLICATE/MISSING/... |
127: | Finding.suspected_amount_vnd              | integer |             Yes | Separate evidence level                        |
128: | SettlementBatch.carrier_transfer_status   | enum    |             Yes | NOT_REPORTED/REPORTED                          |
129: | SettlementBatch.bank_status               | enum    |             Yes | NO_DATA/UNMATCHED/FULL/SHORT/OVER              |
130: | BatchBankAllocation.amount_vnd            | integer |             Yes | > 0, constrained totals                        |
131: 
132: ## Case and claim
133: 
134: | Entity.field                            | Type      |    Required | Notes                                 |
135: | --------------------------------------- | --------- | ----------: | ------------------------------------- |
136: | DiscrepancyCase.status                  | enum      |         Yes | State machine value                   |
137: | DiscrepancyCase.internally_verified_vnd | integer   |         Yes | Not carrier accepted                  |
138: | DiscrepancyCase.carrier_accepted_vnd    | integer   |         Yes | May be unpaid                         |
139: | DiscrepancyCase.received_vnd            | integer   |         Yes | Bank/payment evidence                 |
140: | Evidence.sha256                         | string    |         Yes | Integrity after ingestion             |
141: | Evidence.server_captured_at             | timestamp | Conditional | Direct capture evidence               |
142: | ClaimSubmission.mode                    | enum      |         Yes | CONFIRM_FIRST/AUTO_POLICY             |
143: | ClaimSubmission.provider_reference      | string    | Conditional | Set after provider acknowledgment     |
144: | RecoveryReceipt.amount_vnd              | integer   |         Yes | One of multiple installments          |
145: | RecoveryReceipt.bank_transaction_id     | UUID      | Conditional | Required to state bank-proven receipt |
146: 
147: ## Data classification
148: 
149: - Restricted: credentials, bank statements, raw files, recipient contact/address, evidence media.
150: - Confidential: contracts/rates, COD, claims, billing.
151: - Internal: operational statuses, system logs without secrets.
152: - Public: published help/status content only.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/08-testing/ACCEPTANCE-AND-E2E.md">
  1: # Acceptance Criteria and End-to-End Scenarios
  2: 
  3: ## Core acceptance criteria
  4: 
  5: ### AC-AUTH-01
  6: 
  7: Given an active verified user with valid credentials, when login and MFA succeed, then the user enters only authorized tenant/scope; failed attempts are rate-limited and audited.
  8: 
  9: ### AC-AUTH-02
 10: 
 11: Given a prospective shop owner on SCR-AUTH-02 (/register), when submitting valid shop name, owner name, email or phone, password, and accepted terms, then exactly one Merchant and User(OWNER, PENDING_VERIFICATION) are created atomically and a single-use expiring verification token is issued; when verified with a valid token, the user transitions to ACTIVE and verified timestamp is recorded; invalid inputs, duplicate verified identifiers, unaccepted terms, expired/consumed tokens, and rate-limit violations fail closed with distinct actionable errors.
 12: 
 13: ### AC-AUTH-05
 14: 
 15: Given an active user on Ship Dễ, when setting up MFA with fresh primary authentication, then a 10-minute expiring TOTP factor is provisioned and secret encrypted at rest; when verified with a valid non-replayed TOTP, exactly one active factor and 10 single-use recovery codes are issued, and session carries MFA assurance metadata; when an enrolled user logs in, MFA_REQUIRED is returned with an opaque 5-minute challenge; owners without MFA receive MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED with a bounded setup token; authorized administrators can reset another user's factor with mandatory reason and idempotency, revoking all target sessions and logging immutable audit records.
 16: 
 17: ### AC-USR-01
 18: 
 19: Given an owner, when inviting an operator with one warehouse/account scope, then the invite can be accepted and the operator cannot access another warehouse/account.
 20: 
 21: ### AC-AVL-01
 22: 
 23: Given valid shipment inputs, when carriers respond supported/rejected/timeout, then UI shows AVAILABLE/UNSUPPORTED/UNKNOWN_ERROR respectively and never converts timeout to unsupported.
 24: 
 25: ### AC-QTE-01
 26: 
 27: Given at least two available quotes, when displayed, then all fee components, total, VAT state, SLA and expiry are normalized and raw snapshots remain traceable.
 28: 
 29: ### AC-SEL-01
 30: 
 31: Given eligible options, when recommendation runs, then cheapest uses total fee, fastest uses comparable SLA, balanced exposes score, and manual override is recorded.
 32: 
 33: ### AC-SHP-01
 34: 
 35: Given a valid selected quote, when create times out after reaching the carrier, then Ship Dễ reconciles by client reference and produces at most one waybill.
 36: 
 37: ### AC-LBL-01
 38: 
 39: Given a created shipment, when label is printed and the shipment is cancelled/switched, then the old label is marked invalid and cannot be used in normal operations.
 40: 
 41: ### AC-TRK-01
 42: 
 43: Given duplicate/out-of-order/unknown tracking events, when ingested, then raw events are preserved, duplicates do not duplicate transition, order is handled and unknown status is not guessed.
 44: 
 45: ### AC-EXC-01
 46: 
 47: Given a delivery failure, when an authorized user requests redelivery twice with the same idempotency key, then only one external action is recorded; unsupported API produces a manual checklist.
 48: 
 49: ### AC-RET-01
 50: 
 51: Given an expected return, when scanned twice, then the second receipt is blocked; direct evidence is linked to actor, server time, waybill and original hash.
 52: 
 53: ### AC-RATE-01
 54: 
 55: Given a draft rate authored by A, when A tries to approve it, then approval is denied; reviewer B may approve after source and simulator validation.
 56: 
 57: ### AC-AUD-01
 58: 
 59: Given matched, source-only, carrier-only, ambiguous and incomplete records, when audit runs, then each has exactly one processing status and zero-to-many separate findings with lineage.
 60: 
 61: ### AC-BNK-01
 62: 
 63: Given one bank transaction allocated across multiple batches, when allocations exceed the transaction, then confirmation is rejected; exact-reference and suggestion states are distinguishable.
 64: 
 65: ### AC-CLM-01
 66: 
 67: Given complete evidence and verified policy, when auto-submit is disabled, then claim waits for confirmation; when enabled within limit it submits once; expired/incomplete claims never auto-submit.
 68: 
 69: ## End-to-end scenarios
 70: 
 71: ### E2E-01 Happy shipping
 72: 
 73: Register → shop/warehouse → carrier → order → serviceability → quote → select → create → label → pickup → tracking → delivered → statement → clean audit.
 74: 
 75: ### E2E-02 No carrier option
 76: 
 77: Invalid/unsupported route → show reasons → edit ward/parcel → retry without re-entry → obtain option or save manual draft.
 78: 
 79: ### E2E-03 Partial carrier incident
 80: 
 81: GHN timeout while GHTK succeeds → display GHTK option and GHN unknown incident → selection/create proceeds without global outage.
 82: 
 83: ### E2E-04 Unknown create outcome
 84: 
 85: Create timeout → command unknown → remote lookup finds waybill → one local shipment confirmed; no second create.
 86: 
 87: ### E2E-05 Delivery rescue
 88: 
 89: Delivery failure webhook → exception priority → CS notes → redelivery → delivered → rescue metric.
 90: 
 91: ### E2E-06 Return issue
 92: 
 93: Returning → expected queue → scan → damage evidence → case → claim package.
 94: 
 95: ### E2E-07 Fee discrepancy
 96: 
 97: Approved contract → statement fee higher → matched processing status plus fee finding → internal verify → claim → carrier accepts → bank recovery.
 98: 
 99: ### E2E-08 Missing COD
100: 
101: Source-only delivered order progresses through A/B/C → account threshold checked → overdue suspicion → case; no early false alert.
102: 
103: ### E2E-09 Bank many-to-many
104: 
105: Two transactions fund one batch and one transaction funds another batch → allocations confirmed → batch statuses full/short as calculated.
106: 
107: ### E2E-10 Tenant attack
108: 
109: User changes resource UUID to another tenant → backend returns not-found/forbidden without leaking metadata; event audited.
</file>

100: ## Caller, triggers and boundaries
101:

103: test-driven-development, systematic-debugging and verification-before-completion;
104: reviewer/security-review receive review skills; ui/frontend roles receive

106: rules first. Unknown roles receive no pack; SHIPDE_SKILL_PACK=off disables it.

114: the OpenSpec CLI is installed or invoked. Do not create a second spec authority.

116: `tools/ai-brain/decisions.js` for decision provenance.

118: ## Controller gate evidence
119: 
120: The real gate is `runToolGates` in `tools/ai-brain/orchestrate.js`, called after
121: format checks and before review. It uses `tools/ai-brain/tool-manifest.js`
122: gatesFor/appliesTo, runs available commands, records TOOL_GATE_FAILED and allows
123: one repair; persistent failure returns REFUSED. Missing command/install/executable
124: records TOOL_GATE_UNAVAILABLE, never a tool pass. Aggregate PASSED can mean no
125: applicable runnable gates; inspect individual records, not only aggregate status.
126: Synthetic repo commands with empty triggers do not apply through this gate.
127: Skill text is guidance, never enforcement.
128: 
129: Offline tests execute the existing Controller function with injected fixtures:
130: exit 0, persistent exit 1 with one repair, and unavailable command. This is
131: Controller logic evidence, not a real external scanner or OpenSpec run.
132: GitHub evidence must bind repository, branch, full SHA and checks; PR creation
133: does not grant merge authority. No GitHub mutation or authenticated lookup was run.
134: Task artifact: role-selected pack and in-memory gate records from the tests.
135: Spec validation runs separately below; no claim that loader invokes validation.

162: ### OpenSpec wiring 2026-10-21

164: - Trigger: `pnpm test:specs`, CI step `Work Item acceptance matrices (OpenSpec strict validate)`.
165: - Caller: `tools/openspec-check/run.js` renders each Work Item acceptance matrix into an
166:   ephemeral `openspec/specs/<id>/spec.md` in a temp directory and runs
167:   `openspec validate --specs --strict --json`. Nothing is committed under `openspec/`;
168:   the Work Item remains the only spec authority.

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/CODEX-PLANNING-PROMPT.md">
 1: # Codex Work Item Planning Prompt
 2: 
 3: Use this in a planning-only Codex task before assigning implementation. The user may say: **“Chuẩn bị Work Item tiếp theo.”**
 4: 
 5: ```text
 6: Prepare the next dependency-ready Ship Dễ Work Item. Do not implement production code.
 7: 
 8: 1. Read root AGENTS.md, SEMI-MANUAL-AI-WORKFLOW.md, the delivery register, backlog dependencies, Definition of Ready, traceability and all source documents linked to the candidate item.
 9: 2. Select the earliest eligible row. Every dependency must be MERGED. Do not skip an earlier blocked item without recording why.
10: 3. Create `feat/<lowercase-work-item-id>-<short-slug>` from latest `origin/main`. Do not change application code.
11: 4. Create exactly `docs/product-spec/work-items/<WORK_ITEM_ID>.md` from `WORK-ITEM-TEMPLATE.md` (including for `TASK-FOUND-*`) and fill every business, technical-boundary and acceptance section. Do not leave an aggregate source such as `FOUNDATION-WORK-ITEMS.md` as the executable Work Item path.
12: 5. Record exact actor, outcome, source IDs, scope, non-scope, rules, UI states, API/events/data impact, negative paths, evidence and verification commands.
13: 6. Choose Assigned author:
14:    - 9ROUTER only when risk is LOW, behavior and allowed paths are bounded, deterministic checks prove completion, and no prohibited domain in AGENTS.md is touched.
15:    - GEMINI for every other Work Item, including all foundation, vertical, UI, security, money, carrier-effect and cross-layer work.
16: 7. If a material product choice remains, mark BLOCKED and ask the human; do not invent it.
17: 8. Check Definition of Ready. Only when every gate passes, update exactly that register row: set `work_item_path` to the dedicated file, set `branch` to the prepared branch, and set `status` to `READY_FOR_AUTHOR`. Do not change another row.
18: 9. Commit and push planning documents to the prepared branch. Do not open the implementation PR yet.
19: 10. Return Work Item ID, branch, author choice and reason, source path, readiness evidence, allowed paths and the correct start prompt with placeholders replaced.
20: ```
21: 
22: Planning and later review must use separate Codex tasks. Review starts from the Pull Request evidence, not the planning conversation.
23: 
24: ## Pre-authoring specification checklist (spec-kit)
25: 
26: Verify before setting `READY_FOR_AUTHOR`:
27: - [ ] **Ambiguity check**: Tag open questions or unverified assumptions with `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`. If any remain unresolved, mark `BLOCKED`; never leave the author to guess.
28: - [ ] **Constitution check**: Enforce non-negotiables (tenant scope, RBAC, audit masking, VND integer math, carrier reconciliation, tests at the lowest useful level with test-first ordering for executable acceptance rows and `test not applicable: <justification>` for non-executable rows).
29: - [ ] **Task breakdown**: Decompose work into numbered tasks ordered API/backend before UI, test-first for executable acceptance rows, with `[P]` markers for parallel-safe independent tasks.
30: - [ ] **Slice sizing**: Keep the Work Item a single vertical Pull Request bounded to ~400 changed lines (API/backend before UI inside the same PR). If it cannot fit while staying vertical, split it into independently scoped prerequisite Work Items (own file, register row, branch, PR and acceptance matrix each, linked via register `dependencies`); set `READY_FOR_AUTHOR` on the prerequisites, and record that the feature completes only when the terminal item merges.
</file>

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/GEMINI-START-PROMPT.md">
 1: # Gemini Start Prompt
 2: 
 3: Use one new Gemini task per Work Item after opening `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-gemini`. Replace all placeholders.
 4: 
 5: ```text
 6: Implement exactly one Ship Dễ Work Item: <WORK_ITEM_ID> on the Codex-prepared branch <BRANCH>.
 7: 
 8: Mandatory operating contract:
 9: 1. Read root AGENTS.md completely.
10: 2. Read SEMI-MANUAL-AI-WORKFLOW.md, the matching register row and the complete Work Item.
11: 3. Confirm Assigned author is GEMINI, dependencies are merged, the branch is correct and the worktree is clean.
12: 4. Follow source precedence. Existing prototype code is evidence, not proof of completion.
13: 5. Plan the technical implementation before editing and map every acceptance row to code and evidence.
14: 6. If a material rule, acceptance condition or dependency is missing, mark BLOCKED with evidence and stop; do not invent behavior.
15: 7. Implement only this Work Item as a complete vertical feature: UI, backend, persistence, authorization, error/recovery states, audit, contracts and tests where applicable.
16: 8. Do not add another feature, broad cleanup or unrelated refactor.
17: 9. Run every required validation command. Never report a command as passed unless it actually ran successfully.
18: 10. Update the Work Item, register and traceability with implementation evidence. Fill every PR template section.
19: 11. Commit, push and open one Pull Request titled `[<WORK_ITEM_ID>] <business outcome>`.
20: 12. Set the item to READY_FOR_CODEX and stop. Do not merge or start another Work Item.
21: 
22: Final response:
23: - Work Item and branch
24: - Pull Request URL
25: - implemented requirement IDs
26: - commands actually run and exact results
27: - evidence locations
28: - assumptions, limitations or blockers
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Pre-implementation checklist (spec-kit)
32: 
33: Verify before writing code:
34: - [ ] **Ambiguity check**: If any `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker or missing specification exists, stop and mark `BLOCKED` with evidence; never guess or assume behavior.
35: - [ ] **Constitution check**: Verify tenant scope, RBAC, audit masking, VND integer arithmetic, carrier reconciliation, and tests at the lowest useful level (test-first for executable acceptance rows; `test not applicable: <justification>` recorded for non-executable rows).
36: - [ ] **Task breakdown**: Execute numbered tasks ordered API/backend before UI and test-first for executable rows, running independent `[P]` tasks in parallel where applicable.
37: - [ ] **Slice sizing**: Keep the single vertical Pull Request bounded to ~400 lines (API/backend before UI inside it); if the diff would exceed the budget, stop and escalate a split into prerequisite Work Items to the planner instead of shipping horizontal slices.
38: 
39: ## Review-fix prompt
40: 
41: ```text
42: Read all current Codex findings on <PR_URL>. Fix every actionable finding for <WORK_ITEM_ID> on the existing branch only. Do not dismiss a finding without code/test evidence or a human-approved specification decision. Rerun the complete verification set, update PR evidence, push, set READY_FOR_CODEX and stop.
43: ```
</file>

21: Final response:
22: - Work Item and branch
23: - Pull Request URL or BLOCKED_FOR_GEMINI
24: - changed files and implemented requirement IDs
25: - commands actually run and exact results
26: - evidence locations
27: - blocker/escalation reason, if any
28: ```
29: 
30: ## Pre-implementation checklist (spec-kit)
31: 
32: Verify before writing code:
33: - [ ] **Ambiguity check**: If any `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker or unspecified behavior exists, stop with `BLOCKED_FOR_GEMINI`; never guess.
34: - [ ] **Constitution check**: Confirm scope does not touch prohibited domains (tenant isolation, RBAC, money/COD, carrier side effects).
35: - [ ] **Task breakdown**: Follow the numbered task breakdown (API/backend before UI, tests first for executable rows); run independent `[P]` tasks within allowed paths.
36: - [ ] **Slice sizing**: Keep changes strictly bounded within allowed paths and ~400 lines inside the single vertical Work Item Pull Request.
37: 
38: ## Review-fix prompt
39: 
40: ```text
41: Read the current Codex findings on <PR_URL>. Fix only findings that remain within the approved low-risk scope for <WORK_ITEM_ID>. If any finding requires a prohibited domain or two correction rounds have failed, stop with BLOCKED_FOR_GEMINI. Otherwise rerun all checks, update evidence, push, set READY_FOR_CODEX and stop.
42: ```
</file>

  1: # Orchestrate Module Architecture & Function Map
  2: 
  3: > Task: TASK-AI-142 (Pure move refactor of `tools/ai-brain/orchestrate.js`)
  4: > Source baseline: `tools/ai-brain/orchestrate.js` (9,402 lines, 104 top-level functions, 36 exports)
  5: > Operating contract: PURE MOVE REFACTOR — zero behavior change, zero renames, zero logic edits outside moved code.
  6: 
  7: ## 1. Executive Summary & Module Architecture
  8: 
  9: `tools/ai-brain/orchestrate.js` is the central autonomous execution loop in Ship Dễ. Over iterative delivery, it grew to 9,402 lines covering multiple distinct architectural concerns. This document maps every single top-level function (104 functions total) to its target module, cataloguing its line range, callers across `tools/ai-brain` (including tests, production tools, and `cli.js`), and identifies shared mutable state.
 10: 
 11: ### Target Module Decomposition
 12: 
 13: | Target Module | Purpose | Functions | Approx Lines |
 14: |---|---|---|---|
 15: | `orchestrate/decisions-log.js` | Decision and warning emission helpers, error scrubbing, failure detail formatting, run refusal. | 5 | 42 |
 16: | `orchestrate/route-probe.js` | Writer route probe execution, launch route resolution, model prefix stripping, probe ordering glue. | 3 | 70 |
 17: | `orchestrate/candidates.js` | Candidate combination building, task profile extraction, role resolution, RTK policy, evidence accounts merging and filtering. | 10 | 245 |
 18: | `orchestrate/ranking.js` | Realtime candidate selection for profile, scoring, JEV direct weighting, attempt tracking, failure evidence logging. | 4 | 470 |
 19: | `orchestrate/checkpoint.js` | Checkpoint reading/writing, resume validation, cryptographic receipt generation, review normalization, test evidence compaction. | 21 | 520 |
 20: | `orchestrate/publication.js` | Draft PR title generation, publish cwd resolution, hardened git cherry-pick/commit import, approval selection, PR publication. | 13 | 508 |
 21: | `orchestrate/writer-loop.js` | Writer launch execution, worker root and commit verification, harness selection, fail-before capture, usage reporting, tree dirty checks. | 17 | 755 |
 22: | `orchestrate/review-loop.js` | Review lane execution, host brain gate, detached worktree checkout, prettier/tool gates, reviewItem lifecycle, repair rounds. | 25 | 2818 |
 23: | `orchestrate.js (core runner)` | Default options builder, dependency top-sort, main orchestration loop (runOrchestration), and final finish/reconciliation coordinator. | 6 | 3124 |
 24: 
 25: ## 2. Shared Mutable State & Cross-Module State Boundaries
 26: 
 27: A clean modular split requires identifying all module-level mutable variables, caches, and globals that cannot be trivially duplicated:
 28: 
 29: ### A. `baseGateCache` (Line 1856)
 30: - **Type**: `Map<string, object>` (in-memory test failure and timing cache)
 31: - **Location**: Declared at line 1856 of `orchestrate.js` (`const baseGateCache = new Map();`)
 32: - **Used By**: `runHostBrainGate` (Line 2019: `const cache = options.baseCache || baseGateCache;`)
 33: - **Exported**: Exported in `module.exports` (`baseGateCache`)
 34: - **External Tests Touching It**: `task-ai-142-host-gate-baseline.test.js`, `task-ai-142-hostgate-repair.test.js` inspect and call `.clear()` on `require('./orchestrate').baseGateCache` to ensure isolated gate assertions.
 35: - **Target Module**: `orchestrate/review-loop.js` (which owns `runHostBrainGate`).
 36: - **Refactor Strategy**: `review-loop.js` instantiates and exports `baseGateCache`. `orchestrate.js` re-exports it directly (`baseGateCache: reviewLoop.baseGateCache`) so tests keep object identity. Callers can also explicitly inject `options.baseCache`.
 37: 
 38: ### B. Constants and Enums (Immutable Module State)
 39: - `PROBE_BUDGET_MS = 60000;` (Line 77) -> Target: `orchestrate/route-probe.js` (re-exported by `orchestrate.js` for `capability-probe.js`).
 40: - `ItemStatus`, `RunStatus`, `PublicationStatus` (Lines 86-104) -> Target: `orchestrate.js` core or shared constants module; referenced by `finish` and `runOrchestration`.
 41: - `DEFAULT_REVIEW_BUDGET = 120000;`, `SHA_40`, `ACCEPTED_VERDICTS` (Lines 110-112) -> Target: `orchestrate/review-loop.js` and `orchestrate/checkpoint.js`.
 42: - `WORK_ITEM_ID`, `DRAFT_TITLE_LIMIT` (Lines 2474-2475) -> Target: `orchestrate/publication.js`.
 43: - `FormatGate`, `ToolGate`, `PRETTIER_FILE` (Lines 6894-6907) -> Target: `orchestrate/review-loop.js`.

215: 
216: ## 4. Extraction Plan & Recommended Order
217: 
218: The refactoring is executed iteratively, extracting one module at a time from lowest-dependency/least-coupled to highest-coupled:
219: 
220: 1. **Step 1 (Current)**: Architecture & Mapping documentation (`ORCHESTRATE-MODULE-MAP.md`).
221: 2. **Step 2 (Current Task)**: `orchestrate/decisions-log.js`
222:    - **Functions**: `launchFailureText`, `failureMessageOf`, `failedDecisionDetail`, `markIsolationVerdictStop`, `refuseRun`.
223:    - **Rationale**: 5 functions, 42 lines, 0 shared mutable state, 0 external callers outside `orchestrate.js`, completely clean leaf dependency.
224: 3. **Step 3 (Next)**: `orchestrate/route-probe.js`
225:    - **Functions**: `routeProbeCandidate`, `resolveLaunchRoute`, `stripOpencodeProviderPrefix`, plus `PROBE_BUDGET_MS`.
226:    - **Rationale**: 3 functions, 70 lines, self-contained probe resolution logic consumed by `capability-probe.js` and `rolling-onboard.js`.
227: 4. **Step 4**: `orchestrate/candidates.js`
228:    - **Functions**: `buildCandidates`, `buildProfile`, `buildTaskProfile`, `rtkPolicyForItem`, `roleOf`, `routingRoleOf`, `expandForbiddenDomains`, `hasQuotaAccountReadings`, `mergeEvidenceAccounts`, `resolveEvidenceAccounts`.
229:    - **Rationale**: 10 functions, 245 lines, deterministic profile and candidate construction.
230: 5. **Step 5**: `orchestrate/ranking.js`
231:    - **Functions**: `selectCandidateForProfile`, `recordLaunchFailureEvidence`, `resolveDomainAttempts`, `resolveEvidenceDir`.
232:    - **Rationale**: 4 functions, 470 lines, pure scoring and selection logic.
233: 6. **Step 6**: `orchestrate/checkpoint.js`
234:    - **Functions**: 21 receipt integrity, resume verification, and review normalization functions (520 lines).
235:    - **Rationale**: Zero mutable state, pure cryptographic receipt checking and review serialization.
236: 7. **Step 7**: `orchestrate/publication.js`
237:    - **Functions**: 13 functions (508 lines) handling draft PR creation, git import, approval binding, and publication.
238: 8. **Step 8**: `orchestrate/writer-loop.js`
239:    - **Functions**: 17 functions (755 lines) covering worker launch, harness binding, git tree status, verifyWorkerCommit, and usage reports.
240: 9. **Step 9**: `orchestrate/review-loop.js`
241:    - **Functions**: 25 functions (2,818 lines) covering review lanes, host brain gate, prettier/tool gates, and repair rounds.
242: 10. **Step 10**: `orchestrate.js` (Core runner cleanup)
243:    - Contains top-level coordinator `runOrchestration`, `finish`, `buildDefaults`, and exports.

<file path="docs/product-spec/docs/10-ai-collaboration/REPOSITORY-CLI-MANIFEST.md">
  1: # Ship Dễ Repository and CLI Manifest
  2: 
  3: ## Purpose
  4: 
  5: This manifest is the complete inventory for preparing the Ship Dễ build environment. It separates source workspaces, machine-wide CLI tools, project dependencies, Docker services and agent guidance so that tools are installed once in the correct place and every agent sees the same repository state. Integration lifecycle states and the evidence each one requires follow the five-state contract in `REPO-INTEGRATION-EVIDENCE.md`; `tools/ai-brain/data/tool-manifest.json` is the machine-readable inventory that records, per tool, whether this repository can prove the tool is installed (`installed: true` with a real `evidenceRef`) or only declared (`installed: false`).
  6: 
  7: ## Installation rule
  8: 
  9: Only `vinh05092001/shipde-platform` is cloned as product source. Upstream open-source repositories are not copied beside Ship Dễ. They are consumed through a pinned npm dependency, a pinned Docker image, a reviewed GitHub Action or a reviewed agent-guidance snapshot. Cloning every upstream source repository would create duplicate code, unclear upgrade ownership and no benefit to Gemini, Codex or 9Router.
 10: 
 11: ## Product workspaces
 12: 
 13: | Local path                          | Git branch while parked | Owner       | Purpose                               |
 14: | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------- |
 15: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-platform` | `main`                  | Human       | Protected integration baseline        |
 16: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-claude`   | `agent/claude`          | Claude      | Business and solution analysis only   |
 17: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-dsh`      | `agent/dsh`             | 9Router/DSH | Bounded low-risk author               |
 18: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-gemini`   | `agent/gemini`          | Gemini      | Primary implementation author         |
 19: | `C:\Users\gumac\AI\shipde-codex`    | `agent/codex-review`    | Codex       | Planning and fresh independent review |
 20: 
 21: These are five worktrees of one Git repository, not five independent copies. Branches, commits, Pull Requests and CI are the shared memory between apps.
 22: 
 23: ## Machine-wide CLI layer
 24: 
 25: | Repository/product                                                  | Command                    | Install policy                                                      | Authentication or boundary                                                                |
 26: | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 27: | [Git](https://github.com/git-for-windows/git)                       | `git`                      | Existing installation                                               | No shared credential file in the repository                                               |
 28: | [GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli)                            | `gh`                       | Existing installation                                               | Browser OAuth for `vinh05092001`                                                          |
 29: | [Node.js](https://github.com/nodejs/node) and npm                   | `node`, `npm`              | Existing Node 24 installation                                       | Runtime for agent CLIs only until foundation migration                                    |
 30: | [pnpm](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm)                                | `pnpm`                     | Install major 11 now; project pins exact version in `TASK-FOUND-02` | Requires Node 22+; do not use against the current npm prototype before migration          |
 31: | [Docker Desktop](https://github.com/docker/compose) / Compose       | `docker`, `docker compose` | Install now through Windows Package Manager                         | Native Windows/Hyper-V or Docker backend; no Ubuntu worktree is required                  |
 32: | [9Router](https://github.com/decolua/9router)                       | `9router`                  | Install if missing; never auto-upgrade during an active Work Item   | Bind to localhost; prompt injection and request logging off                               |
 33: | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) | `dsh`                      | Pin `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2`                                   | Only the `shipde-dsh` worktree; credential kept outside Git                               |
 34: | [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli)           | `gemini`                   | Install as a supported fallback; record the resolved version        | Sign in interactively with the approved Google account                                    |
 35: | Google Antigravity CLI                                              | `agy`                      | Install from Google's official installer when available             | Preferred authenticated Gemini implementation client in `shipde-gemini`                   |
 36: | OpenAI Codex CLI                                                    | `codex`                    | Install if missing; record the resolved version                     | Sign in with ChatGPT; use the `shipde-codex` worktree for planning/review                 |
 37: | Claude Code                                                         | `claude`                   | Install if missing; record the resolved version                     | Business/solution analysis only in `shipde-claude`; AgentRouter token remains outside Git |
 38: | [Playwright CLI](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-cli)       | `playwright-cli`           | Install `@playwright/cli@0.1.2` globally                            | Token-efficient browser action execution for AI agents; distinct from Playwright Test     |
 39: | [Gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks)                    | `gitleaks`                 | System binary / scanner                                             | Secret and credential audit gate; reject secrets before commit/merge                      |
 40: | [Promptfoo](https://github.com/promptfoo/promptfoo)                 | `promptfoo`                | Install `promptfoo@0.122.2` globally                                | Prompt security assertions and LLM output evaluation suites                               |
 41: | [Trivy](https://github.com/aquasecurity/trivy)                      | `trivy`                    | Windows package / winget                                            | Vulnerability and container image scanner                                                 |
 42: 
 43: AgentRouter is a direct remote provider for Claude Code, not another product worktree and not a 9Router upstream. Its promotional balance is temporary capacity; the workflow must continue to work if that provider is removed.
 44: 
 45: The guarded installers are `scripts/ai/install-clis.ps1` and `scripts/ai/install-ecosystem.ps1`. Both preview by default, install only missing tools with `-Apply`, do not upgrade an installed CLI, do not sign in, and never read or store an API key.
 46: 
 47: ## Project dependency layer
 48: 
 49: These repositories become versioned dependencies inside `shipde-platform`; they are not global CLI installations.
 50: 
 51: | Foundation item | Repository/package family                                                                                                                                                                                  | Required result                                                                               |
 52: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
 53: | `TASK-FOUND-01` | [ESLint](https://github.com/eslint/eslint), Next.js ESLint integration, [Prettier](https://github.com/prettier/prettier), [Gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks)                                 | Reproducible lint/format baseline and secret scanning without weakening rules                 |
 54: | `TASK-FOUND-02` | [pnpm](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm), [Turborepo](https://github.com/vercel/turborepo)                                                                                                                     | pnpm 11 supply-chain defaults, exact `packageManager`, lockfile and root workspace commands   |
 55: | `TASK-FOUND-03` | [NestJS](https://github.com/nestjs/nest), [Prisma](https://github.com/prisma/prisma), [BullMQ](https://github.com/taskforcesh/bullmq), [OpenTelemetry](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js) | API, worker, migration, queue foundations, and distributed tracing with local health checks   |
 56: | `TASK-FOUND-04` | [Vitest](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest), [Supertest](https://github.com/ladjs/supertest), [Playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright)                                                     | Unit, API integration and browser E2E gates                                                   |
 57: | `TASK-FOUND-04` | [Storybook](https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook), `@storybook/addon-a11y`, [axe-core](https://github.com/dequelabs/axe-core)                                                                          | Reviewable component states, interactions, keyboard/accessibility evidence                    |
 58: | `TASK-FOUND-04` | [MSW](https://github.com/mswjs/msw), [msw-storybook-addon](https://github.com/mswjs/msw-storybook-addon)                                                                                                   | Deterministic API/carrier states without fake production behavior                             |
 59: | `TASK-FOUND-04` | [openapi-typescript](https://github.com/openapi-ts/openapi-typescript) and OpenAPI validation                                                                                                              | Generated frontend contract types and drift detection                                         |
 60: | `TASK-FOUND-04` | [Lighthouse CI](https://github.com/GoogleChrome/lighthouse-ci)                                                                                                                                             | Targeted performance budgets for approved critical routes, not every page on every local edit |
 61: 
 62: Nest, Prisma, Turbo, Playwright, Storybook and test CLIs must run through root package scripts (`pnpm ...`). Global copies are prohibited because agents could otherwise use different versions.
 63: 
 64: ## Local service and MCP layer
 65: 
 66: `TASK-FOUND-03` supplies Docker Compose with pinned image versions or digests for:
 67: 
 68: | Service                                       | Purpose                                | Local installation rule                                           |
 69: | --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
 70: | PostgreSQL 16+                                | Primary relational data and migrations | Container only; do not install a second native PostgreSQL service |
 71: | Redis                                         | Queue and cache backing service        | Container only                                                    |
 72: | MinIO or another approved S3-compatible image | Local object storage                   | Container only; production provider is configured separately      |
 73: 
 74: Additionally, on-demand Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers provide diagnostic interfaces:
 75: 
 76: | MCP Server          | Repository                           | Role                                     | Lifecycle                                 |
 77: | ------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
 78: | Chrome DevTools MCP | `ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp` | Deep runtime CDP diagnostics             | Stopped by default; on-demand via profile |
 79: | Playwright MCP      | `microsoft/playwright-mcp`           | Stateful interactive browser exploration | Stopped by default; on-demand via profile |
 80: | Serena MCP          | `oraios/serena` (`v2.1.0`)           | Semantic code indexing & LSP symbols     | Local venv; on-demand code context        |
 81: | jcodemunch MCP      | `jcodemunch-mcp` (`1.108.401`)       | Fast token-efficient AST search & symbols | Local venv; on-demand code context        |
 82: 
 83: Carrier APIs, bank APIs, SMS/Zalo and production object storage are mocked or disabled until a dedicated Work Item contains verified credentials, capability evidence and safe fallback behavior.
 84: 
 85: ## Agent quality guidance and curated datasets
 86: 
 87: The following focused repositories inform implementation but do not replace Ship Dễ product specifications:
 88: 
 89: - [Vercel agent skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills): only `react-best-practices` and `web-design-guidelines` are approved for audited, commit-pinned use in `TASK-FOUND-04`.
 90: - [Vietnamese Provinces Database](https://github.com/thanglequoc/vietnamese-provinces-database): canonical administrative boundary dataset (`v2.1.0`) for address normalization; must be validated before ingestion.
 91: - Next.js version-matched bundled documentation remains the framework authority.
 92: - `DESIGN.md`, the Ship Dễ UX rules and screen specifications remain the product and visual authority.
 93: 
 94: Do not install all skills from a public collection. Do not install remote skills from a moving branch. The Foundation Pull Request must record the reviewed source commit and vendor only the selected guidance required by both author and reviewer.
 95: 
 96: ## Explicit exclusions
 97: 
 98: - No BMAD, SuperClaude, Superpowers or second orchestration framework.
 99: - No Ponytail, Caveman, generic dashboard/theme repository or auto-generated design system.
100: - No duplicate OpenCode/Cline/Cursor author while DSH and Gemini already own implementation routes.
101: - No WSL or Ubuntu requirement for the current Windows-native workflow.
102: - No globally installed framework/build/test CLI that should be pinned in the project.
103: - No provider credential, request log, browser session or model token committed to Git.
104: 
105: ## Readiness evidence
106: 
107: Repository and CLI preparation is complete only when:
108: 
109: 1. all five Ship Dễ worktrees are clean and point to the intended parked branches;
110: 2. `git`, `gh`, `node`, `npm`, `pnpm`, `docker`, `9router`, `dsh`, `codex`, `claude` and at least one authenticated Gemini client (`agy` preferred, `gemini` fallback) resolve from a new PowerShell window;
111: 3. `docker compose version`, `gh auth status`, Gemini/Antigravity sign-in, Codex ChatGPT sign-in and the Claude/AgentRouter launcher succeed;
112: 4. 9Router and DSH complete the approved `SHIPDE_OK` model smoke test without exposing the key;
113: 5. installed versions are recorded by `doctor.ps1`, and no CLI is auto-upgraded during an active Work Item;
114: 6. project-level repositories are introduced only by their assigned Foundation Pull Request with CI evidence;
115: 7. every adopted repository or tool is recorded in `tool-manifest.json` with a boolean `installed` and an `evidenceRef` naming a real repository file, and every gate (`gate: true`) either has a runnable command or is marked `blocked: true` with a reason, per the five-state contract in `REPO-INTEGRATION-EVIDENCE.md`.
</file>

<file path="packages/testkit/src/auth/mfa-test-helpers.ts">
  1: import { createHmac, randomBytes, createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, createHash } from 'node:crypto';
  2: 
  3: const BASE32_ALPHABET = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ234567';
  4: 
  5: export function base32Encode(buffer: Buffer): string {
  6:   let bits = 0;
  7:   let value = 0;
  8:   let output = '';
  9: 
 10:   for (let i = 0; i < buffer.length; i++) {
 11:     value = (value << 8) | buffer[i];
 12:     bits += 8;
 13:     while (bits >= 5) {
 14:       output += BASE32_ALPHABET[(value >>> (bits - 5)) & 31];
 15:       bits -= 5;
 16:     }
 17:   }
 18: 
 19:   if (bits > 0) {
 20:     output += BASE32_ALPHABET[(value << (5 - bits)) & 31];
 21:   }
 22: 
 23:   return output;
 24: }
 25: 
 26: export function base32Decode(input: string): Buffer {
 27:   const cleanInput = input.toUpperCase().replace(/[=\s-]/g, '');
 28:   let bits = 0;
 29:   let value = 0;
 30:   const bytes: number[] = [];
 31: 
 32:   for (let i = 0; i < cleanInput.length; i++) {
 33:     const char = cleanInput[i];
 34:     const index = BASE32_ALPHABET.indexOf(char);
 35:     if (index === -1) {
 36:       throw new Error(`Invalid Base32 character: ${char}`);
 37:     }
 38:     value = (value << 5) | index;
 39:     bits += 5;
 40:     if (bits >= 8) {
 41:       bytes.push((value >>> (bits - 8)) & 255);
 42:       bits -= 8;
 43:     }
 44:   }
 45: 
 46:   return Buffer.from(bytes);
 47: }
 48: 
 49: export function generateTotpSecret(): string {
 50:   return base32Encode(randomBytes(20));
 51: }
 52: 
 53: export function generateTotpCode(secret: string, timestampMs: number = Date.now()): string {
 54:   const key = base32Decode(secret);
 55:   const epochSeconds = Math.floor(timestampMs / 1000);
 56:   const timeStep = Math.floor(epochSeconds / 30);
 57: 
 58:   const counterBuffer = Buffer.alloc(8);
 59:   counterBuffer.writeBigInt64BE(BigInt(timeStep));
 60: 
 61:   const hmac = createHmac('sha1', key).update(counterBuffer).digest();
 62:   const offset = hmac[hmac.length - 1] & 0x0f;
 63: 
 64:   const binaryCode =
 65:     ((hmac[offset] & 0x7f) << 24) |
 66:     ((hmac[offset + 1] & 0xff) << 16) |
 67:     ((hmac[offset + 2] & 0xff) << 8) |
 68:     (hmac[offset + 3] & 0xff);
 69: 
 70:   const otp = binaryCode % 1000000;
 71:   return otp.toString().padStart(6, '0');
 72: }
 73: 
 74: export function encryptMfaSecret(plaintext: string, keyInput: string | Buffer): string {
 75:   let key: Buffer;
 76:   if (Buffer.isBuffer(keyInput) && keyInput.length === 32) {
 77:     key = keyInput;
 78:   } else if (typeof keyInput === 'string' && /^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/.test(keyInput)) {
 79:     key = Buffer.from(keyInput, 'hex');
 80:   } else {
 81:     key = createHash('sha256').update(keyInput).digest();
 82:   }
 83: 
 84:   const iv = randomBytes(12);
 85:   const cipher = createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', key, iv);
 86:   let ciphertext = cipher.update(plaintext, 'utf8', 'hex');
 87:   ciphertext += cipher.final('hex');
 88:   const authTag = cipher.getAuthTag();
 89: 
 90:   return `v1:${iv.toString('hex')}:${authTag.toString('hex')}:${ciphertext}`;
 91: }
 92: 
 93: export function normalizeRecoveryCode(code: string): string {
 94:   return code.trim().toUpperCase().replace(/[\s-]/g, '');
 95: }
 96: 
 97: export function hashRecoveryCode(code: string): string {
 98:   const normalized = normalizeRecoveryCode(code);
 99:   return createHash('sha256').update(normalized).digest('hex');
100: }
</file>

<file path="packages/testkit/src/msw/handlers.ts">
  1: import { http, HttpResponse, delay } from 'msw';
  2: import type { CanonicalUiState, MswScenarioConfig } from './types.js';
  3: 
  4: let currentScenario: MswScenarioConfig = {
  5:   state: 'SUCCESS',
  6:   delayMs: 0,
  7:   recoveryAttemptsBeforeSuccess: 1,
  8: };
  9: 
 10: let currentAttempts = 0;
 11: 
 12: export function setMswScenario(config: Partial<MswScenarioConfig>): void {
 13:   currentScenario = {
 14:     ...currentScenario,
 15:     ...config,
 16:   };
 17:   currentAttempts = 0;
 18: }
 19: 
 20: export function getMswScenario(): MswScenarioConfig {
 21:   return { ...currentScenario };
 22: }
 23: 
 24: export function resetMswScenario(): void {
 25:   currentScenario = {
 26:     state: 'SUCCESS',
 27:     delayMs: 0,
 28:     recoveryAttemptsBeforeSuccess: 1,
 29:   };
 30:   currentAttempts = 0;
 31: }
 32: 
 33: async function handleStateResponse<T extends Record<string, any> | any[]>(
 34:   successData: T,
 35:   emptyData: T,
 36:   partialData?: T
 37: ) {
 38:   if (currentScenario.delayMs && currentScenario.delayMs > 0) {
 39:     await delay(currentScenario.delayMs);
 40:   }
 41: 
 42:   switch (currentScenario.state) {
 43:     case 'LOADING':
 44:       // Indefinite or long delay
 45:       await delay(5000);
 46:       return HttpResponse.json(successData);
 47: 
 48:     case 'EMPTY':
 49:       return HttpResponse.json(emptyData);
 50: 
 51:     case 'ERROR':
 52:       return HttpResponse.json(
 53:         {
 54:           code: 'INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR',
 55:           message: 'Hệ thống gặp sự cố không mong muốn, vui lòng thử lại',
 56:           statusCode: 500,
 57:           timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
 58:         },
 59:         { status: 500 }
 60:       );
 61: 
 62:     case 'FORBIDDEN':
 63:       return HttpResponse.json(
 64:         {
 65:           code: 'FORBIDDEN',
 66:           message: 'Bạn không có quyền thực hiện thao tác này',
 67:           statusCode: 403,
 68:           timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
 69:         },
 70:         { status: 403 }
 71:       );
 72: 
 73:     case 'PARTIAL':
 74:       return HttpResponse.json(partialData !== undefined ? partialData : successData);
 75: 
 76:     case 'RECOVERY':
 77:       currentAttempts++;
 78:       if (currentAttempts <= (currentScenario.recoveryAttemptsBeforeSuccess || 1)) {
 79:         return HttpResponse.json(
 80:           {
 81:             code: 'CARRIER_TIMEOUT',
 82:             message: 'Kết nối tạm thời bị gián đoạn, đang tự động khôi phục',
 83:             statusCode: 503,
 84:             timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
 85:           },
 86:           { status: 503 }
 87:         );
 88:       }
 89:       return HttpResponse.json(successData);
 90: 
 91:     case 'SUCCESS':
 92:     default:
 93:       return HttpResponse.json(successData);
 94:   }
 95: }
 96: 
 97: export const BASE_API_URL = 'https://api.shipde.local';
 98: 
 99: export const handlers = [
100:   // --- Orders List ---
101:   http.get(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/v1/orders`, async () => {

104:         id: 'ord_01',
105:         orderNumber: 'DH-2026-001',
106:         status: 'pending',
107:         recipientName: 'Nguyễn Văn An',
108:         recipientPhone: '0901234567',
109:         codAmountVnd: 350000,
110:         createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),

376:     return handleStateResponse(successSessions, {
377:       data: [successSessions.data[0]],
378:       meta: { total: 1 },
379:     });
380:   }),
381: 
382:   // --- Session: Revoke ---
383:   http.delete(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/v1/sessions/:sessionId`, async ({ params }) => {
384:     const successRevoke = {
385:       session_id: params.sessionId,
386:       status: 'REVOKED',
387:       message: 'Phiên đã được thu hồi',
388:     };
389: 
390:     return handleStateResponse(successRevoke, successRevoke);
391:   }),
392: 
393:   // --- Session: Revoke All ---
394:   http.post(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/v1/sessions/revoke-all`, async () => {
395:     const successRevokeAll = {
396:       revoked_count: 2,
397:       message: 'Đã thu hồi 2 phiên',
398:     };
399: 
400:     return handleStateResponse(successRevokeAll, {
401:       revoked_count: 0,
402:       message: 'Không có phiên nào cần thu hồi',
403:     });
404:   }),
405: 
406:   // --- Session: Heartbeat ---
407:   http.patch(`${BASE_API_URL}/api/v1/sessions/:sessionId/heartbeat`, async ({ params }) => {
408:     const successHeartbeat = {
409:       session_id: params.sessionId,
410:       last_active_at: new Date().toISOString(),
411:     };
412: 
413:     return handleStateResponse(successHeartbeat, successHeartbeat);
414:   }),
415: ];
</file>

<file path="packages/testkit/src/index.ts">
  1: /**
  2:  * @shipde/testkit
  3:  * Shared test fixtures, assertion helpers, and workspace boundary validation.
  4:  */
  5: import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
  6: import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';
  7: 
  8: export interface TestFixtureMeta {
  9:   name: string;
 10:   category: string;
 11:   createdAt: Date;
 12: }
 13: 
 14: export function createMockId(prefix: string): string {
 15:   return `${prefix}_${Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 9)}`;
 16: }
 17: 
 18: /**
 19:  * Resolves a monorepo package entrypoint or manifest using standard Node module resolution.
 20:  * Throws an error if the package cannot be resolved.
 21:  */
 22: export function resolveMonorepoPackage(pkgName: string, fromUrl?: string): string {
 23:   const req = createRequire(fromUrl || import.meta.url);
 24:   try {
 25:     return req.resolve(pkgName);
 26:   } catch (err: unknown) {
 27:     throw new Error(`Failed to resolve package "${pkgName}": ${(err as Error).message}`);
 28:   }
 29: }
 30: 
 31: /**
 32:  * Asserts that a package name resolves to a valid, existing entry point on disk
 33:  * through real Node package export/entry resolution rather than prefix matching.
 34:  */
 35: export function assertValidMonorepoPackage(pkgName: string, fromUrl?: string): boolean {
 36:   try {
 37:     const resolvedPath = resolveMonorepoPackage(pkgName, fromUrl);
 38:     return typeof resolvedPath === 'string' && resolvedPath.length > 0 && existsSync(resolvedPath);
 39:   } catch {
 40:     return false;
 41:   }
 42: }
 43: 
 44: import type { LivenessResponse, ReadinessResponse } from '@shipde/contracts';
 45: import type { AppConfig } from '@shipde/config';
 46: 
 47: /**
 48:  * Asserts that the given response conforms strictly to the LivenessResponse contract.
 49:  * Fails if missing required fields, if status is not 'ok', or if any sensitive fields leak.
 50:  */
 51: export function assertValidLivenessResponse(data: unknown): asserts data is LivenessResponse {
 52:   if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') {
 53:     throw new Error('Liveness response must be a non-null object');
 54:   }
 55:   const obj = data as Record<string, unknown>;
 56:   if (obj.status !== 'ok') {
 57:     throw new Error(`Expected liveness status 'ok', received '${String(obj.status)}'`);
 58:   }
 59:   if (typeof obj.service !== 'string' || obj.service.trim().length === 0) {
 60:     throw new Error('Liveness response missing or invalid service name');
 61:   }
 62:   if (typeof obj.timestamp !== 'string' || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(obj.timestamp))) {
 63:     throw new Error('Liveness response missing or invalid ISO-8601 timestamp');
 64:   }
 65:   if (typeof obj.correlationId !== 'string' || obj.correlationId.trim().length === 0) {
 66:     throw new Error('Liveness response missing or invalid correlationId');
 67:   }
 68: 
 69:   assertNoSensitiveData(data);
 70: }
 71: 
 72: /**
 73:  * Asserts that the given response conforms strictly to the ReadinessResponse contract.
 74:  * Fails if missing required fields or if any sensitive fields leak.
 75:  */
 76: export function assertValidReadinessResponse(
 77:   data: unknown,
 78:   expectedStatus?: 'ok' | 'degraded' | 'error'
 79: ): asserts data is ReadinessResponse {
 80:   if (!data || typeof data !== 'object') {
 81:     throw new Error('Readiness response must be a non-null object');
 82:   }
 83:   const obj = data as Record<string, unknown>;
 84:   if (!['ok', 'degraded', 'error'].includes(String(obj.status))) {
 85:     throw new Error(`Invalid readiness status '${String(obj.status)}'`);
 86:   }
 87:   if (expectedStatus && obj.status !== expectedStatus) {
 88:     throw new Error(`Expected readiness status '${expectedStatus}', got '${String(obj.status)}'`);
 89:   }
 90:   if (typeof obj.service !== 'string' || obj.service.trim().length === 0) {
 91:     throw new Error('Readiness response missing or invalid service name');
 92:   }
 93:   if (typeof obj.timestamp !== 'string' || Number.isNaN(Date.parse(obj.timestamp))) {
 94:     throw new Error('Readiness response missing or invalid ISO-8601 timestamp');
 95:   }
 96:   if (typeof obj.correlationId !== 'string' || obj.correlationId.trim().length === 0) {
 97:     throw new Error('Readiness response missing or invalid correlationId');
 98:   }
 99:   if (!obj.checks || typeof obj.checks !== 'object') {
100:     throw new Error('Readiness response missing checks map');
101:   }
102: 
103:   assertNoSensitiveData(data);
104: }
105: 
106: /**
107:  * Sensitive key patterns and substring patterns that must never appear in responses or sanitized logs.
108:  */
109: const SENSITIVE_PATTERNS = [
110:   /password/i,
111:   /secret/i,
112:   /token/i,
113:   /authorization/i,
114:   /apikey/i,
115:   /connection.*string/i,
116:   /postgres:\/\//i,
117:   /redis:\/\//i,
118:   /minioadmin/i,
119: ];
120: 
121: /**
122:  * Recursively asserts that an object contains no sensitive information in keys or values.
123:  */
124: export function assertNoSensitiveData(data: unknown, path = ''): void {
125:   if (data === null || data === undefined) {
126:     return;
127:   }
128:   if (typeof data === 'string') {
129:     for (const pattern of SENSITIVE_PATTERNS) {
130:       if (pattern.test(data)) {
131:         throw new Error(`Sensitive data leaked at "${path}": matches pattern ${pattern}`);
132:       }
133:     }
134:     return;
135:   }
136:   if (typeof data === 'object') {
137:     for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(data as Record<string, unknown>)) {
138:       const currentPath = path ? `${path}.${key}` : key;
139:       for (const pattern of SENSITIVE_PATTERNS) {
140:         if (pattern.test(key)) {
141:           throw new Error(`Sensitive key leaked at "${currentPath}": matches pattern ${pattern}`);
142:         }
143:       }
144:       assertNoSensitiveData(value, currentPath);
145:     }
146:   }
147: }
148: 
149: /**
150:  * Asserts that none of the provided secret values appear as substrings within text.
151:  */
152: export function assertNoSecretValues(text: string, secretValues: string[]): void {
153:   for (const secret of secretValues) {
154:     if (secret && text.includes(secret)) {
155:       throw new Error(`Secret value was leaked in text: ${secret}`);
156:     }
157:   }
158: }
159: 
160: /**
161:  * Generates a valid test configuration object with safe local defaults.
162:  */
163: export function createValidTestConfig(overrides: Partial<AppConfig> = {}): AppConfig {
164:   return {
165:     NODE_ENV: 'test',
166:     PORT: 3001,
167:     WORKER_HEALTH_PORT: 3002,
168:     DATABASE_URL: 'postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5433/shipde_dev?schema=public',
169:     REDIS_HOST: 'localhost',
170:     REDIS_PORT: 6379,
171:     REDIS_PASSWORD: undefined,
172:     S3_ENDPOINT: 'http://localhost:9000',
173:     S3_REGION: 'us-east-1',
174:     S3_ACCESS_KEY: 'minioadmin',
175:     S3_SECRET_KEY: 'minioadmin',
176:     S3_BUCKET: process.env.S3_BUCKET || 'shipde-local',
177:     S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE: true,
178:     CARRIER_MODE: 'mock',
179:     LOG_LEVEL: 'info',
180:     AUTH_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS: 43200,
181:     AUTH_LOGIN_OTP_ENABLED: false,
182:     PASSWORD_RESET_TTL_SECONDS: 3600,
183:     FRONTEND_URL: 'http://localhost:3000',
184:     AUDIT_IDENTIFIER_HMAC_KEY: 'test-audit-hmac-key-placeholder-32-chars',
185:     TRUST_PROXY_HOPS: 0,
186:     RBAC_SEED_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS: 1000,
187:     RBAC_SEED_MAX_ATTEMPTS: 10,
188:     RBAC_SEED_BACKOFF_FACTOR: 1.5,
189:     ...overrides,
190:   };
191: }
192: 
193: // --- Carrier Mocks ---
194: export * from './carriers/index.js';
195: 
196: // --- Auth & Verification Mocks ---
197: export * from './auth/index.js';
198: 
199: // --- MSW Canonical State Handlers ---
200: export * from './msw/index.js';
201: 
202: // --- HTTP Integration Test Harness (Supertest) ---
203: import request from 'supertest';
204: export { request };
</file>

<file path="prisma/migrations/20260923000000_feat_auth_05_mfa/migration.sql">
  1: -- FEAT-AUTH-05: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Migration
  2: --
  3: -- Forward Notes:
  4: -- - Adds mfa_factors, mfa_recovery_codes, and mfa_challenges tables.
  5: -- - Extends device_sessions with mfa_verified_at and auth_assurance.
  6: -- - Key Availability: All factor secrets are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM
  7: --   using MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY configured in environment. In production, if
  8: --   MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is absent or shorter than 32 characters, API bootstrap
  9: --   fails closed and cannot decrypt or encrypt factor secrets.
 10: -- - Recovery codes are stored only as one-way cryptographic SHA-256 verifiers.
 11: -- - Challenges are stored only as SHA-256 hashes of opaque single-use tokens.
 12: 
 13: -- AlterTable: add MFA assurance columns to device_sessions
 14: ALTER TABLE "device_sessions" ADD COLUMN "mfa_verified_at" TIMESTAMPTZ;
 15: ALTER TABLE "device_sessions" ADD COLUMN "auth_assurance" VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PASSWORD';
 16: 
 17: -- CreateTable: mfa_factors
 18: CREATE TABLE "mfa_factors" (
 19:     "id" UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 20:     "user_id" UUID NOT NULL,
 21:     "merchant_id" UUID NOT NULL,
 22:     "type" VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TOTP',
 23:     "status" VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'PENDING',
 24:     "secret_ciphertext" TEXT NOT NULL,
 25:     "key_version" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
 26:     "setup_expires_at" TIMESTAMPTZ,
 27:     "activated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ,
 28:     "reset_at" TIMESTAMPTZ,
 29:     "last_accepted_step" BIGINT,
 30:     "created_by" VARCHAR(255),
 31:     "updated_by" VARCHAR(255),
 32:     "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 33:     "updated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 34: 
 35:     CONSTRAINT "mfa_factors_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
 36: );
 37: 
 38: -- CreateTable: mfa_recovery_codes
 39: CREATE TABLE "mfa_recovery_codes" (
 40:     "id" UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

 42:     "code_hash" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
 43:     "consumed_at" TIMESTAMPTZ,
 44:     "consumed_by_session_id" VARCHAR(255),
 45:     "consumed_correlation_id" VARCHAR(255),
 46:     "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 47: 
 48:     CONSTRAINT "mfa_recovery_codes_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
 49: );
 50: 
 51: -- CreateTable: mfa_challenges
 52: CREATE TABLE "mfa_challenges" (

 60:     "failed_attempts" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

 62:     "invalidated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ,
 63:     "correlation_id" VARCHAR(255),
 64:     "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 65: 
 66:     CONSTRAINT "mfa_challenges_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
 67: );
 68: 
 69: -- CreateIndex
 70: CREATE INDEX "mfa_factors_user_id_status_idx" ON "mfa_factors"("user_id", "status");
 71: CREATE INDEX "mfa_factors_merchant_id_user_id_idx" ON "mfa_factors"("merchant_id", "user_id");
 72: 
 73: CREATE INDEX "mfa_recovery_codes_factor_id_consumed_at_idx" ON "mfa_recovery_codes"("factor_id", "consumed_at");
 74: CREATE INDEX "mfa_recovery_codes_code_hash_idx" ON "mfa_recovery_codes"("code_hash");
 75: 
 76: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "mfa_challenges_challenge_hash_key" ON "mfa_challenges"("challenge_hash");
 77: CREATE INDEX "mfa_challenges_user_id_consumed_at_expires_at_idx" ON "mfa_challenges"("user_id", "consumed_at", "expires_at");
 78: 
 79: -- AddForeignKey
 80: ALTER TABLE "mfa_factors" ADD CONSTRAINT "mfa_factors_user_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("user_id") REFERENCES "users"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
 81: ALTER TABLE "mfa_factors" ADD CONSTRAINT "mfa_factors_merchant_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("merchant_id") REFERENCES "merchants"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
 82: 
 83: ALTER TABLE "mfa_recovery_codes" ADD CONSTRAINT "mfa_recovery_codes_factor_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("factor_id") REFERENCES "mfa_factors"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
 84: 
 85: ALTER TABLE "mfa_challenges" ADD CONSTRAINT "mfa_challenges_user_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("user_id") REFERENCES "users"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;

 87: 
 88: -- BR-AUTH-19 / P1-03: authoritative database guarantee of at most one ACTIVE factor per user.
 89: -- Prisma cannot express partial unique indexes, so this lives only in the migration.
 90: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "mfa_factors_user_id_active_key" ON "mfa_factors"("user_id") WHERE "status" = 'ACTIVE';
 91: 
 92: -- BR-AUTH-19 / P1-02: durable tenant-scoped idempotency for admin MFA reset.
 93: CREATE TABLE "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency" (
 94:     "id" UUID NOT NULL,

 96:     "idempotency_key" VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
 97:     "actor_user_id" UUID NOT NULL,

 99:     "reason" TEXT NOT NULL,
100:     "response" JSONB NOT NULL,
101:     "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
102: 
103:     CONSTRAINT "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
104: );
105: 
106: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency_merchant_id_idempotency_key_key" ON "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency"("merchant_id", "idempotency_key");
107: 
108: ALTER TABLE "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency" ADD CONSTRAINT "mfa_admin_reset_idempotency_merchant_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("merchant_id") REFERENCES "merchants"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
</file>

  1: -- FEAT-RBAC-01: Roles and Permissions Migration
  2: --
  3: -- Forward Notes:
  4: -- - Creates roles, permissions, and role_permissions tables
  5: -- - Extends users table with custom_role_id for tenant-scoped custom role assignment
  6: -- - Implements multi-tenant isolation, unique role names per merchant, and cascade deletion
  7: 
  8: -- AlterTable
  9: ALTER TABLE "users" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "custom_role_id" UUID;
 10: 
 11: -- CreateTable
 12: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "roles" (
 13:     "id" UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 14:     "merchant_id" UUID,
 15:     "code" VARCHAR(64),
 16:     "name" VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
 17:     "name_lower" VARCHAR(255),
 18:     "description" TEXT,
 19:     "is_system" BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
 20:     "created_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 21:     "updated_at" TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
 22: 
 23:     CONSTRAINT "roles_pkey" PRIMARY KEY ("id")
 24: );
 25: 
 26: -- AlterTable (idempotency if roles table already existed without name_lower)
 27: ALTER TABLE "roles" ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "name_lower" VARCHAR(255);
 28: UPDATE "roles" SET "name_lower" = LOWER("name") WHERE "name_lower" IS NULL;
 29: 
 30: -- Trigger to maintain name_lower automatically
 31: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_role_name_lower() RETURNS trigger AS $$
 32: BEGIN
 33:     NEW.name_lower := LOWER(NEW.name);
 34:     RETURN NEW;
 35: END;
 36: $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
 37: 
 38: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_role_name_lower ON "roles";
 39: CREATE TRIGGER trg_role_name_lower
 40: BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF "name" ON "roles"
 41: FOR EACH ROW
 42: EXECUTE FUNCTION set_role_name_lower();
 43: 
 44: -- CreateTable
 45: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "permissions" (
 46:     "id" UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

101: BEGIN
102:     IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'role_permissions_role_id_fkey') THEN
103:         ALTER TABLE "role_permissions" ADD CONSTRAINT "role_permissions_role_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("role_id") REFERENCES "roles"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
104:     END IF;
105: END $$;
106: 
107: -- AddForeignKey
108: DO $$
109: BEGIN
110:     IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'role_permissions_permission_id_fkey') THEN
111:         ALTER TABLE "role_permissions" ADD CONSTRAINT "role_permissions_permission_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("permission_id") REFERENCES "permissions"("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE;
112:     END IF;
113: END $$;
114: 
115: -- AddForeignKey (DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED so tenant cascade and role delete both have one defined outcome)
116: DO $$
117: BEGIN
118:     IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname = 'users_custom_role_id_fkey') THEN
119:         ALTER TABLE "users" DROP CONSTRAINT "users_custom_role_id_fkey";
120:     END IF;
121:     ALTER TABLE "users" ADD CONSTRAINT "users_custom_role_id_fkey" FOREIGN KEY ("custom_role_id") REFERENCES "roles"("id") ON DELETE NO ACTION ON UPDATE CASCADE DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED;
122: END $$;
123: 
124: -- Same-merchant constraint trigger (BR-RBAC-04 / database ownership)
125: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION check_user_custom_role_same_merchant()
126: RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
127: DECLARE
128:     v_role_merchant_id UUID;
129:     v_is_system BOOLEAN;
130: BEGIN
131:     IF NEW.custom_role_id IS NOT NULL THEN
132:         SELECT merchant_id, is_system INTO v_role_merchant_id, v_is_system
133:         FROM roles
134:         WHERE id = NEW.custom_role_id;
135: 
136:         IF NOT FOUND THEN
137:             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Custom role % does not exist', NEW.custom_role_id;
138:         END IF;
139: 
140:         IF v_is_system THEN
141:             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cannot assign system role % as custom_role_id', NEW.custom_role_id;
142:         END IF;
143: 
144:         IF v_role_merchant_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.merchant_id THEN
145:             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Cross-tenant custom role assignment: user merchant % does not match role merchant %',
146:                 NEW.merchant_id, v_role_merchant_id;
147:         END IF;
148:     END IF;
149:     RETURN NEW;
150: END;
151: $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
152: 
153: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_check_user_custom_role_same_merchant ON users;
154: CREATE TRIGGER trg_check_user_custom_role_same_merchant
155:     BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF custom_role_id, merchant_id ON users
156:     FOR EACH ROW
157:     EXECUTE FUNCTION check_user_custom_role_same_merchant();
158: 
159: -- Allow platform-level system audit logs without customer merchant binding (Finding 1 / Round 12 / Finding 1 / Round 14 / P1-03 / BR-RBAC-07 / BR-RBAC-04)
160: -- Downstream consumer compatibility & null-safety:
161: -- 1. Existing customer audit log rows retain their non-null merchant_id; only platform-level bootstrap events omit merchant_id.
162: -- 2. Downstream tenant queries (WHERE merchant_id = :tenant_id) continue to return tenant-scoped events without regression.
163: -- 3. Downstream platform audit consumers must handle nullable merchant_id (WHERE merchant_id IS NULL or merchant_id IS NOT NULL).
164: DO $$
165: BEGIN
166:     IF EXISTS (
167:         SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
168:         WHERE table_name = 'audit_logs' AND column_name = 'merchant_id' AND is_nullable = 'NO'
169:     ) THEN
170:         ALTER TABLE "audit_logs" ALTER COLUMN "merchant_id" DROP NOT NULL;
171:     END IF;
172: END $$;
</file>

 114: export interface CanonicalFieldError {

 120: export class CanonicalApiException extends HttpException {
 121:   constructor(
 122:     statusCode: number,
 123:     public readonly code: string,
 124:     message: string,
 125:     public readonly retryable = false,
 126:     public readonly next_action?: string,
 127:     public readonly fields?: CanonicalFieldError[],
 128:     public readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
 129:     public readonly extra?: Record<string, unknown>
 130:   ) {
 131:     super(
 132:       {
 133:         error: {
 134:           code,
 135:           message,
 136:           retryable,
 137:           next_action,
 138:           fields,
 139:           ...(retryAfterSeconds !== undefined && { cooldown_seconds: retryAfterSeconds }),
 140:           ...(extra || {}),
 141:         },
 142:       },
 143:       statusCode
 144:     );
 145:   }
 146: }

 148: @Injectable()
 149: export class AuthService {
 150:   constructor(
 151:     @Inject(PrismaService) private readonly prisma: PrismaService,
 152:     @Inject(RateLimitService) private readonly rateLimitService: RateLimitService,
 153:     @Optional()
 154:     @Inject(VERIFICATION_ADAPTER)
 155:     private readonly deliveryAdapter?: IVerificationDeliveryAdapter,
 156:     @Optional()
 157:     @Inject(APP_CONFIG)
 158:     private readonly config?: AppConfig
 159:   ) {}
